Tech Report: Clock Ticking on Zcash’s Sprout Pool: 22,263 ZEC Unmoved Ahead of NU7 Lock

📅 30 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1209 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nulltx

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that daily pool data highlights Sprout holders moved more than 300 ZEC out in a September rush, then almost stopped.
  • Unless someone acts in the next few days, nearly all of what remains will be unspendable at block 3,543,405.
  • Sources indicate that most coverage of Zcash's upcoming Sprout freeze quotes the same figure, about 22,000 ZEC.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

Recent findings suggest that daily pool data highlights Sprout holders moved more than 300 ZEC out in a September rush, then almost stopped. The last withdrawal was on October 19.

Unless someone acts in the next few days, nearly all of what remains will be unspendable at block 3,543,405.

Sources indicate that most coverage of Zcash's upcoming Sprout freeze quotes the same figure, about 22,000 ZEC. That number is accurate, but it is a single snapshot. It doesn't show whether the people who own those coins are doing anything about the deadline.

We checked the pool every day, and the answer so far is no.

According to ZecStats' daily value-pool records, Sprout has held exactly 22,263.34162335 ZEC since October 19. That is 11 straight days, and more than 12,000 blocks, without a single zatoshi leaving the pool. Our October 25 piece recorded the drop from 22,309 ZEC to 22,263 ZEC. Since then the balance hasn't moved.

Industry observers note that zecStats publishes a daily CSV of every Zcash value pool, using the last block of each UTC day. Its figures follow the valuePools field that a full node returns through the getblockchaininfo call. The archive starts on July 30, 2026, and gives a 92-day picture of the Sprout pool.

In a recent development, across those 92 days, about 374 ZEC, or 1.65% of the pool, left Sprout. That is an average of roughly 4 ZEC a day. The average hides the real pattern, though: the pool moved on only 15 of the 92 days.

Most of the withdrawals came in a few large transfers in September:.

Together with smaller moves on August 31, September 17 and September 19, the 30 days to September 29 saw 310.5 ZEC leave Sprout. That is about 10 ZEC a day.

October was much quieter. Apart from one withdrawal of 46.05 ZEC on October 19, the month's activity was small change:.

Since October 19, there has been no movement at all.

At September's pace, about 70 ZEC more would leave before activation. At October's pace, it would be well under 15 ZEC. On the last 11 days' pace, the answer is zero.

Recent findings suggest that the deadline is set in ZIP 259, which defines how the NU7 network upgrade is deployed. It sets the mainnet activation height at 3,543,405.

According to recent reports, NU7 does not introduce a latest transaction format. Instead, after activation, version 4 transactions become invalid, while versions 5 and 6 remain valid. Sprout's design is the problem. As ZIP 259 puts it: "Because Sprout transfers can only be represented by version 4 transactions, funds remaining in the Sprout pool become unspendable.".

Industry observers note that the coins would not be destroyed, and NU7 does not change Zcash's supply cap. They would simply be stuck in a pool that no valid transaction can spend from. Today the stranded amount would be 22,263 ZEC, about 0.13% of the roughly 17.01 million ZEC in circulation.

The rest of the upgrade is larger:.

ZIP 259 also skips Zcash's usual three-month gap between the first supporting software release and activation. Operators running unsupported software could stay online and follow a pre-NU7 chain.

As of ZecStats' latest upgrade on October 30 at 13:09 UTC, the chain was at block 3,535,877. That leaves 7,528 blocks until activation.

Sources indicate that in October, the network averaged about 1,147 blocks a day, or one roughly every 75.3 seconds. At that rate, block 3,543,405 arrives around 02:00–03:00 UTC on November 6. That is the evening of November 5 in the Americas and the early hours of November 6 in Europe and Africa.

Small changes in block times could move that window by a few hours. Holders who blueprint to move funds on the final day risk missing the cutoff.

Sources indicate that in practice, getting funds out of Sprout means sending a version 4 transaction that moves them into a newer pool before activation. People need software that can still build Sprout transactions and a synced node or wallet that recognizes their old notes.

According to recent reports, the September withdrawals show that some holders are still paying attention. Several were round amounts, such as 99.998 ZEC, which is consistent with someone moving 100 ZEC and paying a fee. The 11-day pause since October 19 suggests something else: most of the remaining 22,263 ZEC may belong to keys that are lost, forgotten or no longer used.

That has been part of the debate about Sprout for years. A pool that has been shrinking slowly since Zcash's early days is now on a fixed timetable. The daily data indicates that most of its remaining balance is not being moved.

Recent findings suggest that every report that cites "about 22,000 ZEC at risk" is technically correct. The more useful figure for anyone tracking the upgrade is the rate of change, and right now that rate is zero.

The useful thing to watch over the next week is whether the Sprout line in ZecStats' daily data moves again before block 3,543,405. If it doesn't, Zcash will activate NU7 with about 22,263 ZEC permanently locked in its first shielded pool. That would be one of the largest deliberate freezes of user funds by any major blockchain upgrade, and nearly all of it would be coins whose owners did not move them in time.

It has been revealed that the Concurrence Data and AI Platform is built and operated on Amazon Web Services (AWS), with data-resident deployments worldwide. A forward-deployed team of Applied AI engineers and deployment strategists builds each organization's workflows on the Concurrence platform, and every agent is validated against millions of simulated patient encounters before it goes live.

It has been revealed that organizations can now procure and deploy the Concurrence Data and AI Platform directly through AWS Marketplace, simplifying procurement with consolidated billing and enabling faster time-to-value for healthcare data and AI initiatives across their AWS environments. Concurrence is Deployed on AWS, meaning eligible purchases through AWS Marketplace can count toward an organization's existing AWS commitment, subject to its agreement's AWS Marketplace allowance. Healthcare institutions can engage Concurrence through their AWS account team, in AWS Marketplace, or through the Concurrence website.

In a recent development, "AI adoption in enterprise healthcare is rarely held back by a lack of good use cases. The hard part is deployment. Latest Update: Compass follows through on Reffkin’s threat, sues 15 MLSs

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1221 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Inman

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The brokerage giant confirmed Thursday that it is filing 15 federal antitrust lawsuits against MLSs across eight states.
  • Industry observers note that several weeks ago at an industry conference, Compass International Holdings CEO Robert Reffkin threatened to sue MLSs that wouldn’t change their rules.
  • The tech giant revealed Thursday that it is filing 15 federal antitrust lawsuits against MLSs across eight states, accusing the organizations of illegally restricting how agents can publicly market homes outside their systems.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The brokerage giant confirmed Thursday that it is filing 15 federal antitrust lawsuits against MLSs across eight states.

Industry observers note that several weeks ago at an industry conference, Compass International Holdings CEO Robert Reffkin threatened to sue MLSs that wouldn’t change their rules. Now, the brokerage giant is taking another 15 of them to federal court.

The tech giant revealed Thursday that it is filing 15 federal antitrust lawsuits against MLSs across eight states, accusing the organizations of illegally restricting how agents can publicly market homes outside their systems. Compass alleges that the MLSs unlawfully fine agents for publicly marketing listings outside the MLS, with penalties it says can reach $15,000.

In a recent development, the announcement marks a major escalation in a fight that has been building since September, fueled by demand letters, legal threats and increasingly pointed public messaging from Compass execs. Eight of the 15 MLSs targeted Thursday are already suing Compass in two separate federal cases, adding another layer to an increasingly complicated legal battle.

A Compass spokesperson described the latest lawsuits to Inman as a follow-through on Reffkin’s warnings at the Council of Multiple Listing Services’ annual conference in Fort Lauderdale in late September, noting that some MLS organizations had filed their own lawsuits before Compass took legal action.

The lawsuits target six MLSs in California, three in North Carolina and six others across the country.

At the center of the lawsuits are MLS rules that require agents to submit listings to the MLS once they begin publicly marketing a property.

According to recent reports, sellers can generally keep their homes off the MLS through an office-exclusive arrangement. But advertising a property on a brokerage website, social media or other public channels typically triggers a requirement to share the listing with the MLS.

Compass argues that those rules unfairly limit competition and prevent agents from offering alternative marketing strategies, even when homeowners want to advertise their properties outside the MLS first.

“Only the law and the homeowner should tell agents how to market a home, and the MLS is neither the law nor the homeowner,” a Compass spokesperson said in a statement shared with Inman. “Agents should be free to compete on the marketing strategies they offer.”.

The brokerage also rejected warnings from MLS leaders that allowing public marketing without requiring listings to be shared through the MLS would harm buyers, sellers or competing agents.

It has been revealed that compass pointed to seven of the nation’s 25 largest MLSs that it mentioned already allow agents to publicly market office-exclusive listings without fines. Those MLSs cover approximately 340,000 agents across 12 states, according to the company.

“If what we are asking for is so bad, why has it worked for years in nearly 30 percent of the country?” the spokesperson stated.

MLS leaders counter that their rules are intended to ensure that publicly marketed homes are available to other brokers and their buyers. They argue that agents who benefit from access to shared MLS listings should also contribute their own publicly marketed properties.

California Regional MLS CEO Art Carter, who spent months negotiating with Reffkin before the dispute reached federal court, emphasized that point in a recent interview with Inman.

“At some point, you’ve got to say, this is a cooperative,” Carter remarked.

Carter also warned that withholding listings from MLS databases could leave appraisers and lenders with incomplete information about home sales, making it harder to determine accurate property values.

According to recent reports, the latest complaints largely echo arguments Compass made in its Oct. 16 antitrust lawsuit against CRMLS, accusing MLS organizations of restricting competition through their listing rules. In the complaints filed Thursday against MLSs, Compass seeks triple damages and court orders blocking enforcement of the challenged rules.

On Sept. 8, Compass attorneys sent California Regional MLS a demand letter calling on the organization to stop fining agents for publicly marketing office-exclusive listings. The brokerage gave CRMLS until Oct. 6 to comply, warning that it was prepared to spend millions of dollars on litigation if its demands weren’t met.

Similar letters went to other MLS organizations across the country.

On Sept. 23, Compass International Holdings sent a separate letter demanding that MLS organizations stop sharing its agents’ production and listing data with third-party companies that help competing brokerages recruit agents. The letter specifically identified vendors Courted, BrokerMetrics and Brokerkit as examples of companies using MLS data for recruiting.

Sources indicate that compass argued that information provided to MLS organizations for real estate transactions shouldn’t be used to help competitors recruit its agents. It sought greater control over how that data was distributed, including the ability to exclude information associated with its brokerage brands from feeds used by recruiting companies.

Industry experts who recently spoke to Inman questioned parts of Compass’ argument, noting that MLS data serves purposes beyond recruiting and that access is often governed by agreements with brokerages and technology vendors.

Compass later raised the concern in its October antitrust lawsuit against CRMLS, alleging it lost millions of dollars in commissions after agents were recruited away using data the MLS allegedly sold to competing brokerages.

On Sept. 30, Reffkin took his fight over private listings directly to MLS executives at the Council of Multiple Listing Services’ annual conference in Fort Lauderdale. During a contentious session that drew pushback from attendees, Reffkin warned that Compass would begin filing antitrust lawsuits in mid-October against MLSs that continued fining agents for publicly marketing office-exclusive listings.

Photo by Michael Roberts of AJ Canaria Creative Services.

He said Compass wanted to display listings on its own website without agents facing penalties, while some MLS executives questioned whether the manufacturer’s demands went further and could undermine cooperation.

Sources indicate that the dispute reached federal court Oct. 5, when CRMLS sued Compass. Compass filed its own antitrust complaint against CRMLS on Oct. 16.

According to recent reports, amid the escalations, tensions and litigation in recent weeks, MLS organizations have also begun raising money to defend their rules in court. CRMLS revealed aims for an MLS Cooperation Legal Defense Fund on Sept. 30, while CMLS subsequently announced a separate legal action fund to be run by an independent nonprofit.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Anthropic PBC isn’t satisfied with having Claude just write new software.
  • The firm announced the launch of Claude Ship, which is a fresh suite of artificial intelligence agents capable of automating code reviews, bug fixes and approvals.
  • Industry observers note that claude Ship is an effort by Anthropic to eliminate the newly introduced bottleneck that has emerged in the code review and approval process at companies that have already adopted AI code generation tools.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 20:30 EST / NOVEMBER 23 2026.

Anthropic PBC isn’t satisfied with having Claude just write new software. With a new upgrade today, Claude now can tell developers when the code it has generated is ready to ship into production environments.

The firm announced the launch of Claude Ship, which is a fresh suite of artificial intelligence agents capable of automating code reviews, bug fixes and approvals. The last one is the most interesting of those capabilities, because code reviews and fixes are nothing new for AI. But Claude’s ability to automatically approve code changes based on the policies predetermined by an organization’s developer team is a novel development that has not been seen before.

Industry observers note that claude Ship is an effort by Anthropic to eliminate the newly introduced bottleneck that has emerged in the code review and approval process at companies that have already adopted AI code generation tools. At those organizations, fresh code is being whipped up in double-quick time, and there are also AI agents for checking that code and providing fixes if it’s not working as hoped. But until now, the final review and approval process has always been performed by humans. Claude Ship changes that.

The idea is that human developers can delegate final approval authority to Claude, so now all they really have to do is determine the quality and security standards of the code they’re asking AI to create.

In a recent development, “Most teams want a person to approve every change and that’s easy to keep up with when people write every line,” Anthropic remarked in a blog post. “But a lot of developers build with agents now. On the Claude Code team, Claude writes most of our code and we wanted everything after the pull request to move that fast too.”.

Industry observers note that anthropic said Claude Ship consists of three parts. The first is Code Review, which is a tool that has been generally available for some time already. The other two are PR Steward and Claude Approvals, and they’re both still in beta.

PR Steward is designed to handle issues such as failing continuous integration checks, merge conflicts and feedback from Code Review. After each push, it will leave comments on what changes were made and how to roll them back if necessary.

It has been revealed that once PR Steward is done, Claude Approvals takes over. It works by applying an approval policy that’s left as a file in the codebase’s repository. The approval process can incorporate various elements, including the findings in Code Review and the organization’s own classifiers, with policies written in natural language.

According to recent reports, anthropic is urging early adopters to be cautious. Because Claude Ship is still in beta, it recommends running Claude Approvals in observe-only mode first. It also advises teams to begin with just one repository first, and set monthly spending limits so they can maintain more control over everything.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Although XRP is at risk of losing its top-four position in the global cryptocurrency market, the asset still ranks among the three largest crypto assets in Japan.

In a recent post shared by the renowned Ripple-backed XRP treasury firm Evernorth, the company highlighted XRP’s growing performance in the Japan crypto market.

Earlier today, Evernorth shared monthly data from the Japan Virtual and Crypto Assets Exchange Association (JVCEA) revealing that XRP recorded about ¥132.8 billion in spot trading volume in September 2026.

While this accounted for about 15% of Japan's total crypto spot trading volume during the month, XRP emerged as the third most-traded cryptocurrency in Japan after Bitcoin and Ethereum.

This indicates that XRP has outperformed other major altcoins that are right now trading in the Japan crypto market, hitting about $880 million in trading volume.

While further data revealed Solana and Dogecoin ranking next to XRP on the list as the fourth- and fifth-largest cryptocurrencies in Japan, respectively, the data also showed a wide gap from XRP’s ¥132.8 billion spot volume.

This means that XRP is significantly ahead of Solana and Dogecoin in the Japan crypto trading market, as Solana recorded only about ¥19.47 billion in trading volume during the same month.

Dogecoin, on the other hand, saw less participation, as it recorded only ¥11.27 billion in spot volume during the same period.

With XRP sitting in the third spot, the asset has become one of the most actively traded cryptocurrencies in Japan despite its persistent price volatility.

#179291. Your ‘just sold’ posts are missing the best part of the story

📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1145 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Inman ↗ Open Full Page

Your ‘just sold’ posts are missing the best part of the story

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1145 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Inman

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, turn closings into case studies.
  • I’ve always found it interesting how much time and energy we put into selling a home, only to reduce the entire experience to a “just sold” graphic once the transaction closes.
  • We spend weeks, sometimes months, developing a marketing strategy, communicating with sellers, negotiating with buyers and navigating challenges along the way, but so little of that work makes it into the content we share afterward.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, turn closings into case studies. Use ChatGPT Voice and footage you already have, plus this free Canva template, to tell the story behind the sale.

I’ve always found it interesting how much time and energy we put into selling a home, only to reduce the entire experience to a “just sold” graphic once the transaction closes.

We spend weeks, sometimes months, developing a marketing strategy, communicating with sellers, negotiating with buyers and navigating challenges along the way, but so little of that work makes it into the content we share afterward.

I don’t think there’s anything wrong with celebrating a closing. But I’ve always felt that the story behind the sale is often more interesting than the sale itself, especially when you consider what a prospective client is trying to figure out when deciding who to hire.

Recent findings suggest that most sellers probably assume any experienced agent can put their home on the market. What they don’t necessarily know is how that agent approaches marketing, how much effort they’ll put into a listing or how they’ll respond when something doesn’t go according to initiative. Those are difficult things to communicate in a listing presentation when every agent is promising some version of the same thing.

For years, I’ve tried to give people a better understanding of our work by creating case studies of the homes we’ve sold. Initially, that meant compiling listing footage into a Reel with a longer caption explaining the transaction. More recently, I’ve been experimenting with carousels that tell those stories across multiple slides using footage we already created to market the property.

What I like about this approach is that people can see what working with us might actually look like, rather than simply taking our word for it.

We recently sold a property in San Pedro where we hosted nine open houses, mailed 500 postcards, ran digital advertising and created a video that generated more than 1.5 million organic views. We found a buyer and opened escrow, but shortly before closing, that buyer backed out, and we had to start again.

A post shared by KRYS BENYAMEIN | LA & OC Real Estate Agent (@krysbenyamein).

We eventually found another buyer and successfully closed, but when we shared the case study, we didn’t lead with the sale price or how much marketing we’d done. We opened with, “Imagine finally selling your house. Then the buyer backs out right before closing.”.

I liked that opening because it put the reader in the seller’s position. Most homeowners can imagine how frustrating that experience would be, and it naturally creates curiosity about what happened next. From there, we explained how we responded, got the property back in front of buyers, and ultimately closed.

We’ve used the same approach to tell different stories, including a transaction in Hesperia, California, where we coordinated a sale for sellers who had moved out of state, and a humorous carousel about a San Diego transaction that generated 15,741 views.

A post shared by KRYS BENYAMEIN | LA & OC Real Estate Agent (@krysbenyamein).

According to recent reports, not every transaction needs an extraordinary twist. Sometimes the interesting part is a problem you solved, a decision you made, or the work that went into making the experience easier for your client. The challenge is recognizing those moments and figuring out how to communicate them.

The storytelling portion generally takes me about 15 minutes, although gathering information and designing the finished post take additional time.

Before writing, I go through the transaction and take inventory of everything we’ve done. I want to know how many open houses we hosted, how many people attended, how many postcards we mailed, how much content we published and how many views our videos generated. I’ll also look at offers received and anything else that helps explain how the sale unfolded.

This has made me more conscious of documenting our work as we’re doing it. It’s difficult to communicate the effort behind a sale if you can’t remember the specifics, and having those numbers also makes it easier to evaluate what worked.

I then gather content we’ve already created, whether that’s property videos, walkthroughs, open house footage, or photographs. Repurposing footage gives that content another life, but agents could create something similar using listing photos.

In a recent development, once I have everything together, I open ChatGPT Voice and talk through the transaction. I’ll explain the sellers’ circumstances, our approach, the decisions we made and anything unexpected. I don’t organize my thoughts beforehand because I find it more helpful to get everything out and work through the story conversationally.

Industry observers note that what I’ve found particularly useful is having ChatGPT ask follow-up questions to identify the most compelling angle. Sometimes what I initially find interesting isn’t what another homeowner would care about, and that back-and-forth helps me consider their perspective.

It has been revealed that once we’ve found the angle, we work on the writing, particularly the opening two slides because Instagram can serve both to your audience. Lately, I’ve preferred carousels with moving video backgrounds, but we’ve also created Reels and experimented with humor. I’ve shared an editable version of our Canva template for anyone who wants to try the format.

If you want to try this with one of your transactions, open ChatGPT Voice and use this prompt:.

In a recent development, “Interview me about [Address] I recently closed. Ask me one question at a time about the seller’s goals, our marketing strategy, the decisions we made, challenges we encountered and the outcome. Help me identify the most compelling part of the story and why another homeowner would care. Once we’ve found the angle, help me write a seven-slide Instagram carousel with a strong opening and a natural narrative. Use specific details and results, avoid generic sales language, and don’t invent anything.”.

We’ve also been sharing these case studies in emails to our database, giving us another opportunity to demonstrate our experience to homeowners and agents who may eventually refer us business.

In a recent development, if you’ve been in the business for any length of time, you probably have dozens of transactions worth revisiting, with interesting stories buried in them. You don’t need a fresh closing every week to share those experiences, and you don’t need to make every transaction sound more dramatic than it was.

According to recent reports, there’s tremendous value in helping people understand the work we do, particularly when so much happens behind the scenes. If we’re already investing all this time and effort into helping our clients, it seems like a missed opportunity not to share more of it.

Use this FREE Canva template to replicate these results.

Sources indicate that krys Benyamein is a Realtor with Allstars Realty in Southern California. Get connected on Instagram or LinkedIn.

Recent findings suggest that GARDEN GROVE, Calif., Nov. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Harbinger, an American industrial technology platform company, today announced it has closed financing agreements totaling more than $100 million with Erebor Bank, co-founded by Palmer Luckey, and Pinegrove Venture Partners, which is sponsored by Brookfield Asset Management and HRTG Partners. The complementary financing structures include senior debt provided by Erebor and a separate convertible note from Pinegrove.

The transactions mark an vital step in Harbinger's evolution from an electric vehicle manufacturer to a broader industrial technology platform company reinventing the critical systems the world depends on across mobility, power, defense, autonomy and components. Harbinger develops advanced electrification technologies, including all-electric and hybrid medium-duty vehicle platforms, battery and drivetrain systems, energy storage and auxiliary power solutions, autonomous driving technology and defense applications.

Recent findings suggest that harbinger is now scaling production and fulfilling major commercial orders, including its recent multi-year order for 2,000 all-electric trucks from FedEx. Harbinger has added 400 jobs this year, primarily at its Orange County, California headquarters, and prepares to continue rapid growth next year, with the goal of creating hundreds of additional jobs around the country.

"Erebor finances companies building the future of American industryâbusinesses that are making real products, building factories, and scaling U.S. manufacturing," said Palmer Luckey. "Traditional lenders have struggled to support the unique capital needs of businesses developing real technology and scaling domestic jobs. Harbinger is exactly the kind of business we built Erebor to back: an American manufacturer building world-class technology. We're proud to provide the capital to help build more of America's industrial future here at home.".

According to recent reports, the debt financing comes on the heels of Harbinger's recently unveiled Series D funding round, and represents an expansion beyond the equity-driven funding model Harbinger has historically utilized as an emerging technology company. By accessing financing structures more commonly associated with established industrial manufacturers, Harbinger is building a more diversified capital strategy to support long-term growth while demonstrating how a new generation of American manufacturers can finance production at scale.

It has been revealed that "Building an industrial technology tech giant at scale requires a different financing approach," said John Harris, Co-Founder and CEO, Harbinger. "The capital needed to ramp production and deliver vehicles to customers shouldn't have to come entirely from equity. Major vehicle and aerospace manufacturers have long relied on debt financing to support their production operations, and we're bringing that same approach to Harbinger. Erebor is now our primary banking partner, and together with Pinegrove, they're helping us build the financial foundation to support our next stage of growth.".

In a recent development, erebor is a nationally chartered bank financing the companies rebuilding American industry. Erebor serves customers across 43 states, including businesses in manufacturing, defense, energy, AI, robotics, and aerospace, industries critical to America's national security and economic growth. Built on modern technology, regulated by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), and a member of the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC), Erebor has grown to $8 billion in assets by expanding access to capital for businesses historically underserved by legacy banks.

It has been revealed that "Harbinger is building an impressive industrial technology platform, and we're excited to partner with John and the team as they enter their next phase of growth," said Jim Ellison, Head of Credit, Pinegrove. "Our flexible convertible structure was designed around the company's capital needs and provides Harbinger with additional resources to continue scaling production and investing behind the significant opportunity ahead.".

Harbinger engineers systems from first principles, using deep vertical integration to design safer, more reliable, more capable and more efficient solutions at economic parity. Its technologies serve a range of applications, including medium-duty trucks, recreational vehicles (RVs), mobile healthcare units, power infrastructure and defense vehicles. Harbinger's mission is to solve the problems industry stopped questioning and raise the standard for what customers should expect.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Burn limits on Circle's legacy USDC bridge began falling on October 31, and the V1 contracts pause on December 1.
  • On the same migration page, a block of instructions written for AI coding assistants still claims Noble, Sui and Aptos "still require V1." Circle's own release notes say two of those three chains moved to V2 weeks ago.
  • In a recent development, circle's legacy cross-chain transfer protocol entered its final month today.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

Burn limits on Circle's legacy USDC bridge began falling on October 31, and the V1 contracts pause on December 1.

On the same migration page, a block of instructions written for AI coding assistants still claims Noble, Sui and Aptos "still require V1." Circle's own release notes say two of those three chains moved to V2 weeks ago.

In a recent development, circle's legacy cross-chain transfer protocol entered its final month today. From October 31, burn limits on CCTP V1 start falling toward zero, and on December 1 the V1 contracts pause. Any app still using them will stop moving USDC between chains.

It has been revealed that most coverage has focused on those two dates. But the guide developers are told to follow, Circle's V1-to-V2 migration page, contains a mistake in the section written for AI tools.

Embedded in the page is an "Agent Instructions" block, guidance meant for AI coding assistants that read the documentation for developers. It says: "Noble, Sui, and Aptos still require V1." For two of those three chains, Circle's other published records say the opposite.

The schedule is fixed. Circle revealed in an August 27 blog post that "CCTP V1 (Legacy) deprecation begins October 31, 2026 and completes on December 1, 2026.".

From today, V1 burn limits fall, and the migration guide says "message limits will tighten over time until no upcoming burns can be initiated." On December 1 the V1 contracts pause, and any integration still pointing at them can no longer transfer USDC between chains.

Circle has been firm about this. "Migration from CCTP V1 (Legacy) to CCTP V2 is required, not just recommended," the organization wrote, adding that V2 "uses separate contracts and APIs and is not backward compatible.".

Industry observers note that funds already in transit are protected. The guide claims "all pending redemptions will remain available" during the phase-out, and that Circle "will maintain minter allowances greater than the total of pending attestations.".

The migration page has two audiences. Human readers see the main guide. AI coding assistants also parse a separate instruction block, which tells them how to answer developer questions.

In that block, the guidance is clear: "Noble, Sui, and Aptos still require V1.".

The main text above it states something different. According to the human-facing guide, "CCTP V2 contracts are available on all CCTP V1 chains except for Noble and Sui," and "Sui will be supported by V2 before the deprecation begins." Aptos isn't listed as an exception there at all.

So one page gives two different answers about the same chains, and the out-of-date answer is the one written for AI tools.

Circle's 2026 CCTP release notes show how out of date the instruction is:.

Industry observers note that circle's supported chains and domains page now lists both Sui and Aptos in its CCTP table, with Standard Transfer support. The page's V1-only section names one chain: Noble.

As of today, Aptos has had V2 for more than two months and Sui for more than three weeks. The instruction telling AI tools that both "still require V1" was overtaken by Circle's own updates before the shutdown began.

Noble is the one chain in that line where the instruction is still accurate, and it is leaving CCTP entirely.

In a September 10 announcement, Circle stated "Noble will not receive CCTP V2" and set out its exit:.

For Noble, V1 is the only route available, and it is being closed.

A wrong line in documentation would normally be a small issue, but the timing makes this one more serious.

Many developers now ask AI assistants to write or patch integration code, and those assistants read documentation like this page. A developer asking how to bridge USDC to Sui or Aptos could be told, based on Circle's own instruction block, to use V1. That is the route whose burn limits started falling today and which pauses in a month.

The fix in the code is not small either. Moving to V2 means:.

An integration built on V1 now would have to be rebuilt within weeks.

For teams working with Sui and Aptos, the published records point one way: build on V2, using the contract addresses for domains 8 and 9. Don't follow the V1 guidance from the agent-instruction block.

It has been revealed that for Noble, the deadline is January 12, 2027. Before then, integrators need to remove Noble as a CCTP route, and holders need to move or redeem their USDC.

Recent findings suggest that for everyone else, the burn-limit reductions have started. December 1 is the last day V1 integrations work, and any app still on V1 after that will stop moving USDC between chains.

At the 2026 Breakpoint event, Brennan Watt, CEO of Anza, gave a walkthrough of Solana’s wins this year, while sharing what is in store for 2027.

According to Watt, 2026 was a major year for Solana as it migrated its consensus to Alpenglow, slashed the block times in half from 400 ms to 200 ms while doubling capacity.

Recent findings suggest that the Alpenglow upgrade went live on mainnet on October 21, 2026, cutting transaction finality from about 12.8 seconds down to roughly 150 milliseconds. It replaced TowerBFT with Votor, a faster path to reaching agreement.

After Alpenglow, @bw_solana laid out @anza_xyz roadmap for Solana in 2027 Performance: network compute capacity doubles, transactions cut 80% CU units for token accounts Expressivity: vector processing for models running fully onchain, 64 → 96 accounts per transaction, read account data instead of copying it so less data moves per transaction Market Structure: Alpenglow. Next with faster block distribution and Constellation for clearer ordering rules and more competition among validators Resilience: simpler protocol with fewer special cases, safer to change https://t.co/EpvDdSyjln.

Solana recently transitioned to 1.0, marking the network’s graduation from “mainnet beta” to “mainnet” and retiring the beta designation it has carried since launch. Solana 1.0 recognizes the progress on network performance, resilience, and developer experience.

According to Watt, Solana is eyeing significant improvements in 2027 across four categories. First is Resilience, which involves simplifying the protocol, reducing special cases, and making it safer to change.

“So, we're going to go ahead and simplify the protocol, replacing legacy abstractions and interfaces, pushing more of the execution on chain, and modernizing some of the wire formats. And all of this, you know, enhances resiliency, but it also allows us to move quicker and be more agile and deploy things and evolve the protocol more promptly,” Watt stated.

Second is Market Structure, which centers on Alpenglow, which aims for faster block distribution, and Constellation, which aims for clearer ordering rules and more competition among validators.

In a recent development, “Several vital Alpenglow extensions are coming,” Watt stated. Alpenglow rolls out in two phases: first is Votor, its voting protocol, which is already live on the platform; second is Rotor, a single relay layer planned for a later release that will replace Turbine, the protocol that spreads a block’s data across the network.

Recent findings suggest that third is Performance, where network compute capacity doubles and transactions use 80% fewer compute units for token accounts. Last is Expressivity, which involves vector processing for models running fully onchain and an increase from 64 to 96 accounts per transaction.

Watt also spoke about improvements in onchain development: “The cost of storing data on Solana came down by 27% this year. And just in the coming two weeks, we're going to bring this thing down by another 7x.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that while it’s easy to get starstruck when working for an athlete or other high-profile client, Yohann Sangaré, an agent with eXp’s sports and entertainment division, discourages it. “You come as a problem solver, not a fan,” he said.

Sangaré, a French former professional basketball player who played for 16 years across Europe, sometimes avoids reading up too much about his athlete clients’ accomplishments in their prospective sports so that he can focus on the task at hand: Finding them the right home and advising them on large investments.

In a recent development, sangaré came to the U.S. when he was hired to work for Tony Parker, his former teammate, in San Antonio, Texas; he started as a financial advisor for professional athletes. During COVID, he moved into real estate, specializing in finding homes for athletes instead.

Sangaré explains that the pros tend to make a lot of money for a short period of time, and for that reason they’re usually interested in buying investment properties (often right after they’ve found homes for themselves and their family members). A big part of their real estate agents’ job, then, is to keep their eyes on investment properties with the potential for strong returns.

Athletes have specific needs. “As a rookie, they’re just starting out, and they may not want to buy,” Sangaré told Taylor Anderson at eXpcon in Salt Lake City last month. Depending on the length of the contract, a rental might be a better idea. “There are times you tell people now’s not the right time to buy. If they feel you’re working in their best interests, they will trust you,” mentioned Sangaré, who is part of eXp’s relatively fresh sports and entertainment division (which several brokerages offer).

Sources indicate that you have to be patient when working with athletes, he stated, since their situations are tied to ever-changing contracts; of course, players can be traded, and have to move quickly. You also have to be prepared to wait and work with them as they grow in their careers.

What you don’t have to be: A major follower of their particular sports. Sangaré admits that as a European, he doesn’t know much about football or baseball, but that doesn’t stop him from working with athletes in those sports. Sometimes not being starstruck helps him work with a more level head, he noted.

According to recent reports, but you do need to know the nuances of sports contracts. For example, some leagues, like the NBA, offer several-year guarantees, while others, like the NFL, don’t; housing options will vary based on those.

Industry observers note that often the connection to an athlete client comes through their financial advisor or sports agent, Sangaré mentioned. “The sports agent is always talking to the player, and he’ll know to reach out to you when someone gets traded,” he said.

But that can be a long road. Sangaré stated it can take anywhere from five months to two years from starting a relationship with a sports agent to seeing any traction with a player, but you want to start that relationship early since once their clients do start to get traded, they’ll undoubtedly be approached by many other real estate agents. One practical tip he gives is going to the NBA Summer League in Las Vegas and taking agents out for coffee or lunch. “You have to be present where they’re present,” he said.

And when you do get connected to the client, make sure you don’t start with a sales pitch. “You can’t try to sell them something right away,” Sangaré mentioned; instead, you want to counsel them on how they can protect themselves and what they really need to know when buying a home — whether as an investment property or to live in.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Investment firm Roundhill has suddenly terminated plans to launch two fresh XRP- and Solana (SOL)-based exchange-traded funds (ETFs).

This decision comes after over a year of regulatory filings and multiple delays.

As per the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) filings on Nov. 18, Roundhill has officially withdrawn prepares to launch the Roundhill XRP Covered Call Strategy ETF and Roundhill Solana Covered Call Strategy ETF.

According to recent reports, interestingly, it submitted the applications for these two funds on Oct. 17, 2025. Therefore, these two funds had been awaiting launch for over 13 months.

As per the latest regulatory filings, Roundhill has been consistently delaying the effective dates for these two funds.

However, instead of launching them, the investment firm has decided to drop both products.

In its requests to withdraw the filings for these funds, Roundhill revealed that it "has no further intention to pursue effectiveness of the Fund." The firm noted that it had not sold any shares under the registrations for these two funds.

Intriguingly, Roundhill failed to elaborate on the sudden decision to axe its plans to launch these two ETFs.

It has been revealed that roundhill was planning to launch income-generating XRP and Solana ETFs using a covered call strategy. In such a strategy, investors sell options to earn premiums while also maintaining exposure to the price movements of XRP and Solana.

It has been revealed that unlike spot-based ETFs, these funds would not have held the cryptocurrencies directly. Instead, they would have used options written against existing cryptocurrency ETFs.

A covered call strategy can be useful for generating regular income. However, it can also cap profits during strong market rallies.

Recent findings suggest that notably, there has been relatively low demand for income-generating cryptocurrency investment products. This raises concerns about investors' interest in these ETFs.

Surprisingly, this decision came amid substantial net inflows into spot-based XRP and Solana ETFs.

Sources indicate that U.S. spot XRP and Solana ETFs recorded net inflows of roughly $969 million between May and October 2026, according to data from SoSoValue.

Overall, these spot ETFs held around $3.26 billion in assets under management as of the end of October.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that the organization didn’t disclose the terms of the deal.
  • In August, reports emerged that the company had drawn takeover interest from Anthropic PBC.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 20:40 EST / NOVEMBER 23 2026.

Amazon.com Inc. today announced prepares to hire the technical staff of startup Decart.AI Inc. and acquire its core technology.

It has been revealed that the organization didn’t disclose the terms of the deal. However, sources told Bloomberg that Amazon is paying about $7.5 billion. That’s nearly twice the valuation Decart reportedly received after its most recent funding round in May.

In August, reports emerged that the company had drawn takeover interest from Anthropic PBC. The artificial intelligence provider reportedly sought to buy Decart for $6 billion but walked away from the deal in September. Rumors that Amazon could swoop in emerged the following month.

According to recent reports, decart founders Dean Leitersdorf, Moshe Shalev and Orian Leitersdorf will join the tech giant along with Decart’s research team. Additionally, Amazon is acquiring the technology behind the organization’s DOS platform, which helps boost the efficiency of AI models. Decart claims that the software can reduce the cost of some neural networks by a hundredfold.

In a recent development, the firm hasn’t shared detailed information about how DOS works. However, the blog post in which Decart revealed its May funding round did reveal that the platform optimizes AI models by “tuning the kernels.”.

Kernels are the basic building blocks of neural networks. They’re relatively simple code snippets designed to run across a large number of chip cores. One common approach to optimizing them, kernel fusion, combines multiple kernels into a single code snippet that uses less hardware. In July, Decart disclosed that a custom model it had developed with DOS uses kernel fusion.

Sources indicate that the company says that the platform also includes “proprietary compilers.” AI compilers translate neural networks into the platform-specific programming language of the host chip. They also optimize the models along they way. For example, the compiler that Amazon Web Services offers for its AWS Trainium machine learning chip uses quantization to compress models into a more memory-efficient form.

Sources indicate that it’s unclear whether Decart positions DOS as an alternative to the default compilers provided with AI accelerators. According to Amazon, Decart has “worked closely” with its engineers since 2025 to optimize the performance of workloads deployed on its Trainium chips. The newest commercially available iteration of the chip, Tranium3, provides 2.52 petaflops of performance when processing FP8 data.

Amazon stated that the acquisition will help “further optimize both its inference and custom silicon performance.” According to the company, the goal is to not only speed up customers’ models but also lower their cost.

“Every leap forward in AI starts with getting more out of every chip,” mentioned Peter DeSantis, Amazon’s senior vice president of foundational AI models, custom silicon and quantum computing. “More efficient compute means better training, better reinforcement learning, faster inference, and better models for customers at a lower cost.”.

The acquisition doesn’t include Decart’s portfolio of internally developed AI models. Its two newest algorithms, Lucy 2.5 and Oasis 3, are world models that generate virtual environments based on prompts. The former algorithm is optimized for low-latency content creation, while the latter is designed to generate training data for robots.

Founded in 2013, Aosom operates across Europe and North America, with local subsidiaries in nine countries, including France, the UK, Germany, Spain, Portugal, Canada and the US.

Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin led the daily ranking of stablecoin inflows into decentralized finance (DeFi), according to Token Terminal data that RWA Foundation shared on X. The DeFi total value locked (TVL) of Ripple's stablecoin grew by $22.3 million over 24 hours, and Tether added $21.6 million. RWA Foundation titled its chart "Ripple led stablecoin DeFi growth.".

Paxos, Open Standard and Societe Generale followed with $7.8 million, $4 million and $1.2 million, respectively. World Liberty, United Stables, MetaMask, Tori and Liquity each added less than $700,000 over the same period.

About $1.05 billion was on the XRP Ledger, Ripple's home network. On Ethereum, the stablecoin is used in DeFi pools on Aave V3, Curve and Morpho.

Sources indicate that RLUSD is issued by Standard Custody & Trust under the supervision of the Fresh York State Department of Financial Services (NYDFS), and its reserves are held at custodian bank BNY. In the fall, RLUSD received a Moody's rating and was listed on Coinbase and Robinhood, and Ripple received final approval from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) to launch Ripple National Trust Bank.

Ripple has also integrated RLUSD with payment providers Arf, Convera and Cross River Bank, and the stablecoin is now used in dollar settlements between companies.

In a CNBC interview on Nov. 19, Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse called blockchain-based transactions "a wave of emerging technology." "I think 10 years from now you'll see blockchain implemented across our financial infrastructure," he noted.

#179280. Raleigh’s housing reforms helped ease rents, Pew study finds

Raleigh’s housing reforms helped ease rents, Pew study finds

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (912 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housingwire

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that for years, homebuilding leaders have argued that the most effective way to lower housing costs is to build more, and that cities that adopt pro-housing reforms will be rewarded with greater supply and more attainable housing.
  • Industry observers note that following the pandemic, Raleigh overhauled its zoning and land use laws to make building easier, Pew found.
  • It has been revealed that the report highlights how adding newly introduced housing supply at scale can improve housing affordability, echoing similar impacts that followed concerted rezoning efforts in Minneapolis-St.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that for years, homebuilding leaders have argued that the most effective way to lower housing costs is to build more, and that cities that adopt pro-housing reforms will be rewarded with greater supply and more attainable housing. New research from The Pew Charitable Trusts shows what happened when Raleigh, N.C., followed that playbook.

Industry observers note that following the pandemic, Raleigh overhauled its zoning and land use laws to make building easier, Pew found. The result was a building boom, particularly for the townhomes and apartments the city’s earlier rules constrained. This uptick in homebuilding made renting more affordable in North Carolina’s capital city, especially for middle-income households and younger residents.

It has been revealed that the report highlights how adding newly introduced housing supply at scale can improve housing affordability, echoing similar impacts that followed concerted rezoning efforts in Minneapolis-St. Paul, Minn., and Austin, Texas. The same dynamic is playing out across the Sun Belt, where many of the nation’s fastest-growing metros also have some of the loosest zoning rules, and where rents and home prices have dropped more dramatically than anywhere else in the country.

Raleigh didn’t rely on a single fix to make building housing easier. Its reforms combined a rewrite of its form-based code, an end to parking minimums, denser building near transit and a housing bond to support affordable housing.

“Of all of the drivers of housing costs – population growth, an influx of high-income earners, high land costs and high construction costs – we have the most agency and direct control over restrictive zoning regulations,” Patrick Young, Raleigh’s planning and development director, remarked in a statement.

Raleigh’s 2021 zoning reform, which expanded the city’s already-established form-based code, opened the door to more “missing middle” housing. It did so by replacing units-per-acre caps with physical standards such as lot size, yards, and building height.

It has been revealed that the changes legalized duplexes, triplexes and quadplexes in more residential districts and expanded where townhomes can be built. Under the new form-based code, further refined in 2022, builders can now construct small apartment buildings and tiny houses with up to two dwelling units on compact infill lots.

As a result, builders can now construct missing middle housing in more of Raleigh’s neighborhoods, a shift that Pew links to better affordability for middle-income and younger residents.

Sources indicate that raleigh eliminated its citywide parking minimums in 2022. That allowed developers to fit more housing units on each property and, in some cases, spared them the expense of building costly parking structures, which can often make a project too costly to pursue.

The city also spurred housing growth by allowing taller, denser buildings near major transit corridors. Transit Overlay District zones allowed for an extra story along Bus Rapid Transit corridors, extending half a mile along some local bus routes.

Additionally, a density bonus allows developers to exceed height limits by up to 50% if at least 20% of the extra units are designated as affordable, below-market units.

The City of Raleigh approved an $80 million housing bond in 2020 that is projected to create at least 700 affordable homes, fund homebuyer assistance and help homeowners with home repairs.

About $14 million has already gone to four developments totaling more than 240 units, while another $24 million in gap financing will back over 470 additional units, more than 90% of which will be affordable to households earning 60% of area median income or less.

According to recent reports, between 2021 and 2024, Raleigh added 16,884 housing units, growing its housing stock by 7.7%, even as the city’s population grew by 5.8% over the same period. Raleigh’s housing growth also outpaced the state (5.7%) and national (3.2%) rates during that period.

Of the 16,884 units added, roughly 2,000, or 12%, were affordable to households earning 80% or less of area median income (AMI), with Raleigh’s housing bond funds helping support their development. Density bonuses contributed about 200 of those affordable units, accounting for 10% of the total.

According to recent reports, additionally, Raleigh’s code changes intentionally shifted a large share of production away from detached single-family homes toward townhomes, duplexes and tiny homes. Since 2021, the city has issued more than twice as many townhouse permits as in 2015 to 2020, and has permitted more than 200 duplex units and over 200 accessory dwelling units (ADUs).

As a result, average monthly rents rose at only half the national pace and fell in real, inflation-adjusted terms. Pew’s analysis estimates inflation-adjusted rents declined 15% from 2022 to 2025, and, as of 2025, the income needed to afford the city’s median rent dropped from 79% of AMI to 65%.

It has been revealed that raleigh’s experience mirrors a wider trend among fast-growing Sun Belt markets, where less restrictive zoning and fewer barriers to housing development have supported greater housing production and helped moderate housing costs. The South accounted for more than half of all U.S. housing starts between 2021 and 2025, while Sun Belt markets continue to lead the nation in rent and home price declines.

According to recent reports, according to Yardi Matrix’s October 2026 multifamily report, rents fell year over year in 12 major US markets. The Sun Belt accounted for ten of those, led by Austin, Houston, Nashville, Tampa and Phoenix. The for-sale market highlights a similar pattern, with home prices dropping disproportionately in the Sun Belt while climbing in the Northeast and Midwest.

Sometimes the most valuable data is the house nobody bought

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (834 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Inman

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Canceled listing data in the MLS can reveal where buyers stated no.
  • When agents sit down to price a listing, we know the drill: Pull the solds.
  • But there’s another category of data sitting right there in the MLS that we frequently overlook: the houses nobody bought.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Want to price more precisely? Canceled listing data in the MLS can reveal where buyers stated no. Learn three steps to add failed listings to your next CMA.

When agents sit down to price a listing, we know the drill: Pull the solds. Look at what’s coming soon, active and pending. Adjust for condition, location, square footage and amenities. Figure out where our house fits.

But there’s another category of data sitting right there in the MLS that we frequently overlook: the houses nobody bought.

Sources indicate that expired. Canceled. Withdrawn. Earlier in my career, I looked at these failed listings all the time. Then the market changed. When inventory became tight, and buyers were competing for homes, digging through failed listings often wasn’t necessary to determine where a property would sell.

Now the market is shifting again; pricing must be more precise, and I’m sharpening my approach by bringing an old tool back into my pricing process.

Industry observers note that A sold comp tells us where a buyer remarked yes, but a failed listing can help us figure out where buyers said no. And in a buyer-favored market, that’s valuable information.

Imagine you’re pricing a home, and the recent comparable sales range from $600,000 to $625,000. Then you expand your search.

Sources indicate that suddenly, you know considerably more than the sold comps alone told you. Other sellers have already tested the upper limits of pricing, and buyers responded. It’s essentially a series of pricing experiments someone else conducted for you — and they paid the carrying costs.

Recent findings suggest that one of the most interesting things buried in MLS history is the pricing journey. A property might show a final list price of $649,000 and an eventual sale of $630,000. Dig deeper, and you may discover this:.

$725,000 → $699,000 → $675,000 → canceled → relisted at $649,000 → sold for $630,000.

That’s a different story. The sale tells us what one buyer eventually paid. The listing history tells us buyers had previously rejected that house at $725,000, $699,000 and $675,000.

It has been revealed that it also illustrates something sellers don’t always understand: Getting to the right price eventually isn’t necessarily the same as pricing correctly from the beginning. After months of market exposure and multiple reductions, buyers may stop asking, “Could this be the house?” They start asking, “What’s wrong with it?”.

It has been revealed that when I find a comparable property that sat for 90 days without selling, I want to know what did sell during those same 90 days. Sometimes we blame the market when the market was functioning just fine. Buyers were buying houses. They simply weren’t buying that one.

Recent findings suggest that maybe they chose the renovated house at $640,000. Maybe they paid $650,000 for the better lot. They may have even paid more for another property because it offered something the failed listing didn’t. That’s useful information when you’re sitting across from a seller who believes buyers just need more time to appreciate their home.

If buyers repeatedly toured the property and purchased competing homes instead, the market may already have delivered its opinion.

This is where agents have to resist oversimplifying the data. An expired listing isn’t automatic proof that a house was overpriced, and a canceled listing certainly isn’t either.

Sources indicate that listings fail for all sorts of reasons. Sellers change their minds. Job transfers fall through. Repairs surface. Agents get fired. Sometimes a seller receives a perfectly acceptable offer and decides not to move.

So, investigate. Call the previous agent. I might simply say:.

Industry observers note that “I’m pricing a similar property and noticed yours was on the market last year. Is there anything you can tell me about the activity or why the seller decided not to continue?”.

Twenty-seven showings and no offers tell me something. Two showings in four months tells me something different.

There’s one more number worth considering: the cost of the pricing journey.

It has been revealed that find a house that started high, sat, reduced, expired, relisted and eventually sold. Then compare it with similar homes that entered the market closer to where buyers were actually buying.

Industry observers note that sellers often view aspirational pricing as a no-risk strategy: “We can always come down.” Technically, that’s true. But time isn’t free, and neither is market perception.

The next time you’re preparing a CMA in a shifting or buyer-favored market:.

Recent findings suggest that we’re very good at studying success in real estate. But as pricing gets harder, I’ve found myself returning to an old habit: studying the failures, too. Sold listings tell us where buyers have been willing to say yes. Sometimes the house nobody bought is the one that tells us exactly where they started saying no.

by Todd Bishop on Nov 17, 2026 at 11:57 amNovember 17, 2026 at 12:33 pm.

In a recent development, microsoft is a partner and investor in both OpenAI and Anthropic, and it sells their AI models to its own customers. But another role was on full display during the company’s Ignite keynote Tuesday: competitor.

“Simply stated, anything you can do in Claude or ChatGPT, you can do better with Copilot and for less,” stated Judson Althoff, CEO of Microsoft’s commercial business, during the opening keynote at the company’s annual conference for IT professionals and business customers in San Francisco.

Industry observers note that jacob Andreou, Microsoft’s executive vice president of Copilot, went further. “We’ve all seen Anthropic and OpenAI embrace documents, slides, and spreadsheets, but their simplified viewers and editors force compromise on power and collaboration,” he stated.

It has been revealed that the full versions of Word, Excel and PowerPoint inside Copilot are included in the subscription. “That means that Copilot is the only way to draft a PowerPoint presentation without spinning a meter,” Andreou remarked.

Microsoft’s cost comparison: Andreou backed up the pitch with a chart of estimated monthly costs per business user, including subscription and usage fees. It put Copilot at $30 for an “everyday” AI user, compared with $81 for ChatGPT and $205 for Claude.

For “advanced” users of each company’s agent tools, it showed $96 for Copilot, $149 for ChatGPT and $299 for Claude. Most of the Claude figure is estimated usage charges on top of Anthropic’s $20 enterprise seat.

Recent findings suggest that the numbers come from research Microsoft commissioned and paid for from GigaOm, based on testing Microsoft ran in October on modeled workloads. They reflect enterprise pricing, which adds usage charges to a per-seat fee, not the flat monthly subscriptions that individuals pay for ChatGPT and Claude.

In a recent development, partners and rivals: The pitch comes as Anthropic expands into Microsoft’s core business. Last week it introduced new Claude-based tools for spreadsheets and whiteboards that compete more directly with Office. The tech giant is expected to make its IPO this week, putting new scrutiny on its financials and long-term growth prospects.

The companies’ products are also intertwined. Anthropic’s Claude for Microsoft 365, for example, lets people use Claude inside Office apps for tasks such as sorting email and creating slide decks.

The product has less than a tenth as many weekly owners as the paid version of Copilot in Office, The Information reported Monday, citing internal Microsoft data. Andreou is one of the executives who see that as a sign Microsoft can keep customers from switching, the report stated.

Fresh MAI models: Microsoft AI also released a new batch of its own MAI models, built to compete with OpenAI and Anthropic for a fraction of the price. It’s a notable stance, given that Microsoft still sells their models, too. On the same stage, CEO Satya Nadella unveiled that OpenAI’s GPT-6.2, released Tuesday morning, is now available in Microsoft Foundry.

The lineup includes MAI Code 2, available in GitHub Copilot starting Tuesday. Microsoft claims it delivers 96% of the coding performance of Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the price, on benchmarks Microsoft chose.

Microsoft also introduced MAI Cyber 2 Flash, a security model it notes matches OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra on one benchmark at less than 2% of the cost per task. Other new models cover image editing, live speech and transcription.

In a recent development, the other new business: MAI Licensed Weights. Companies can take a Microsoft AI model, customize it with their own data and run it in their own Azure environment, with help from Microsoft’s Frontier Organization consulting arm. AT&T used an earlier version of the program, Custom Models, to build a MAI model for 5G network analytics.

It’s the latest step in Microsoft’s push for what Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman has called “long term self-sufficiency,” which started with seven homegrown models at Build in June.

Keeping costs in check: The cost theme ran through the keynote. In a demo, Althoff indicated Copilot building a keynote outline, a slide deck and a customer tracker for a retail conference, plus an agent he named Amelia to keep the work going.

Sources indicate that the cost of his two-hour Sunday session: about 10,000 credits, or roughly $100. Althoff presented that as a bargain compared with the staff time it would have taken: “my team hits the ground running for NRF without me bothering them,” he noted.

It has been revealed that microsoft is also selling tools to keep that bill in check. A newly introduced Agent 365 Business Analytics feature demonstrates business leaders what’s driving their AI spending and what they’re getting for it, and a companion Cost Management tool lets IT set spending policies and get alerts. Microsoft cited a McKinsey survey in which 93% of respondents reported exceeding their AI budgets.

According to recent reports, in another notable announcement, Microsoft and Salesforce unveiled “Copilotforce,” bringing Salesforce customer data and actions into Copilot, Teams and Fabric. The Copilot plugin is available in preview.

Earlier, Nadella opened the keynote by addressing last week’s global Outlook outage.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

AKT stakers are close to approving Akash's move from Cosmos to Solana, with Mintscan projecting a pass at 97.2% yes as voting enters its final hours.

But a yes on Proposal 346 opens a door rather than completing a move. Before a single AKT reaches Solana, two independent audits and at least two more on-chain votes still have to happen.

In a recent development, the summary going around is simple: Akash is leaving Cosmos for Solana. The proposal itself is narrower than that, and the details matter for anyone holding AKT.

Industry observers note that proposal 346 on akashnet-2, titled "Migrate the Akash Protocol to Solana," closes at 15:02 UTC on November 2. A yes vote approves the migration plan and authorises AKT to launch as an SPL token through a one-way portal that stays open for two years. It does not set a cutover date, it does not move a single lease, and on its own it does not open the portal.

Sources indicate that the technical spec for that portal was published the day after voting opened. It highlights how many further steps lie between this vote and a working SPL AKT.

The proposal text in Akash's AEP repository says a yes vote does two things:.

It also says plainly what it doesn't do: "it does not set a cutover date and does not move the marketplace." Live leases, staking and governance on akashnet-2 continue as normal. The marketplace moves only after audits and rehearsals pass and "a separate cutover proposal passes on this chain.".

Sources indicate that A no vote would stop the whole plan. In the proposal's words: "Nothing moves; the token does not launch and the program returns to option analysis.".

At 08:43 UTC on November 2, about six hours before voting closed, Mintscan's page for Proposal 346 highlighted an expected result of "Will PASS":.

In a recent development, turnout stood at 68.80% of bonded stake, against a quorum of 33.40%. The same figures can be read from Akash's own chain API, through the proposal object and its tally endpoint.

In a recent development, mintscan's 97.2% is yes as a share of all votes cast. Akash's pass threshold leaves abstentions out, and on that basis yes stands at about 98.7%, far above the 50% needed. The veto share is negligible.

Recent findings suggest that the tally has barely changed since early morning. A read of the chain at 07:29 UTC showed almost exactly the same totals, with only a handful of AKT added to the yes side. With turnout and margin that large, the outcome is not in doubt. The more useful question is what happens after it passes.

According to recent reports, the portal's design is in AEP-95, "One-Way AKT Sink to Solana,", a draft published on October 27 by core developers Artur Troian and Joseph Chalabi. It describes a "deliberately one-way" bridge with no return path. The authors say this removes "the largest class of bridge attacks.".

Recent findings suggest that why supply doesn't change: every SPL AKT is backed by AKT locked on Akash, and nothing is minted independently on Solana. The token is a legacy SPL mint with six decimals and no freeze authority.

The spec's own risk table names the biggest trust point. The upgrade authority over the Solana programs could "mint without limit." That power is meant to sit with a time-locked multisig appointed by Akash governance, with monitors set to alert on every admin action.

In a recent development, at launch, SPL AKT has no protocol role. It will support "transfers and DEX liquidity only, with no staking or governance rights." Inflation stays on Akash. To seed trading, Overclock Labs, Akash's core developer, will send 1 million AKT through the bridge to a Solana treasury vault. That deposit follows the same rules as everyone else's.

Proposal 346 requires "two independent audits of the token and portal code before launch," with reports published within 30 days. AEP-95's launch sequence indicates what that requirement means on-chain.

So Proposal 346 is the first of at least five on-chain decisions. The "2 to 3 weeks" launch estimate depends on the audits finishing and the upgrade and parameter votes passing on schedule.

Recent findings suggest that for now, nothing. The proposal's disclosures set out what changes later:.

Discussion of the proposal continues in GitHub Discussion #1123.

The proposal lists four items as "still open, to be settled and published before the cutover proposal":.

It has been revealed that the second item matters most to holders. The portal closes two years after launch, and the proposal doesn't yet say what happens to AKT that hasn't crossed by then. The final tally will confirm whether the plan goes ahead, but that answer, and the decisions in the votes that follow, will matter more to most holders than today's margin.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mara Geraghty explains how hurricane deductibles affect insurance claims, what homeowners may owe after a storm, and why reviewing coverage matters.
  • 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- How do hurricane deductibles work in Florida homeowners insurance?
  • The HelloNation article explains that a hurricane deductible often differs from a standard deductible.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mara Geraghty explains how hurricane deductibles affect insurance claims, what homeowners may owe after a storm, and why reviewing coverage matters.

DAVENPORT, Fla., Nov. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- How do hurricane deductibles work in Florida homeowners insurance? The answer is provided in a HelloNation article featuring insights from Mara Geraghty, Insurance Agent of Davenport, Florida. The article explains why understanding these costs matters before a hurricane causes damage.

How Is a Hurricane Deductible Calculated?

The HelloNation article explains that a hurricane deductible often differs from a standard deductible. Instead of a fixed amount, it is usually a percentage of the home's dwelling coverage.

For example, a home with $300,000 in dwelling coverage and a 2% hurricane deductible would have a $6,000 deductible. At 5%, that amount would increase to $15,000.

The article notes that these amounts depend on the insured value, not the repair bill or market price.

How Do Hurricane Deductibles Affect Insurance Claims?

The article explains that homeowners must pay their deductible before insurance covers the remaining eligible damage.

If a hurricane causes $10,000 in covered damage and the deductible is $6,000, the insurer may pay $4,000, subject to policy terms.

Notably, the move arrived when Solana was trading around $74, briefly shifting into green territory just a few days after it retested $67, the lowest level seen since June 2026.

Since the prolonged price correction has continued to weaken investor confidence, it appears that the whales have acted upon the growing fear and withdrawn the assets they had initially committed to the Solana network to hedge against further losses.
