Tech Report: Georgia builders give affordable housing an essential newly introduced identity

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (977 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housingwire

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Put an affordable housing project on a planning commission agenda, and the neighborhood naysayers come out of the woodwork to fight.
  • Recent findings suggest that they argue it will destroy the neighborhood’s character.
  • Recent findings suggest that what’s in a name?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Put an affordable housing project on a planning commission agenda, and the neighborhood naysayers come out of the woodwork to fight.

Recent findings suggest that they argue it will destroy the neighborhood’s character. Labeling the development as workforce housing doesn’t help much.

Recent findings suggest that what’s in a name? An affordable home – or neighborhood – by any other name is still affordable, no? Still, companies rebrand when the current brand is struggling. And Georgia homebuilders and land developers are taking a crack at giving “affordable housing” a brand makeover, one that’s less stigma and more economic and social fabric dynamism.

The Georgia Residential Land Development Council and the Home Builders Association teamed up to dub affordable housing “essential homes.” They are pairing it with a tagline: “Homes for the people who keep Georgia working.”.

But defining essential homes as housing that workers can afford near where they work could be applied broadly as lawmakers from the federal to local levels wrestle with how to make housing more affordable.

“It’s a reality nationally that the buying power of the average American is not considered in land use and zoning policies,” Jay Knight, GRLDC’s chairman, told HousingWire TBD. “Essential homes for essential people intends to move the conversation from sticks and bricks allowed to the key people being prohibited.”.

Industry observers note that the definition names no home size or price point. It asks whether the people who work in a community can afford to live there. Teachers, firefighters, nurses, first responders, healthcare workers and skilled tradespeople are among the livelihoods the term “essential” captures best. They also include younger Georgians hoping to buy a first home.

Industry observers note that austin Hackney, HBAG’s executive vice president, said in a statement that the term puts a human face on the affordability debate. He said that when workers can’t find homes within reach of their income, the effects reach employers, schools and local businesses.

The rebrand comes with a policy push. The groups say zoning restrictions, long permit reviews, infrastructure requirements and delayed final plat approvals add substantial costs that end up in home prices.

GRLDC helped advance Senate Bill 447, which took effect July 1. The law sets timelines and accountability for Georgia’s land disturbance permit reviews. The council’s next target is final plat and bond reform. It wants reasonable approval timelines, standardized bonding requirements, and an end to delays that keep completed developments from moving forward.

According to recent reports, the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development considers housing affordable when occupants pays no more than 30% of gross income on housing costs. Programs add other definitions, often tied to area median income. Affordable housing typically targets households at 60% of the area median income or less, while workforce housing covers roughly 60% to 120%.

Workforce housing, however, isn’t explicitly defined in federal law or regulation, according to a March 2026 Congressional Research Service analysis. But the term is used to avoid saying a housing development is affordable housing.

Opposition often centers on neighborhood character. Researchers also find residents may fear newcomers’ socioeconomic status more than the buildings themselves. Property values are another common worry, though research cited by the Florida Housing Coalition found almost no negative effect on neighboring market-rate homes.

Recent findings suggest that knight noted the definition problem became clear at a speaking engagement. He asked a room of roughly 40 people to define affordable housing. One woman said Section 8. Someone else said anything under $400,000. A person from the Northeast thought it meant rent control.

Knight said that convinced him people weren’t talking about the same thing, which made the conversation unproductive. His business partner suggested essential homes. Knight said the organizations liked it immediately.

Terms such as affordable homes, starter homes, first-time buyer or workforce housing arrive with a definition already attached. Knight said “essential homes” encourages people to ask what it means, which gives the groups a chance to set the definition themselves.

The rationale behind the rebranding is that if local governments can dictate what can be built, the standard shouldn’t exceed what their own employees can buy. Knight remarked the average municipal employee earns about $60,000 to $62,000 a year in Georgia. That means they can afford about a $225,000 home.

In most U.S. markets today, that would buy roughly 1,100 square feet on a 35-foot detached lot, with no garage and no homeowners association, he said. He added that would put the price at about three and a half times annual income, close to the ratio GIs returning from World War II paid in the late 1940s and 1950s.

Recent findings suggest that knight remarked zoning conditions have pushed home prices to a much higher ratio. High-cost areas like California, New York and Florida are prime examples. In Silicon Valley, the median home price is 11.4 times median household income, according to an annual report from Harvard University’s Joint Center for Housing Studies. The Miami metro’s ratio is 7.6.

According to recent reports, high prices relative to income are a major reason the median first-time homebuyer is now 40. It’s an all-time high, according to the National Association of Realtors. Such a disparity is why California and Florida have been at the forefront of housing reforms.

It has been revealed that the Georgia campaign will put faces to the term: a police officer, a teacher, a nurse and a forklift operator. Knight noted it will portray the kinds of workers that municipalities court with industry.

Sources indicate that knight, who sits on an advisory council for the National Association of Home Builders, stated he has shared the term with the executive director of the Houston Home Builders Association. He said Houston is now discussing it, since builders nationwide are having the same conversations.

“Who can be against essential housing?” Knight said.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Italian physical artificial intelligence cybersecurity company Exein SpA today introduced an AI agent called Ray that it claims can help manufacturers find the security weaknesses that matter most in their connected-device firmware.
  • In a recent development, ray is built into Exein Analyzer, the tech giant’s firmware security platform, which examines firmware for vulnerabilities, security weaknesses and compliance challenges.
  • The new offering is designed to address a growing security gap for manufacturers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 07:00 EST / NOVEMBER 24 2026.

Italian physical artificial intelligence cybersecurity company Exein SpA today introduced an AI agent called Ray that it claims can help manufacturers find the security weaknesses that matter most in their connected-device firmware.

In a recent development, ray is built into Exein Analyzer, the tech giant’s firmware security platform, which examines firmware for vulnerabilities, security weaknesses and compliance challenges. Engineers can then use Ray to explore those findings in a conversational way, looking at the security posture of a single product or an entire fleet.

The new offering is designed to address a growing security gap for manufacturers. Some connected products contain thousands of software components, and a single scan of one can flag hundreds of potential challenges, Exein mentioned. Which of those weaknesses actually needs to be fixed first is said to be the harder question.

Rather than working through separate vulnerability lists, security scores, trackers and compliance reports, engineers can put questions to Ray about Analyzer’s findings. Among the questions engineers can ask are what is driving a product’s security score, which vulnerabilities need attention first and which compliance challenges affect a firmware image.

In a recent development, to pick out the small number of issues that pose the greatest risk, Ray draws on Analyzer’s scan results, vulnerability reachability data and compliance findings. An explanation of why each problem matters is provided alongside the results. In cases where the same weakness appears across multiple products, Ray is said to help teams see when addressing one issue could improve security across an entire product line.

Exein is launching Ray after a run of attacks on connected infrastructure across Europe, including cyberattacks on supermarket refrigeration systems that disrupted stores in several countries in October and November. Similar risks extend to industrial equipment, healthcare, energy and transport systems, according to the tech giant.

“Europe is connecting more of the physical world to software,” co-founder and Chief Technology Officer Giovanni Falcione said, “but too many products were never designed for the threat environment we have today. The recent attacks on refrigeration systems are a reminder that a weakness buried inside firmware can have consequences far beyond IT.”.

Sources indicate that the rate at which those weaknesses can be found and exploited is being “dramatically” accelerated by AI, Falcione said. With Ray, he said, engineering teams get a clearer way to work out what needs fixing before products reach the field, without every firmware engineer having to become a cybersecurity expert.

Also included in Ray is support for reading Analyzer’s findings against regulatory requirements such as the European Union’s Cyber Resilience Act. Reporting obligations under the act for actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe security incidents have applied since September, with the wider requirements taking effect in December 2027.

Industry observers note that founded in 2018, Exein offers technology that is distributed across more than 2 billion connected devices in sectors including industrial automation, automotive, energy, healthcare and robotics. The organization’s other offerings include Photon, which provides runtime security for connected devices, physical AI and autonomous AI agents. It raised $270 million at a $1.7 billion valuation in September.

Make it 8: Connecticut joins first responder homebuying push

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (835 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Inman

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Connecticut is the latest state to help first responders reach their homeownership goals with assistance for down payments and closing costs.
  • The “First Responders’ Time to Own” program gives state and local police officers, full-time and volunteer firefighters and emergency medical service personnel $25,000 in forgivable assistance through the Connecticut Housing Finance Authority (CHFA) and the Connecticut Department of Housing.
  • In addition to down payment and closing cost help, the program gives applicants a 0.125 percentage point interest rate reduction on their CHFA first mortgage.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Connecticut is the latest state to help first responders reach their homeownership goals with assistance for down payments and closing costs.

The “First Responders’ Time to Own” program gives state and local police officers, full-time and volunteer firefighters and emergency medical service personnel $25,000 in forgivable assistance through the Connecticut Housing Finance Authority (CHFA) and the Connecticut Department of Housing. To qualify, first responders must have completed two years of service and purchase a primary residence within the community they serve.

In addition to down payment and closing cost help, the program gives applicants a 0.125 percentage point interest rate reduction on their CHFA first mortgage.

In a recent development, “Connecticut’s police officers, firefighters and EMS personnel dedicate themselves to protecting our families and communities, and we want to make sure they have the opportunity to build their own futures here,” Governor Ned Lamont stated in a prepared statement on Tuesday. “By helping reduce one of the biggest barriers to buying a home, we’re investing in the people who serve our state and the communities that depend on them.”.

The program is part of Public Act 26-12, a state bill that aims to increase the number of first responders with a number of incentives, including college tuition reimbursement and improved labor protections.

Sources indicate that “The people who protect and serve our communities should be able to afford to live in those communities, and this program with help them do it,” Comptroller Sean Scanlon noted in a written statement. “Helping the people who put their lives on the line for us every day buy their first home is literally the least we can do, and I’m proud to have worked with Governor Lamont and legislature to make this a reality.”.

It has been revealed that seven other states also have down payment assistance programs for first responders. Florida, Nevada, Georgia and South Carolina provide flat amounts, ranging from $10,000 to $35,000. Texas, Maryland and Ohio’s programs are percentage-based and offer assistance ranging from 2.5 percent to 5 percent of the purchase price.

The terms of each program vary. Most states forgive the assistance after five to seven years, but Nevada requires homebuyers to repay the funds within 30 years. And like Connecticut, Ohio also offers a 0.25 percent mortgage rate discount.

Sources indicate that “Homeownership offers more than a place to live. It creates stability, strengthens connections to community and provides an opportunity to build wealth over time,” CHFA CEO and Executive Director Nandini Natarajan noted in an announcement. “Through First Responders’ Time to Own, we’re helping the people who answer the call for our communities take an vital step toward achieving their own homeownership goals.”.

First responders often fall through the cracks of housing assistance programs because they don’t earn enough to afford market-rate housing but earn too much to qualify for federal housing vouchers.

It has been revealed that inman explored this dilemma last September in a feature on workforce housing in resort towns like Jackson Hole, Vail and Tahoe. These towns can’t operate without first responders and other essential workers in the hospitality and retail sectors. However, rental and for-sale home prices have far outpaced what these workers earn, forcing them to commute long distances from more affordable towns or take on second and third jobs to survive.

It has been revealed that the solution for some of these towns has been investing in workforce housing, which caps prices for households that earn between 60 percent and 120 percent of their area’s AMI. Most workforce housing is rent-only, but some states are extending the programs to include for-sale properties.

Sources indicate that “I think the fact that workforce housing can be necessary or is a thing in the first place is really an indictment of the state of housing affordability in the country today,” Realtor.com Senior Economist Jake Krimmel said. “I think it’s key to ground any conversation about workforce and affordable housing in that reality. It’s a market failure and a policy failure that someone could be a doctor, a teacher or another kind of professional and cannot afford to pay the market rent or own a home outright.”.

Windermere Principal Economist Jeff Tucker noted workforce housing isn’t a panacea for affordability and works within an ecosystem of other housing and economic policies, such as upzoning, to create a more equitable market.

Tucker’s comments came a month after the Senate introduced the ROAD to Housing Act of 2025, and three months before the House introduced the Housing for the 21st Century Act. The bills were eventually combined into the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, which passed in June.

In a recent development, “A broad package of necessary reforms to make more housing construction possible in much of the country is a really notable component of a long-term solution to the housing affordability challenges we face,” Tucker mentioned. “Our current housing shortage took years to develop. So it’ll take years to build our way out of it.”.

  • Founded last year, the tech giant notes its clients collectively own or manage approximately 14 million acres worldwide — nearly the land area of West Virginia.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Lisa Stiffler on Nov 17, 2026 at 1:36 pmNovember 20, 2026 at 5:15 pm.

Seattle startup Aarden AI on Tuesday announced $8 million in newly introduced funding to grow its team and accelerate its work helping landowners evaluate potential uses for their properties and navigate deals with developers building data centers, clean energy projects, housing and other projects.

Founded last year, the tech giant notes its clients collectively own or manage approximately 14 million acres worldwide — nearly the land area of West Virginia. Aarden’s team said it has evaluated more than $500 million worth of land deals.

Recent findings suggest that “But land markets remain opaque and manual with far too much friction. Finding the right site, and building trust with the right partners swiftly, is more key than ever for our economy and our environment,” founder and CEO Danan Margason said in a statement.

The company combines data on hundreds of land attributes with historical market data and proprietary models to assess development suitability, valuation trends, ownership and community sentiment. Its tools and services also help developers identify sites and connect with landowners.

Aarden generates revenue through subscriptions to its technology, which includes AI-native data, models and investment tools, and through fees for services tied to specific deals or analyses.

According to recent reports, the new funding brings Aarden’s total investments to $12 million. Overture Ventures led the round, with participation from Madrona and Propeller Ventures. The startup previously raised $4 million in a round led by Planeteer in June 2025. The organization has 13 employees and intends to nearly double in size over the next 12 months.

Margason said he launched the business on the premise that while there have long been tools to support developers, landowners have been largely on their own to evaluate and optimize deals so they’re not taken advantage of or end up partnering with untrustworthy organizations.

One customer, timberland investment manager Resource Management Service, uses Aarden to evaluate whether tracts are best suited for continued timber production, conservation, solar development or other uses.

“Diligence that used to take months now produces investment-grade answers we can act on, and that is shaping how we manage value across our portfolio,” remarked Alex Hinson, president and CEO of Resource Management Service.

Other companies offering property research and analysis tools include Acres, which provides land data, valuations and due diligence tools, and Land id, which offers property insights and mapping tools.

Ben Eidelson, a partner at Stepchange Ventures, which participated in the startup’s first funding round, said the organization is already having an impact.

“We now have the capability to make smarter decisions about land, optimizing for the outcomes that matter from conservation to the local economy,” Eidelson said on LinkedIn.

#179266. The first price is the one nobody scores

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (752 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Housingwire ↗ Open Full Page

The first price is the one nobody scores

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (752 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housingwire

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that agents are more confident in the comparative market analysis than they have been in years.
  • Industry observers note that that is a fair reading of what a CMA does at the kitchen table.
  • The pressure on that single day is rising.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that agents are more confident in the comparative market analysis than they have been in years. In the 2026 Survey of Best Practices for CMAs and Listing Presentations, from Giant Steps Advisors in partnership with Lone Wolf Technologies, 89.6% of 2,165 real estate professionals said they expect CMAs to become more relevant, up from 67% in 2020. HousingWire reported on October 22 that the same respondents are ready to bring AI into the work, with 83.2% very or somewhat likely to use AI-assisted CMA tools, and suggested that the lasting value of the document may lie in explaining a price rather than producing one.

Industry observers note that that is a fair reading of what a CMA does at the kitchen table. It is also an incomplete one, because it judges the document on a single day. The CMA is scored on whether it persuades the seller to sign. Whether the price it argued for held up once buyers began making offers is a question the industry has no standard way to answer.

The pressure on that single day is rising. Roughly two-thirds of agents in the survey named pricing as the leading seller objection, up from 52.7% in 2020, and 33.6% said they had lost a listing because they and the seller could not agree on a price.

According to recent reports, at the same time, the survey found that 90.8% of respondents trust the MLS above any other source for comparable sales. Similar sources, increasingly similar tools and familiar formatting tend toward similar documents. When two agents arrive with reports that look alike, the seller is left choosing between two persuasions with nothing to say which one was right last time.

Sources indicate that the industry does keep a score, but it is the wrong one for this purpose. In the National Association of Realtors 2025 Profile of Home Buyers and Sellers, the final sale price was a median of 99% of the final listing price. The final listing price is the one left standing after any reductions. A home listed too high, cut twice and then sold sits in that figure looking almost exact, because the comparison begins after the correction has already been made. Reductions are not unusual.

Redfin reported that 21.2% of listings carried a price cut in the four weeks to November 1, 2026. The figure that tells a seller how well a CMA priced their home is the sale price compared with the first asking price, but that is not the figure the industry reports.

Even the first asking price is not always the number the CMA stood behind. HousingWire’s October report noted research showing that about half of agents put a listing price in their CMA and about half do not. Where the price is left off the page, the CMA can never be checked against the outcome, because it never committed to a number in the first place.

The gap widens when agents move. HousingWire reported in March that roughly 230,000 agents moved to a new brokerage in 2025, according to Courted’s 2025 State of Brokerage Recruiting and Retention Report. The sale prices stay in the closed files after an agent leaves. The judgment that set the first prices, and the sense of where that judgment ran high or low, leaves with the agent.

None of this is an argument against AI in the CMA, or against the CMA as a persuasion tool. Persuasion is part of the job, and a seller deserves an agent who can explain a price clearly and defend it under pressure. The difficulty is that the explanation is examined closely on the day it is given, while the outcome arrives months later and is measured against a different number.

Industry observers note that the industry has spent years making the valuation faster to produce and easier to present, and the survey suggests the next generation of tools will make it faster still. The question it has not yet asked is the one a seller would ask if they knew to: When this agent’s first prices met real buyers, how close did they come? Until someone asks it, every CMA will be judged on the day it persuades and never on the day the house sells.

Nikola Gojkovic is the founder of CMAflow and writes on residential valuation methodology.This column does not necessarily reflect the opinion of HousingWire’s editorial department and its owners. To contact the editor responsible for this piece: [email protected].

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that investors often turn to recommendations made by Wall Street analysts before making a Buy, Sell, or Hold decision about a stock. While media reports about rating changes by these brokerage-firm employed (or sell-side) analysts often affect a stock's price, do they really matter?

Before we discuss the reliability of brokerage recommendations and how to use them to your advantage, let's see what these Wall Street heavyweights think about MINISO Group Holding Limited Unsponsored ADR (MNSO).

In a recent development, MINISO Group Holding Limited at the moment has an average brokerage recommendation (ABR) of 2.00, on a scale of 1 to 5 (Strong Buy to Strong Sell), calculated based on the actual recommendations (Buy, Hold, Sell, etc.) made by 11 brokerage firms. An ABR of 2.00 indicates Buy.

Of the 11 recommendations that derive the current ABR, five are Strong Buy and one is Buy. Strong Buy and Buy respectively account for 45.5% and 9.1% of all recommendations.

Check price target & stock forecast for MINISO Group Holding Limited here>>>.

The ABR suggests buying MINISO Group Holding Limited, but making an investment decision solely on the basis of this information might not be a good idea. According to several studies, brokerage recommendations have little to no success guiding investors to choose stocks with the most potential for price appreciation.

Sources indicate that do you wonder why? As a result of the vested interest of brokerage firms in a stock they cover, their analysts tend to rate it with a strong positive bias. According to our research, brokerage firms assign five "Strong Buy" recommendations for every "Strong Sell" recommendation.

In other words, their interests aren't always aligned with retail investors, rarely indicating where the price of a stock could actually be heading. Therefore, the best use of this information could be validating your own research or an indicator that has proven to be highly successful in predicting a stock's price movement.

Zacks Rank, our proprietary stock rating tool with an impressive externally audited track record, categorizes stocks into five groups, ranging from Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) to Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell), and is an effective indicator of a stock's price performance in the near future. Therefore, using the ABR to validate the Zacks Rank could be an efficient way of making a profitable investment decision.

In spite of the fact that Zacks Rank and ABR both appear on a scale from 1 to 5, they are two completely different measures.

Sources indicate that the ABR is calculated solely based on brokerage recommendations and is typically displayed with decimals (example: 1.28). In contrast, the Zacks Rank is a quantitative model allowing investors to harness the power of earnings estimate revisions. It is displayed in whole numbers -- 1 to 5.

Sources indicate that it has been and continues to be the case that analysts employed by brokerage firms are overly optimistic with their recommendations. Because of their employers' vested interests, these analysts problem more favorable ratings than their research would support, misguiding investors far more often than helping them.

In contrast, the Zacks Rank is driven by earnings estimate revisions. And near-term stock price movements are strongly correlated with trends in earnings estimate revisions, according to empirical research.

In addition, the different Zacks Rank grades are applied proportionately to all stocks for which brokerage analysts provide current-year earnings estimates. In other words, this tool always maintains a balance among its five ranks.

Another key difference between the ABR and Zacks Rank is freshness. The ABR is not necessarily up-to-date when you look at it. But, since brokerage analysts keep revising their earnings estimates to account for a firm's changing business trends, and their actions get reflected in the Zacks Rank quickly enough, it is always timely in indicating future price movements.

Looking at the earnings estimate revisions for MINISO Group Holding Limited, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current year has remained unchanged over the past month at $1.28.

Analysts' steady views regarding the company's earnings prospects, as indicated by an unchanged consensus estimate, could be a legitimate reason for the stock to perform in line with the broader market in the near term.

In a recent development, the size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, has resulted in a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) for MINISO Group Holding Limited. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stocks here >>>>.

It may therefore be prudent to be a little cautious with the Buy-equivalent ABR for MINISO Group Holding Limited.

‘Do not search Amazon’: Meta’s Muse now shops elsewhere by default

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (640 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Geekwire

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Todd Bishop on Nov 17, 2026 at 2:36 pmNovember 18, 2026 at 9:45 am.
  • Two months after Amazon slammed the door on Muse, the AI agent has stopped knocking.
  • The shopping skill that guides Muse, Meta’s personal AI agent, now tells it to “leave out Amazon unless the user asks for it,” according to the instructions Muse provides when asked.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Todd Bishop on Nov 17, 2026 at 2:36 pmNovember 18, 2026 at 9:45 am.

Two months after Amazon slammed the door on Muse, the AI agent has stopped knocking.

The shopping skill that guides Muse, Meta’s personal AI agent, now tells it to “leave out Amazon unless the user asks for it,” according to the instructions Muse provides when asked. The instructions include a template brief for Muse’s browser that says, “Do not search Amazon.”.

The change was spotted last week by Juozas Kaziukenas, founder of the e-commerce research firm Marketplace Pulse, who asked Muse for the text of its shopping skill and compared it with the version from the day before. He posted the before-and-after on Friday. GeekWire asked Muse for its shopping skill and got the same language.

“Amazon blocked Muse, so now Muse blocked Amazon,” Kaziukenas wrote on X.

In a recent development, muse is also told not to name Amazon as a site to search in that browser brief, “even as an example,” unless the user asked for Amazon. The skill steers the agent to Walmart and Target for general goods, Best Buy for electronics, and Home Depot or Lowe’s for home improvement.

For Muse users, not much changes in practice. Amazon began blocking Muse in September, less than two weeks after Meta launched the agent, showing anyone who tried to shop through it a message saying continued access by an unauthorized AI agent violates Amazon’s Conditions of Use. Kaziukenas said any Amazon search would fail anyway because of the block.

What’s upcoming is that Meta appears to be going along with what Amazon asked for. When it began blocking Muse, Amazon said it had asked Meta to “remove Amazon from the experience.” Meta hadn’t said publicly how it would respond.

Meta didn’t respond to an inquiry about the change. An Amazon spokesperson stated the firm had nothing to share.

Amazon objected that Muse didn’t identify itself when it browsed the site and appeared to capture and store customer credentials. Meta has remarked Muse has no visibility into people’s passwords or payment methods. The standoff set off a broader debate over who owns the customer relationship when an AI agent does the buying.

It has been revealed that since then, both sides have kept moving. More than 10 million people in the U.S. and Canada signed up for Muse in its first six weeks, Forbes reported, and Walmart, Best Buy, Sephora and Wayfair are among the retailers working with Meta on it.

In a recent development, the business stakes are high for Amazon. It generated more than $68 billion in advertising revenue last year, including sponsored products that appear as people browse its pages — ads a shopper might never see if an outside agent does the searching. Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg has said Muse will take a small cut of the transactions it handles.

Industry observers note that amazon has fought this battle before, suing Perplexity last November over the shopping agent in its Comet browser. It’s now pressing that case in part on the same Conditions of Use it cited in blocking Muse.

Industry observers note that on Amazon’s earnings call last month, CEO Andy Jassy said outside shopping agents aren’t making a meaningful dent in Amazon’s advertising business. “Few customers are doing much shopping this way yet,” he said, adding that the experience still isn’t great or more convenient than going straight to a retailer.

Jassy remarked Amazon expects to work with “horizontal agents,” general-purpose assistants like Muse, but believes its own Alexa for Shopping will be the main agent people use to shop Amazon. Amazon launched Alexa for Shopping in May, combining its Rufus shopping chatbot with the Alexa+ assistant.

It has since started letting some customers text Alexa to shop, much as people do with Muse.

Recent findings suggest that leading cryptocurrency exchange Coinbase has unveiled the official listing of artificial intelligence (AI) giant Anthropic (ANT) shares on its trading platform in the U.S. and U.K.

The listing comes as Anthropic, the company behind the popular AI chatbot Claude, officially made its much-anticipated stock market debut on Thursday, Nov. 19, with its shares seeing massive volatility.

In a recent development, as per the latest X post from Coinbase, the exchange announced the availability of Anthropic (ANT) shares for eligible people in the U.S. and U.K.

Industry observers note that it's important to mention that ANT isn't a cryptocurrency but a traditional stock. Coinbase's support for ANT shares shows the company's efforts to expand its offerings beyond crypto into traditional financial markets.

Industry observers note that anthropic has set a upcoming historic precedent, having successfully raised about $81 billion in its initial public offering (IPO). This is the biggest IPO ever.

The artificial intelligence manufacturer sold 980 million shares at $83 per share, significantly higher than its previously announced price range of $70 to $78.

This brought Anthropic's initial valuation to about $1.5 trillion, making the tech giant one of the most valuable publicly listed firms in the world right from the get-go.

But as Anthropic shares started trading on the Nasdaq exchange, the ANT ticker saw massive volatility.

As per Reuters, Anthropic shares began trading at $111.50. This represented an enormous 34% premium over the IPO price.

At the initial peak, Anthropic's market cap exceeded $2 trillion, surpassing SpaceX's valuation when it debuted on the market in June.

It has been revealed that anthropic shares slipped to around $95 as the stock gave back a significant chunk of its gains. This was partly due to investors looking to book their profits.

Nonetheless, Anthropic shares were still trading comfortably above their $83 IPO price.

The volatility surrounding Anthropic's stock market debut signals increasing doubts about the AI investment craze.

The listing of Anthropic shares is just one of Coinbase's moves to enter traditional financial markets.

Instead of just providing cryptocurrency trading, the exchange is looking to become a platform for multiple asset classes.

Recent findings suggest that interestingly, Coinbase had already listed Anthropic pre-IPO perpetual futures for eligible non-U.S. owners on Nov. 18.

The perpetual futures were derivative contracts that allowed traders to speculate on Anthropic's valuation before its shares officially started trading on Nasdaq.

Industry observers note that with the latest listing, eligible Coinbase users in the U.S. and U.K. can now trade the publicly listed Anthropic shares.

Anthropic's blockbuster debut comes as financial markets have been rocked by recent volatility, with tech stocks and crypto facing selling pressure.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A secure lender platform cannot protect a buyer who acts on fraudulent instructions received through another participant’s email.
  • It has been revealed that an analysis of 668 reported wire fraud events spanning a decade identified approximately $123.8 million in reported financial exposure and approximately $11.5 million in documented losses.
  • We examine what those reported events suggest about trust, why participants outside the funding process matter and how organizations can strengthen verification across business relationships.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A secure lender platform cannot protect a buyer who acts on fraudulent instructions received through another participant’s email. An agent’s familiar name can make a message persuasive even when the agent has no authority to move funds. For mortgage, title and real estate professionals, those connections deserve a place in the fraud prevention conversation.

It has been revealed that an analysis of 668 reported wire fraud events spanning a decade identified approximately $123.8 million in reported financial exposure and approximately $11.5 million in documented losses. The findings point to a practical concern for everyone involved in a transaction: protecting an organization’s systems addresses only part of the risk.

We examine what those reported events suggest about trust, why participants outside the funding process matter and how organizations can strengthen verification across business relationships.

Industry observers note that approximately 79% of reported events, 78% of reported exposure and 80% of documented losses were associated with participants operating outside the title company’s direct control. Of the 668 events reviewed, 57 resulted in documented financial loss.

Sources indicate that these figures describe the reported events analyzed. They should not be treated as an industry-wide loss rate or as proof that risk has shifted over time. Association with an external participant also does not, by itself, establish where an account was compromised or who was responsible for a loss.

Industry observers note that the concentration nevertheless raises an important business question. If a fraudulent request gains credibility through a customer, agent, attorney or other participant, will the next organization in the transaction recognize and verify it before someone acts?

Recent findings suggest that the traditional approach to fraud prevention focuses on authority. Organizations identify who can move money, approve payments, authorize disbursements or initiate wire transfers and then build controls around those functions.

In a recent development, that remains necessary. But an attacker may also seek access to someone who influences the person sending money. Transaction details, familiar correspondence and knowledge of an approaching closing can help a fraudulent message appear credible without access to the lender’s or settlement provider’s systems.

It has been revealed that residential real estate transactions are particularly susceptible to this type of manipulation because they depend on trust at every stage of the process. Buyers trust agents. Sellers trust agents. Consumers trust lenders. All parties trust the professionals coordinating the transaction. Most participants are communicating with several unfamiliar parties while simultaneously navigating a process that is complex, time-sensitive and financially significant.

For a consumer, a request that appears to come from a familiar professional may feel like part of that process. Fraud prevention must help customers distinguish a trusted relationship from a verified instruction.

It has been revealed that mortgage lenders, title companies, brokerages and independent professionals operate with different resources and security practices. A participant may use an email account without the monitoring or administrative oversight available within a larger organization. That difference creates a coordination challenge, not a reason to assign blame.

An agent may understand the buyer’s timeline and concerns better than anyone else. A loan officer may be the person the buyer calls when a request seems confusing. A settlement professional may be the first to see that expected funds have not arrived. Each has an opportunity to reinforce safe behavior at a different point.

Industry observers note that the strongest internal controls lose some of their value when customers receive inconsistent guidance about who will provide instructions, how to verify them or where to report a suspicious message. Those expectations should be established before the closing deadline makes every request feel urgent.

In a recent development, lenders, agents and settlement providers should explain their respective roles early. Identify who will provide wiring instructions and how the customer should independently confirm them. Reinforce that guidance as closing approaches rather than relying on a single warning in an email signature.

According to recent reports, before acting on wire instructions, confirm them directly with the appropriate party using a previously established, independently verified phone number. Do not rely on a phone number supplied in the message you are trying to verify.

Replying to the same email thread is not sufficient because an attacker may control the account. Question unexpected changes and escalate unusual requests through your organization’s established procedures before money moves.

Industry observers note that awareness efforts should reach loan officers, agents, transaction coordinators and customer-facing staff, as well as employees authorized to disburse funds. Training should explain how a routine message or introduction can influence a consumer’s decision to trust instructions.

Strong email security, multifactor authentication, employee training, monitoring and incident response capabilities remain essential. Broader coordination adds to those protections. It does not reduce the need to secure accounts and systems within each business.

Organizations should identify whom to contact when instructions appear suspicious or expected funds do not arrive. Staff should know how to pause their part of the transaction, involve the appropriate settlement and lending contacts and activate established fraud response procedures. Customers need a clear way to raise concerns without feeling that they are creating an inconvenience.

The difference between reported exposure and documented loss in the analysis is substantial. It is consistent with the value of verification and intervention, but the totals alone do not establish which controls prevented losses or explain every event’s outcome.

It has been revealed that organizations can learn more by reviewing their own near misses. Where did a questionable request enter the process? Who recognized it? Was the customer able to reach the right person? Did a partner’s instructions conflict with the organization’s guidance? Those questions turn an avoided loss into an opportunity to improve the next transaction.

Wire fraud prevention is a shared responsibility across mortgage lending, title and settlement services and real estate. A participant does not need authority over funds to influence where those funds go.

Sources indicate that the practical response is to make verification part of the customer experience from the beginning. Clear roles, consistent guidance and accessible escalation help people act safely when a familiar name or urgent request makes fraud difficult to recognize.

Successful fraud prevention frequently occurs because someone slows down, asks an additional question and verifies information before money moves.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, at the same time, Binance's first post-hack reserve snapshot indicates its biggest assets covered with buffers as small as 2.7 ETH and $6 of USDT.
  • Some of the money stolen from Binance has started going back to Binance.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

On-chain data shows the attacker behind the $6.3 billion Binance theft depositing about $4 million into three Binance deposit addresses.

According to recent reports, at the same time, Binance's first post-hack reserve snapshot indicates its biggest assets covered with buffers as small as 2.7 ETH and $6 of USDT. Binance's full zero-knowledge proof of those figures is due by Tuesday.

Some of the money stolen from Binance has started going back to Binance.

Recent findings suggest that blockchain intelligence firm Arkham has flagged the entity it tracks as "Binance Hacker" depositing about $4 million into three Binance deposit addresses. Arkham states those addresses "likely represent nested service(s)." These are third-party exchanges that use Binance for liquidity and custody, giving their own customers deposit addresses that sit on Binance's infrastructure.

If Arkham is right, the hacker isn't depositing into an ordinary Binance account. The money would be going to smaller platforms that operate through Binance. Exchanges have long known this is a weak point for stolen funds moving into normal trading. Either way, Binance is now receiving stolen funds at its own deposit addresses while it works to show customers it has replaced what was taken.

According to recent reports, the FBI has attributed the October 29 theft to North Korea. The deposits come at a sensitive moment. Binance has just published its first reserve snapshot since the hack and has promised a full cryptographic proof of it by Tuesday.

$4 million is a small slice of a theft worth about $6.3 billion, but it matters for two reasons.

It shows how the laundering works. Nested services are a common way into the regulated financial system. A third-party platform that relies on Binance for custody may run weaker identity checks on its own users. Funds deposited there can be swapped and withdrawn without the hacker ever opening a Binance account.

Binance can act on it. Binance can't freeze bitcoin and ether sitting in wallets nobody controls, and it doesn't control the stablecoins that issuers like Tether and Circle have frozen. Deposits that land at its own addresses are different: they are on Binance's platform, so Binance can freeze them itself. One of the first tests of how Binance handles the money still in the hacker's hands is whether it freezes these funds and identifies the services that own the addresses.

While the hacker's funds move, Binance has been rebuilding its reserves. Its proof-of-reserves page now indicates:.

The first page covers Binance's six largest assets. Customer balances are what customers hold. Reserves are on-chain wallet balances, including assets held with outside custodians.

The second page has four more assets, and two of them stand out:.

Industry observers note that why USD1 and RLUSD matter: these are two of the stablecoins whose issuers froze stolen funds after the attack. World Liberty Financial froze $27 million of USD1, and Ripple began freezing RLUSD the same night. Both now show reserves above what Binance owes customers.

Assets with outside custodians: part of several reserves sits with outside custodians rather than in Binance's own exchange wallets:.

Asset | Held with third-party custodians.

In a recent development, the striking part isn't that the ratios reach 100%. It's how closely they stop there.

Compared with October's report: Binance's previous monthly report, published in early October before the hack, indicated BTC at 100.35% and USDT at 103.88%. ETH was already at exactly 100.00%. After the theft:.

According to recent reports, not every asset is that tight. USDC, ZEC and BNB carry buffers of 1.3% to 6%. The thinnest buffers are in BTC, ETH, USDT and SOL, which are among the assets the attacker took in the largest amounts.

According to recent reports, how Binance says it got here: the pattern fits Binance's account of replacing the stolen assets in stages. It reported 80% replaced on Friday, 90% on Saturday and 95% on Sunday. The remaining 5% is in less-liquid tokens it is still buying. The money came from:.

Binance confirmed taking 7,499 BTC from SAFU and has pledged to refill the fund to about $1 billion.

What the snapshot can't show: it was taken a little over a day after the theft, once the rebuild was under way. It shows the balance sheet after the replacement, not how large the gap was on October 29.

Binance says the full proof takes 40 to 50 hours to compute. Its latest update says it will be ready "by Tuesday, 2026-11-03 (UTC)." The system is open source, in Binance's zkmerkle-proof-of-solvency repository.

What the proof guarantees, according to the project's circuit design document:.

Recent findings suggest that the design also guards against a "dummy user attack" identified by Ethereum Foundation researcher Enrico Bottazzi. In that attack, fake accounts holding cheap tokens are used to offset debts in major assets.

What it doesn't prove: the reserve side. The project's verifier config describes the totals as information "published by CEX, it represents CEX's liability." The reserve figures are checked a different way, against the wallet addresses Binance publishes through the page's "Download All Address" option.

It has been revealed that what customers can do: each user can get a Merkle proof for their account and check it against the published root. They can use the verifier code in Binance's repository rather than Binance's own interface. That doesn't prove Binance is solvent, but it confirms the user's balance was counted.

Recent findings suggest that binance has rebuilt its reserves to 100% across its ten largest assets, but on several of them the buffer is only a few coins. Meanwhile, stolen funds are reaching its deposit addresses through platforms that run on its infrastructure. Tuesday's proof can confirm customer balances. It can't show how Binance handles the stolen money arriving at its own door.

Latest AI-powered customer acquisition system combines website development, lead generation and AI-powered follow-up to help med spas attract prospects, respond to inquiries and schedule consultations.

PASADENA, Calif., Nov. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Attracting potential clients is important for any medical spa, but turning that interest into appointments can be a challenge. Phone calls may come in while staff members are assisting clients, website inquiries may arrive after business hours, and prospective clients may lose interest when they do not receive a timely response.

In a recent development, to help med spas address these challenges, Pasadena-based digital marketing and web development agency Cybertegic has developed an advanced AI-powered customer acquisition system that combines website development, lead generation, customer management software, and AI customer service agents. The system is designed to help manage the process from a potential client's first interaction to follow-up and appointment scheduling.

The need for a more responsive booking process is reflected in industry research. A 2025 survey of more than 1,100 U.S. med spa clients found that 79% of regular clients had skipped booking because it was too difficult to reach someone or make an appointment online.[1] This highlights how missed communication and booking difficulties can affect a practice's ability to attract and retain clients.

How Customer Service AI Helps Med Spas Manage Fresh Leads.

Med spa owners and front-desk teams often handle several responsibilities at once. They may be assisting clients, answering phone calls, responding to social media messages, checking appointment availability, and managing daily operations.

When multiple inquiries arrive at the same time, some prospective clients may have to wait for a response. Others may never receive a follow-up, particularly when they contact the practice outside regular business hours.

Cybertegic's system uses AI agents to manage these interactions and reduce repetitive manual communication.

Depending on the practice's setup, AI agents can:.

By handling routine first responses and follow-up activities, AI agents can help practices stay engaged with prospective clients without requiring staff to personally manage every interaction.

AI agents can provide general information based on the practice's approved content, while qualified professionals handle treatment recommendations, medical questions, and decisions about treatment suitability.

Turning Missed Opportunities Into Managed Follow-Ups.

One common challenge for med spas is reaching potential clients who show interest but are not immediately ready to book.

According to recent reports, for example, someone may inquire about Botox, laser treatments, or skin rejuvenation services but want more information before scheduling. Another person may submit a website form and become busy before responding to the practice's follow-up. Some may call after hours and move on if nobody answers.

Without an organized follow-up process, these inquiries can easily get lost.

Cybertegic's AI-powered system helps address these situations by keeping prospect information and communication organized through customer relationship management (CRM) software. This functions as a shared record of inquiries, contact details, conversations, and follow-up activity.

Industry observers note that AI agents can then help maintain communication through configured follow-up messages, answer additional questions, and guide interested prospects toward a consultation. Staff members can also review the conversation history and take over when a more personal response is needed.

This approach helps reduce dependence on scattered messages, individual inboxes, spreadsheets, and manual reminders.

Connecting Website Development, Lead Generation and AI Follow-Up.

AI follow-up is only one part of the customer acquisition process. Med spas also need an effective online presence to attract people who are searching for aesthetic treatments and nearby providers.

Cybertegic's system brings three vital areas of customer acquisition together:.

Website development: Provides a constantly updated, professional online presence where prospective clients can explore treatments, learn about the practice, and submit inquiries.

Lead generation: Attracts potential clients through targeted digital marketing and gives interested customers quick, easy access to book an appointment.

Customer management and AI agents: Organizes incoming inquiries, assists with initial conversations, automates follow-ups, and helps guide prospective clients toward appointments.

Together, these capabilities create a clearer lead-management process. Rather than treating website visitors, phone inquiries, follow-up messages, and appointment scheduling as separate activities, med spas can manage them through a connected customer acquisition system.

In a recent development, "Med spa owners shouldn't have to choose between taking care of their existing clients and keeping up with new inquiries," said Johnny Chou, CEO of Cybertegic. "Our goal is to use AI agents to help with the repetitive work of responding to questions, collecting information, and following up with prospective clients. This gives med spa teams a more organized way to manage new opportunities while keeping personal service at the center of the client experience.".

Supporting Med Spa Growth in Pasadena and Southern California.

For med spas in Pasadena and throughout California, attracting local clients involves more than appearing in search results or running digital advertising campaigns. Practices also need a dependable way to handle the interest those marketing efforts generate.

Cybertegic's approach addresses both sides of the process by combining digital marketing, website development, and AI-powered customer communication. The system is designed to help med spas improve inquiry management, maintain consistent follow-ups, and reduce the administrative work involved in moving prospective clients toward appointments.

By allowing AI agents to assist with routine communication while staff members focus on consultations, treatment services, and client relationships, med spas can create a more manageable customer acquisition process as their businesses grow.

More information about Cybertegic's digital marketing and technology services is available at www.cybertegic.com.

  • Jeff Bezos says Nvidia should look inside the company for its next CEO, and he doesn’t give an outsider much chance of success.
  • “If you don’t bring Jensen back, I would not hire an outsider.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Todd Bishop on Nov 17, 2026 at 5:05 pmNovember 17, 2026 at 5:07 pm.

Jeff Bezos says Nvidia should look inside the company for its next CEO, and he doesn’t give an outsider much chance of success. The Amazon founder, now co-CEO of AI engineering startup Prometheus, made the comments Tuesday at Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World event.

“If you don’t bring Jensen back, I would not hire an outsider. Nvidia is too complicated,” Bezos noted. Outside CEOs at complex companies, he added, “have a vanishingly small chance of succeeding,” and he would consider hiring one “a last resort.”.

Industry observers note that nvidia’s board says it has no intends to bring Huang back. Harvey Jones, the longtime director named the company’s first board chair last week, opened Nvidia’s earnings call Tuesday afternoon by saying the board “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.”.

Jones noted the search will include internal and external candidates, and that the board wants a permanent CEO in place swiftly but won’t rush the pick.

Recent findings suggest that huang, the Nvidia co-founder and CEO for 33 years, had posted a statement on X that morning offering to return. He said he had “made serious mistakes” in his personal life and would cooperate with the board’s independent investigation.

“If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the manufacturer, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO,” he wrote.

Nvidia announced Huang’s resignation last Thursday, a day after the New York Times reported that he’d had an affair with an Nvidia executive who reported to him. Days earlier, he admitted to an affair with a woman who U.S. officials believe was recruited by Chinese intelligence, according to the Wall Street Journal.

CFO Colette Kress, who spent 13 years at Microsoft earlier in her career, is serving as interim CEO.

Two major Nvidia investors, Altimeter Capital’s Brad Gerstner and Atreides Management’s Gavin Baker, asked the board to leave open “the potential return of Jensen Huang.” Analyst Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives wrote in a note Sunday that talk of a Huang comeback is “ridiculous.”.

Industry observers note that the Amazon precedent (not really): Bezos has been through a founder handoff of his own. He turned over the Amazon CEO job in 2021 to Andy Jassy, a longtime insider who built AWS. When Semafor raised the comparison, Bezos called it a poor one, saying there has never been a more carefully planned transition.

According to recent reports, he said he didn’t know enough about what happened in Nvidia’s board meetings to say whether Huang should return. But he called Huang a remarkable founder who deserves “admiration and respect no matter what.”.

Recent findings suggest that huang himself stated in a Bloomberg interview recorded Oct. 14 that he hoped his successor was already inside the company.

Recent findings suggest that the Nvidia comments came in a wide-ranging interview. Bezos also mentioned Blue Origin is using Prometheus tools on two projects, called President Trump by far the most communicative of the presidents he has worked with, and said Robert Pattinson was the clear choice to play the next James Bond after screen tests of five finalists.

In a recent development, business as usual, officially: Nvidia reported third-quarter revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year earlier, including $107.6 billion from its data center business. On the call, it raised its forecast for next fiscal year’s revenue growth to about 75%, from 70%.

Kress didn’t mention Huang by name on the call. Asked about the leadership transition, she said customers, suppliers and employees remain behind the company, calling it “business as usual.” She ended the call with a short pep talk that finished, “We’ve got this.”.

In case the board was wondering about one outsider in particular, Bezos is spoken for. During the Semafor interview, he described running Prometheus as “Nirvana.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Data infrastructure startup Zipher Technologies Ltd.
  • According to recent reports, founded in 2024, Zipher takes over the day-to-day running of enterprise data workloads, from resource allocation to framework selection and scheduling.
  • Recent findings suggest that the organization already manages production workloads for a number of Fortune 500 enterprises in sectors including financial services, travel, consumer packaged goods and energy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 08:00 EST / NOVEMBER 24 2026.

Data infrastructure startup Zipher Technologies Ltd. today revealed that it has raised $53 million in funding for a platform where artificial intelligence agents, not data engineers, decide how enterprise data workloads run.

According to recent reports, founded in 2024, Zipher takes over the day-to-day running of enterprise data workloads, from resource allocation to framework selection and scheduling. Customers set performance targets and budgets, leaving the rest to the tech giant’s agents. The platform runs on Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud, with support for data tools including Databricks Workflows, Apache Airflow, dbt and Azure Data Factory.

Recent findings suggest that the organization already manages production workloads for a number of Fortune 500 enterprises in sectors including financial services, travel, consumer packaged goods and energy. Those customers see cost-efficiency gains of 40% to 60%, it states, with service-level agreement adherence improving by as much as 80%.

It has been revealed that among them is Hertz Global Holdings Inc. Gaurav Rastogi, senior director of enterprise data analytics and BI platforms at Hertz, said the car rental tech giant has seen compute cost reductions of 25% to 40% depending on the workload while “supporting consistent performance through seasonal peaks.”.

In a recent development, behind the numbers is an argument that AI agents have changed the way enterprises use their data platforms, with anyone in an organization now able to spin up a data workload in seconds. Zipher’s agents learn each of those workloads, dependencies included, and then pick the engine each one runs on based on capacity and load at the time.

It has been revealed that the agents can go as far as rewriting a workload’s framework, code and syntax. Dan Coster, Zipher’s co-founder and chief executive, said that as agents create more workloads, the infrastructure needs to “make its own decisions.”.

According to recent reports, the funding is intended to support research and development along with go-to-market work. Zipher plans to build out its U.S. enterprise sales team and expand across Latin America, Asia-Pacific and the Europe, Middle East and Africa region.

Sources indicate that zipher was founded by Coster and Chief Technology Officer Yoav Gill Ben Ephraim, both alumni of Unit 8200, the Israel Defense Forces’ intelligence technology unit. Ben Ephraim previously served as director of data platform at Payoneer Global Inc. and held a senior data role at Microsoft Corp. The company is headquartered in Latest York, with offices in Tel Aviv.

Industry observers note that the $53 million, which covers both Zipher’s seed and Series A rounds, came from TLV Partners, Maor Investments and Glilot Capital Partners. Angel investors and advisers include Dremio Corp. co-founder Tomer Shiran, Monte Carlo AI Inc. co-founders Barr Moses and Lior Gavish and Cribl Inc. co-founder Clint Sharp.

According to TLV Partners Managing Partner Shahar Tzafrir, enterprises in an agentic world need a platform that decides where and how each workload runs. The Zipher team, he added, has “proven it in production with Fortune 500 customers who keep expanding their use of the platform.”.

Sources indicate that the recommendations of Wall Street analysts are often relied on by investors when deciding whether to buy, sell, or hold a stock. Media reports about these brokerage-firm-employed (or sell-side) analysts changing their ratings often affect a stock's price. Do they really matter, though?

Let's take a look at what these Wall Street heavyweights have to say about Star Bulk Carriers (SBLK) before we discuss the reliability of brokerage recommendations and how to use them to your advantage.

According to recent reports, star Bulk Carriers presently has an average brokerage recommendation (ABR) of 1.29, on a scale of 1 to 5 (Strong Buy to Strong Sell), calculated based on the actual recommendations (Buy, Hold, Sell, etc.) made by seven brokerage firms. An ABR of 1.29 approximates between Strong Buy and Buy.

Of the seven recommendations that derive the current ABR, six are Strong Buy, representing 85.7% of all recommendations.

Check price target & stock forecast for Star Bulk Carriers here>>>.

Sources indicate that the ABR suggests buying Star Bulk Carriers, but making an investment decision solely on the basis of this information might not be a good idea. According to several studies, brokerage recommendations have little to no success guiding investors to choose stocks with the most potential for price appreciation.

According to recent reports, are you wondering why? The vested interest of brokerage firms in a stock they cover often results in a strong positive bias of their analysts in rating it. Our research highlights that for every "Strong Sell" recommendation, brokerage firms assign five "Strong Buy" recommendations.

Recent findings suggest that in other words, their interests aren't always aligned with retail investors, rarely indicating where the price of a stock could actually be heading. Therefore, the best use of this information could be validating your own research or an indicator that has proven to be highly successful in predicting a stock's price movement.

With an impressive externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool, the Zacks Rank, which classifies stocks into five groups, ranging from Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) to Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell), is a reliable indicator of a stock's near-term price performance. So, validating the Zacks Rank with ABR could go a long way in making a profitable investment decision.

In spite of the fact that Zacks Rank and ABR both appear on a scale from 1 to 5, they are two completely different measures.

It has been revealed that broker recommendations are the sole basis for calculating the ABR, which is typically displayed in decimals (such as 1.28). The Zacks Rank, on the other hand, is a quantitative model designed to harness the power of earnings estimate revisions. It is displayed in whole numbers -- 1 to 5.

Recent findings suggest that it has been and continues to be the case that analysts employed by brokerage firms are overly optimistic with their recommendations. Because of their employers' vested interests, these analysts glitch more favorable ratings than their research would support, misguiding investors far more often than helping them.

In contrast, the Zacks Rank is driven by earnings estimate revisions. And near-term stock price movements are strongly correlated with trends in earnings estimate revisions, according to empirical research.

Furthermore, the different grades of the Zacks Rank are applied proportionately across all stocks for which brokerage analysts provide earnings estimates for the current year. In other words, at all times, this tool maintains a balance among the five ranks it assigns.

According to recent reports, another key difference between the ABR and Zacks Rank is freshness. The ABR is not necessarily up-to-date when you look at it. But, since brokerage analysts keep revising their earnings estimates to account for a organization's changing business trends, and their actions get reflected in the Zacks Rank swiftly enough, it is always timely in indicating future price movements.

Looking at the earnings estimate revisions for Star Bulk Carriers, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current year has remained unchanged over the past month at $4.53.

Analysts' steady views regarding the tech giant's earnings prospects, as indicated by an unchanged consensus estimate, could be a legitimate reason for the stock to perform in line with the broader market in the near term.

Industry observers note that the size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, has resulted in a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) for Star Bulk Carriers. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stocks here >>>>.

It may therefore be prudent to be a little cautious with the Buy-equivalent ABR for Star Bulk Carriers.

Breaking: Homebuilder underwriting works better when you name the bet

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (904 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housingwire

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • [In the fifth of seven excerpts from his newly introduced book, ‘Less Wrong, More Right,’ Scott Cox argues that underwriting should identify one key assumption, then test supply, pricing power and buyer willingness with evidence.].
  • In underwriting, the money question is narrower and harder than it looks: what, specifically, is this deal depending on?
  • It has been revealed that I once spent several weeks going back and forth with a builder about a deal he was presenting.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

[In the fifth of seven excerpts from his newly introduced book, ‘Less Wrong, More Right,’ Scott Cox argues that underwriting should identify one key assumption, then test supply, pricing power and buyer willingness with evidence.].

In underwriting, the money question is narrower and harder than it looks: what, specifically, is this deal depending on? Almost everything else in underwriting is a way of finding that one thing and then testing it.

It has been revealed that I once spent several weeks going back and forth with a builder about a deal he was presenting. He was being sloppy about his comp analysis – overstating his market position, understating the competitive set. I knew it, and I kept pushing on it. He kept defending it. We went in circles.

Recent findings suggest that after a few weeks of this, he finally lost patience. “Come on, Scott,” he mentioned. “Even if you’re right about the comps, four years from now there will be half the projects in this submarket that there are today.”.

It has been revealed that I stopped. That’s an entirely different argument, I told him. And a completely different bet. Why didn’t you say so? Where’s the pipeline analysis? Let’s look at it.

Recent findings suggest that he was right, as it turned out. The supply argument was sound. And I had spent weeks pressing him on a number that – even if I’d won the argument – wasn’t the one that mattered. He hadn’t named his real bet. I hadn’t asked what it was. We were both analyzing the wrong thing.

According to recent reports, that failure – his and mine – is the most common and most expensive mistake in underwriting. Not a specific bad assumption about costs, or an aggressive absorption rate, or a pricing premium that didn’t materialize. Those are the visible problems. The underlying one is simpler: not knowing what the deal is actually depending on, or not communicating it.

According to recent reports, every project depends on one thing being true – sometimes two, rarely three – that, if wrong, makes the deal fail to perform regardless of how well everything else turns out. It’s a premium spot with no comps – how hard can the price be pushed? It’s a rough neighborhood – with great access and it looks to be transitioning – do people take the same risk to buy as to rent here? Before there is a there there, how fast can we sell in our latest MPC? Will the bond market keep buying bonds early in the life of our deal? How much competition will we have five years from now? One of these is carrying most of the weight.

Good underwriting means identifying that assumption first, then allocating effort accordingly. If the real bet is that this corridor will have half the supply in five years due to land-use and infrastructure constraints, you should be spending far more time on a detailed pipeline analysis – project by project, timing by timing – than on the precision of your current comp spread. The comp analysis matters, but it’s not the question. The question is whether the supply thesis holds.

If the real bet is that buyers will pay a premium for your product, the work is different. Have you comped the house in exhaustive detail – not category-level, but feature by feature? What do buyer-preference surveys actually show about the specific features you’re banking on? Is there evidence from comparable markets that buyers pay more for those features, in that amount? Do you know how to sell it effectively? Generic confidence in your product is not the same thing as a tested value proposition. If you can’t answer those questions specifically, you’re not underwriting the real bet – you’re hoping it works out.

Recent findings suggest that the problem is that most pro formas don’t reveal what they’re depending on. Effort gets distributed roughly evenly across the model – costs, absorption, pricing, schedule – with each assumption tweaked modestly in the optimistic direction. The result looks rigorous because it covers everything. But covering everything is not the same as testing the thing that matters. When several mildly aggressive assumptions sit next to each other in a spreadsheet, no one can see that one of them is critical and uncertain and the rest are secondary – which is not to say unimportant.

When I walk builders through this kind of underwriting, I sometimes hear “if we did all that and were hyper realistic as you suggest, we’d never buy anything.” I could not disagree more, and this attitude contains within it two related mistakes.

One, why would having very realistic underwriting cost you deals? The only thing costing you deals is a return threshold higher than the market will allow. Is it better to have aggressive underwriting and unrealistic hurdles? Is self-deception really necessary? Two, and this is notable, aggressive underwriting and unrealistic hurdles can cause you to make poor choices on deals, and deal risk.

Industry observers note that as an example, if you consistently underestimate your development schedules and costs, you have a bias against finished-lot deals – because you incorrectly think you get a sufficient premium for self-development. Realism is the path to better choices about what to do, not a hindrance to doing anything.

Adapted from Less Wrong, More Right (Part IV: Underwriting), available on Amazon.
