#179252. What music sells a house? Agents say it’s not about genre

📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1522 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Inman ↗ Open Full Page

What music sells a house? Agents say it’s not about genre

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1522 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Inman

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Agents explain how they pick open house music, the one rule most follow and why none can prove it works.
  • Recent findings suggest that ask real estate agents what soundtrack sells a house, and you’ll get two answers.
  • Inman asked agents and brokers from Manhattan to Breckenridge, Colorado, and they described the music they play at showings and open houses and how they match it to the property.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Taylor Swift, classical or silence? Agents explain how they pick open house music, the one rule most follow and why none can prove it works.

Recent findings suggest that ask real estate agents what soundtrack sells a house, and you’ll get two answers. One is a carefully curated playlist, while the other is silence.

Inman asked agents and brokers from Manhattan to Breckenridge, Colorado, and they described the music they play at showings and open houses and how they match it to the property.

It has been revealed that none could point to hard numbers showing a playlist moved a home faster or for more money. What they did offer was a clear set of rules from the agents who use music, and an equally firm argument from those who won’t touch it.

Industry observers note that ben Jacobs, co-founder of the Chestler Jacobs Team at Douglas Elliman in Upcoming York City, thinks music raises more questions than it answers. He said he’s not a fan of playing music during showings.

“Buyers may wonder if the agent is trying to mask something, whether it’s street noise, construction nearby, sounds within the building or even a noisy appliance,” Jacobs told Inman. “You want buyers to experience the home as it actually is, without anything distracting from their ability to evaluate the space.”.

His co-founder, Jessica Chestler, remarked music has its place. That place is just not a private showing.

“Music can be wonderful for setting a mood at a cocktail party, listing launch or special event, but during a showing, I think there’s something to be remarked for letting the property speak for itself,” Chestler said.

Megan Sullivan works at the same brokerage, and she uses music for the very reason Jacobs avoids it. Sullivan sells large estate homes across Fairfield and Westchester counties out of Douglas Elliman’s Greenwich, Connecticut, office. Some of those homes sit within earshot of things a seller can’t fix.

It has been revealed that “I actually do like incorporating music into certain showings, particularly when a property is impacted by outside noise from planes, trains or automobiles,” Sullivan mentioned. “Thoughtfully selected background music can help create a more welcoming atmosphere and soften those distractions, allowing buyers to focus on the overall experience of the home. I think it’s very property-specific.”.

Jeffrey Hensel is a broker associate with North Coast Financial, a California hard money lender that funds fix-and-flip and probate deals. He looks at it from the investor side.

It has been revealed that “Dead silence can amplify every creak, clank, and drip in an otherwise quiet home,” he said. “Background music masks these sounds and provides some white noise to help set a calm mood.”.

According to recent reports, agents in the pro-music camp mostly aren’t trying to cover anything up. They simply want buyers to stay longer.

Sandra Daniels of Harry Norman, Realtors | Forbes Global Properties serves the East Cobb and Marietta area outside Atlanta. She’s at the moment listing a $3.9 million estate in The River Club in Suwanee, Georgia.

For those showings, she rotates light classical piano, The Macarons Project and a Spotify playlist called “Nora Ephron + Nancy Meyers Dinner Party.”.

“Put a buyer in a home with a glass of Champagne or a cup of coffee and the right music playing, and that cozy, inviting atmosphere encourages people to stay, relax and feel at home,” Daniels told Inman.

Daniels also has a low-tech trick for vacant listings she expects to sell in the first week. She bought an old-school CD player and a few classical CDs. She leaves it on repeat through the first weekend of showings and stops by each evening to turn off the lights and music and lock up.

Natalia Bassova, founder and CEO of Resort Real Estate in Breckenridge, Colorado, saw the same effect at a luxury mountain listing. The home looked great, she said, but it showed cold.

It has been revealed that “By adding some background instrumental music, it gave the buyers more time to spend in the home. They spent more time in the kitchen and great room areas,” Bassova said. “The property didn’t change, but the atmosphere did.”.

According to recent reports, for mountain and luxury homes, Bassova plays acoustic and piano music, including Ludovico Einaudi and The Piano Guys. For condos and upcoming construction, she switches to soft contemporary instrumentals.

Agents who play music disagree on genre, but almost all agree on one thing: avoid lyrics.

“If the buyer begins to think about the music, then it is having a negative impact,” Bassova noted. Her never-play list covers anything with strong lyrics, politics, swearing or heavy bass.

Recent findings suggest that andrea Seeney is a global real estate advisor with Atlanta Fine Homes Sotheby’s International Realty and a trained opera singer and classical pianist. She compared lyrics to a seller’s personal effects.

“Acoustic performances are best because they set a tone and allow the buyer to fill in the blanks with their own thoughts,” Seeney said.

Recent findings suggest that she leans toward jazz and usually plays Spotify’s Coffee House radio or its Ella Fitzgerald playlist. She says music works on buyers through memory: a song can take someone back to a time and place they enjoyed, “and that memory then reflects positively on the home.”.

Recent findings suggest that hensel takes the lyrics rule a step further, to genre itself. If an agent plays hip-hop or country for a buyer who doesn’t listen to it, he states, that signals an assumption about who the buyer is. That can create friction neither side notices. His pick is quiet cocktail-lounge jazz like Miles Davis or Bill Evans, at a steady tempo and volume.

Recent findings suggest that he also cited retail research by psychological scientists Adrian North and Lorraine Sheridan of Curtin University and Charles Areni of Macquarie University. It found that shoppers who heard classical music rated merchandise as higher quality and were willing to spend more.

Some agents ignore the rulebook completely.

Rachel Kilmer, an agent with ReeceNichols Real Estate in Kansas City, Missouri, plays Taylor Swift at nearly every open house. She swaps in country for more rural listings.

“In Kansas City, she’s a conversation starter,” Kilmer said. “People come in, and it’s, ‘Are you a Swiftie?’ ‘No, but I love the Chiefs!’ It really helps loosen up the conversation.”.

She added, “I’m the one sitting there listening to it for two hours!”.

Monica Shea, a broker with KW Aspire in Colorado Springs, Colorado, builds whole open houses around a theme, and the music follows.

In a recent development, she played the Eras Tour set list at a Taylor Swift–themed open house and the Frozen soundtrack at a hot cocoa bar event. A Halloween open house got not-too-spooky Halloween music. For regular showings, she has sellers put on a YouTube channel with seasonal background music and scenery.

Shea’s never-play list puts her directly at odds with a few other agents: smooth jazz. Shea says she never plays “anything that sounds like the Weather Channel.”.

Marcel Finkelstein of Team BlackStar at eXp Realty hosts open houses every Sunday across Monmouth County, New Jersey. He sees music as more of an icebreaker than a staging tool.

His Apple Music rotation includes lounge instrumentals, vocal-free dance-pop and Bon Entendeur. It also has Afro house from DJ Alex Niyazov and the warm trumpet and sax of Fausto Papetti and Paul Mauriat.

He uses the same approach whether the listing is a $600,000 two-bedroom condo in Manalapan or a $2 million six-bedroom in Colts Neck.

“I want the atmosphere to feel calm, comfortable and welcoming, rather than like a sales presentation,” Finkelstein remarked.

Finkelstein added that his Instagram followers also know how much he loves music.

It has been revealed that “Every week, I share fresh songs and incorporate music into my stories and posts about homes,” he stated. “It’s a personal interest that carries through into how I present properties.”.

In a recent development, on setup, agents who play music give similar advice. Keep the volume low enough that buyers can ask questions and the agent can hear their feedback. Use one good speaker rather than several.

Recent findings suggest that bassova puts hers in the middle of the home, and Seeney puts a small Bluetooth speaker in the kitchen. When sellers have a Sonos system, Daniels connects to it from her MacBook or iPad. Otherwise, she brings her own Bose speaker.

Kilmer runs her music from an iPad instead of her phone. “That way, incoming calls and texts don’t interrupt the music,” she remarked.

As for proof, none of the agents Inman spoke with track music as a performance metric. Bassova said she gets buyer feedback that certain homes feel relaxing, but nothing tied to days on market or offers.

So the evidence is anecdotal, and the playlists don’t agree. Agents can’t even settle on jazz. Both camps share one goal: the buyer should notice the home, not the soundtrack.

As Bassova said, “If the buyer begins to think about the music, then it is having a negative impact.”.

Washington’s biggest economic threat may be the conviction that it’s already doing everything right.

That was the pointed warning from a Technology Alliance panel Tuesday, where a conversation about talent and economic growth became a challenge to the state’s self-image as an innovation leader.

“You said spicy, right?” Rob Ogburn asked, taking up the invitation to speak bluntly.

“The economy is very strong. The economy is not competitive at all,” said Ogburn, executive director of Business and Community Services at Central Washington University.

While tech giants such as Microsoft and Amazon and sectors including aerospace and biotech are powering today’s economy, that doesn’t mean Washington is positioned to win tomorrow’s investment, develop its workforce or spread opportunity beyond its major employment centers.

Amelia Ransom, former vice president at Smartsheet and past Nordstrom leader, questioned the definition of success, arguing that future growth also depends on investing in people and businesses outside the corporate spotlight.

In a recent development, “Who do we mean when we say winning? Who is it? Who are we talking about, and who are we leaving out?” Ransom said, later adding, “We have to close the daylight between who we say we are and who we actually are.”.

The panel was held in downtown Seattle and moderated by Jolenta Coleman-Bush, director of Microsoft Philanthropies. It also included Rachel Smith, president of Washington Roundtable.

Rather than simply calling for more talent and innovation, panelists examined how Washington develops the people already here, whose perspectives inform its decisions and how effectively its institutions and stakeholders work together.

It has been revealed that unification is essential. U.S. Sen. Maria Cantwell, D-Wash., led the passage of the CHIPS and Science Act in 2022 to bolster semiconductor manufacturing and innovation in AI and energy. But her home state has received just 0.3% of the funding awarded so far, Ogburn said.

He argued that other states and regions were more effective at uniting to make their case for investment, showing their collective resources and the problems they could solve.

“We showed up and said, ‘We’re competing with our neighbor, and we’re better than them.’ No investor is going to look at that and say you’re going to make the best use of my money,” Ogburn said.

Cultivate talent, don’t just recruit it. Ransom compared workforce development to a restaurant, a grocery store and a garden: recruiting ready-made workers, developing the talent already here and growing the long-term pipeline.

According to recent reports, “The middle is where we probably need to spend more time, which is at the grocery store, which means you’ve got to learn to cook,” she said. Her point: Invest in Washington’s existing employees, students, and businesses.

Smith wants employers to identify the high-wage, high-skill jobs they need filled so educators and businesses can coordinate strategies to prepare workers for those roles.

It has been revealed that fill essential information gaps. Panelists called for a clearer picture of community skills and barriers to opportunity, more voices to challenge prevailing assumptions, and closer examination of how regulations affect businesses.

Sources indicate that “We’ve gotten in this war of the rankings where everybody’s like, “No, we’re the best. No, we’re the worst.” And we we’ve got to stop doing that,” Smith remarked.

The region needs data-backed insights into the reasons behind the rankings, she said. Smith pointed to the recently formed Economic Development Council and its planned statewide strategy as a step toward a more coordinated approach.

Whether these efforts succeed, Ogburn mentioned, should be judged by the communities themselves.

“And then, if you want to measure success, go back to those communities and ask them if they feel successful,” he said. “Do they have agency and self-determination?”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chicago-based mortgage lender Rate on Tuesday unveiled the launch of EquitySimple, a fixed-rate home equity loan designed to help homeowners consolidate debt, finance home improvements and cover major expenses.

The product gives borrowers a lump-sum payment with a fixed interest rate and predictable monthly payments and is structured as a second mortgage, allowing homeowners to tap their equity without refinancing their existing first mortgage or giving up a lower interest rate.

The launch comes as consumers face rising debt burdens and homeowners hold substantial equity. U.S. credit card balances reached a record $1.29 trillion in the third quarter of 2026, while average credit card interest rates exceed 21%, according to Federal Reserve data.

Recent findings suggest that rate noted that 68% of its fixed-rate home equity loans funded between Jan. 1 and Nov. 19 carried interest rates below 8%, with a median rate of 7.88%. The company cautioned that historical rates do not guarantee current pricing, which varies based on borrower and property characteristics.

“Too many homeowners are paying credit card interest rates above 20% while sitting on significant equity they’ve worked hard to build,” Victor Ciardelli, founder and CEO of Rate, said in a statement. “We’re committed to helping our members build the good life around home, health and wealth, but financial stress can get in the way.”.

Sources indicate that equitySimple uses a flat fee that covers lender and third-party costs, including appraisal and title expenses. Borrowers are responsible for applicable state and local taxes, as well as prepaid interest. Rate said it discloses the loan’s rate, payment and fees before borrowers commit, and it does not add charges at closing.

The firm is also offering a digital application process, with the option for borrowers to work directly with a loan officer or move between the two channels. Rate remarked loan officers can help borrowers evaluate whether using home equity to consolidate unsecured debt is appropriate, given that the home serves as collateral for the upcoming loan.

According to recent reports, eligible borrowers may be able to close in as little as 14 days, compared with an industry average of about 40 days, according to Rate. The company clarified that the timeline is not guaranteed and depends on property, credit and documentation requirements.

It has been revealed that “We’ve spent 26 years helping people get into their homes. EquitySimple is about helping them use the value they’ve built in those homes to find relief,” stated Adam Boyd, president of consumer lending at Rate.

EquitySimple is available in 49 states and Washington, D.C. The product is not at the moment available in Texas.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

DraftKings (DKNG) is a Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell) that runs one of the largest online sportsbook and iGaming platforms in the U.S.

The boom that followed sports betting legalization has faded, and growth is slowing just as the company spends heavily to fight a new threat from prediction markets like Kalshi. After a wide third-quarter miss and a sharp guidance cut, analysts are lowering their estimates and the stock is trading close to 2026 lows.

Based in Boston, DraftKings (DKNG) got its start in daily fantasy sports in 2012. It has since expanded into online sports betting, iGaming (online casino), lottery services and, most recently, its Predictions platform, which offers event contracts.

DraftKings grew rapidly as state after state legalized online sports betting, creating a steady stream of new markets and customers. Much of that initial expansion opportunity has now played out, shifting the focus to gaining market share in existing states and generating growth from newer products.

According to recent reports, draftKings has a market cap of $9 billion and trades at 33 times forward earnings. It has Zacks Style Scores of “F” for Value, “B” for Growth and “D” for Momentum.

According to recent reports, on November 6, DraftKings reported a third-quarter loss of 0.53persharebelowtheZacksConsensusEstimate-0.21. Revenue of $1.33 billion missed the $1.38 billion consensus, and the adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $316.9 million from $126.5 million a year ago.

The organization also cut its fiscal 2026 outlook and revenue guidance fell to a range of $6.35 billion to $6.55 billion, below the $6.68 billion consensus. Adjusted EBITDA guidance was cut to $175 million to $275 million from a prior $700 million to $900 million.

Sources indicate that most of that EBITDA cut reflects spending on Predictions, but the core business slipped too. Core EBITDA guidance was lowered to about $900 million at the midpoint from roughly $1 billion. Management blamed customer-friendly sports outcomes for about 60% of that and heavier iGaming promotions for most of the rest.

The core numbers show a maturing business. Monthly unique payers rose 13% to 4.1 million, but average revenue per payer grew only about 3% to $109. Like-for-like handle grew 12%. These are respectable numbers, but they’re not the kind of growth that justified the stock’s valuation during the legalization boom.

It has been revealed that prediction markets are the new wild card, with platforms like Kalshi offering sports event contracts that operate outside the state-by-state sportsbook framework. This puts them in direct competition for the same bettors.

Sources indicate that draftKings has responded by building its own Predictions business, and it isn’t cheap. The tech giant expects to put $650 million to $700 million of adjusted EBITDA into Predictions this year and another $250 million to $350 million in fiscal 2027. The business has grown fast, with more than 1.6 million customers so far this year, but it isn’t expected to turn EBITDA positive until fiscal 2028.

The regulatory backdrop adds another layer of risk. Management’s own underwriting allows for the possibility that sports contracts are shut down in July 2028, and it remarked investment levels remain sensitive to court developments. If prediction markets win in court, the competition intensifies. If they lose, much of that spending loses its purpose.

Analyst sentiment has turned decisively negative, with no upward estimate revisions over the past 30 days. Analysts have made two downward revisions to fiscal 2026 estimates and three to fiscal 2027.

It has been revealed that the fiscal 2026 Zacks Consensus Estimate has fallen 46% over the past month, from $1.00 to $0.54. That now implies an 18% decline from last year's $0.66.

Industry observers note that near-term expectations have weakened as well. The fourth-quarter consensus has dropped 39% in the past 30 days, from $0.75 to $0.46.

Fiscal 2027 estimates have fallen from $1.75 to $1.43. While that still implies a substantial rebound, the Most Accurate Estimate of $1.33 sits below consensus, suggesting further downward revisions could be ahead.

The stock is down 50% on the year and trending towards its 2022 lows. The moving averages are likely candidates for resistance until the fundamental story changes.

The 50-day is at $20.65 and the 200-day is $23.50 and should be used as selling points for those trying to play a bounce. Longer there is a clear road lower for the stock, with the next support level around the $11 level.

Recent findings suggest that the easy growth from upcoming state releases is behind DraftKings. Core results are being hit by bad sports outcomes and heavy promotions, while a costly push into prediction markets has wiped out most of this year’s EBITDA. With estimates heading lower and the Kalshi risk hanging over the industry, investors may want to stay away until the picture clears up.

Jeff Bezos has a space firm, a newspaper, an AI startup that’s raised $14.5 billion and, apparently, a seat in the room when Amazon decides who gets a license to kill.

Speaking Tuesday at Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World event, the Amazon founder mentioned he was “heavily involved” in the casting of Robert Pattinson as the next James Bond, a pick Amazon MGM Studios confirmed Monday.

According to recent reports, amazon got a 50% stake in the Bond franchise when it acquired MGM for $8.5 billion in 2022, then took creative control last year in a joint venture with longtime producers Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson.

Bezos mentioned a large initial pool of would-be Bonds was narrowed to five finalists, who then did “real old-fashioned screen tests”: three scenes apiece, in full costume on real sets with other actors.

The other finalists were Nicholas Hoult, Jack Lowden, Josh O’Connor and Callum Turner, according to The Fresh York Times, which reported that the tests took place in London in late October.

Bezos said the decision-makers got together Friday and spent a couple of hours reviewing the screen tests before settling on Pattinson.

Sources indicate that “By the time we got to this list of five, they were all amazing,” Bezos mentioned. “But there was something special about Rob Pattinson and his performances.” He said the group, including director Denis Villeneuve, reached a quick consensus. It was “kind of immediately undebated.”.

Bezos admitted that the group was initially “slightly biased” against Pattinson because he’s already so famous.

“We sort of thought, you know, maybe we should have somebody a little more unknown,” he mentioned. “But in the screen tests, it was so obvious he is James Bond.”.

The trader's latest post on X highlights a pattern he has found throughout Bitcoin's price history: previous bull runs have always ended with devastating market corrections.

"Every bull market phase in the history of BTC has ended with at least a 75% correction of the prior parabolic bull trend," Brandt's X post reads.

Continuing his warning, Brandt raised an alarming question: "Is this what is happening with Bitcoin?".

According to recent reports, the trading veteran has not put a number on the possible crash. But his words point toward the possibility that the current drop in Bitcoin might be part of a larger correction and not just a temporary dip.

A look at Bitcoin's historical crashes could paint a scary picture.

Bitcoin has a history of sharp corrections following major bull runs.

For example, the crypto asset dropped by around 84% from its December 2017 high to its December 2018 low. Another example of such a deep price correction can be found in the 2022 bear market, when BTC saw a drop of around 77% from its November 2021 all-time high.

These historic crashes have shown the extreme losses that Bitcoin investors have faced during such market corrections.

At the time of writing on Nov. 20, Bitcoin is presently trading at around $62,000, which is almost 51% below its October 2025 all-time high.

If it were to undergo a 75% price correction from its all-time high, then it would drop to around $31,550.

But it's worth mentioning that Brandt referred to a correction of the prior parabolic bull trend, which may not be the same as a 75% correction from the peak.

Interestingly enough, this is not the first time the trader has warned about an even darker future for Bitcoin's price.

Earlier, on Nov. 15, Brandt shared a weekly BTC chart showing a potential head-and-shoulders formation, a technical pattern that usually signals a bearish reversal.

According to Brandt, if the pattern is confirmed, there's a chance that Bitcoin could never revisit its previous all-time high in his lifetime.

LAS VEGAS, Nov. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Wolfbox, a leader in automotive electronics and off-road gear, previewed a slew of new and soon-to-launch automotive accessories at the 2026 SEMA Show, held Nov. 3â6 at the Las Vegas Convention Center.

Recent findings suggest that at the North Hall, Booth #10339, Wolfbox featured the trail-ready FlexPilot configurable four-channel mirror dash cam system, K9 Pro three-channel dash cam with full-color nighttime recording and NomadPixel 5 programmable off-road LED pods. Other showcase items included portable tire inflators, jump starters, cordless vehicle-care tools and aftermarket pickup accessories.

"Wolfbox began with dash cams, and our customers have pushed us to solve more of what they face on and off the road," said Wolfbox product manager Jason Lo.

"At SEMA, we brought that full range together, from camera systems to trail lighting, air tools and truck bed gear, so builders and buyers could see how it all works in vehicles.".

FlexPilot: Camera Coverage Where Off-roaders/Overlanders/RVs Need It.

Drivers of different vehicles have different needs when it comes to dash cams. Off-road drivers may need a close view of terrain near the wheels or underbody, while RV and trailer owners need coverage along the sides and behind the vehicle.

It has been revealed that built for trucks, off-road vehicles and RVs, the FlexPilot dash cam's QuadFlexâ¢ system lets owners tailor camera coverage and screen layouts to their vehicles and how they use them. The system supports up to four cameras selected from five camera types, with mounting options at the bumper or mirror, on the tailgate, beneath the chassis or behind a trailer.

Sources indicate that flexPilot also includes a 12-inch, 1,500-nit adaptive display that automatically adjusts its brightness to ambient light. Select between single, dual, triple or quad views and which camera feeds appear.

Front and rear cameras use Sony STARVIS 2 sensors and record in 4K, while exterior, side and interior options record in 1080p.

It has been revealed that flexPilot rolled out on Kickstarter on Nov. 17. Interested customers can back the campaign at: https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/wolfbox/wolfbox-flexpilot-multi-angle-monitoring-with-dash-cam?ref=b3g3ju.

K9 Pro: Excelling at Full-Color Recording, Even at Night.

For rideshare drivers and families, the newly introduced Wolfbox K9 Pro combines road recording with full-color cabin footage after dark for ultimate security. This dash cam records 4K video at the front, 2.5K inside the cabin and 2.5K at the rear. All three channels record simultaneously, bringing road and passenger-compartment footage together in one system.

It has been revealed that the front camera uses a Sony STARVIS 2 IMX678 sensor, with HDR on both the front and rear cameras. The cabin camera has ColorAliveâ¢ night vision to capture interior activity in full color after dark. The rear camera carries an IP69K rating for exterior use.

NomadPixel 5: Adding Personality to Trail Lighting.

Recent findings suggest that nomadPixel 5 combines off-road illumination with an app-controlled pixel display in a pair of five-inch, IP69K-rated LED pods. Owners can display custom text, graphics and animations, from a vehicle name to a club logo. Each light can be configured separately.

The LED pods deliver strong trail illumination at 8,850 raw lumens per light, or 17,700 per pair, with a rated beam distance of 275 meters at 1 lux per light.

Practical Tools for the Trail and Garage.

For off-roaders and overlanders, the HyperFlow 60D portable off-road air compressor helps drivers air tires back up after trail use. Its twin-cylinder design delivers rated airflow of 5.1 CFM at 40 PSI, with a maximum pressure of 150 PSI and support for tires up to 40 inches.

Wolfbox also unveiled the MegaVolt 32 Air, which combines a jump starter rated at 6,000 peak amps, an air compressor, a power bank and an LED emergency light in one unit.

Recent findings suggest that for vehicle care, Wolfbox showcased two cordless electric air blowers. The MegaFlow 500 Pro is a heavy-duty cordless blower with stepless speed control and a swappable battery, designed for drying vehicles and clearing dust and debris after off-road trips.

Meanwhile, the more compact MegaFlow 200 Pro air duster pairs adjustable speed control and a built-in display with a one-press turbo button for maximum airflow, while its swappable battery supports long cleaning sessions.

Recent findings suggest that wolfbox also offers a solution for pickup owners who need more efficient access to their truck. The Retractable Bed Step with aluminum anti-slip treads has a 330-pound capacity and bolts onto compatible full-size and heavy-duty pickups without drilling.

Up Close with Wolfbox in the Silverado.

According to recent reports, at the Wolfbox booth, visitors were able to climb into a Wolfbox-branded 2025 Chevrolet Silverado 4WD to experience the in-vehicle products and watch camera feeds in real time. A camera-placement voting wall invited attendees to mark their preferred camera mounting positions and discuss the views they would find most useful.

An air duster-focused tabletop football game gave visitors a chance to try Wolfbox's cordless electric air dusters, using airflow to move a foam ball toward an opponent's goal. Nearby, a water-immersion display highlighted how well off-road and pixel lights operate while submerged.

Industry observers note that since 2019, Wolfbox has provided more than 2.5 million drivers across 94 countries with reliable dash cam technology and automotive solutions. Winner of awards from SEMA and TWICE, the brand has also expanded its driving ecosystem with the new GEARS line, bringing rugged bed covers, power steps, and high-output lighting to off-road enthusiasts.

For more information, visit wolfbox.com and gears.wolfbox.com.

Congratulations, you’ve made it to Friday again this week. But before you head out for the weekend, we’re bringing you a quick catch-up on the biggest headlines and the most helpful how-tos for your business. So, Take 5 and peruse our top editor picks for this week and why they matter to your business.

Sources indicate that homeownership is slipping further out of reach for young Americans, according to the National Association of Realtors’ 2026 Profile of Home Buyers and Sellers. The report, released on Thursday, revealed that the share of first-time homebuyers rose 1 percent year over year to 22 percent. Despite the small gain, first-time buyer activity remains near historic lows (21 percent) and 18 percentage points below pre-2008 trends (40 percent). Same as last year, the median age of a first-time homebuyer was 40 — roughly a decade older than the typical median age in the 1980s.

According to recent reports, why it matters: This annual report gives you a pulse on national real estate trends and how you might want to pivot your strategies. For example, as noted above, the median age of the first-time homebuyer is 40, and the share of single women homeowners has risen to 20 percent. A longer nurture campaign might be in order (ahem, see below), and if you’re not already marketing toward single women, perhaps you should. Read the full report for more.

EXTRA: The buyer who can’t close for a year is your best asset in 2026.

Recent findings suggest that AI has been the topic of conversation for the past couple of years. And there’s a lot of talk. So how do you suss through the noise and find what works for your business? Jimmy Burgess has created a no-nonsense list of seven AI tools that are actually worth your time.

Why it matters: Burgess shares not only his top tools but also how to use them. These tools will help you turn prompts into better questions, find the questions your future clients are asking, remember the details that matter, evaluate your AI search visibility, turn one video into multiple pieces of content, make video editing easier and use AI as a strategist rather than a writing assistant. Don’t feel overwhelmed. You don’t have to use all of them at once.

Recent findings suggest that krystopher Benyamein recently sold a property in San Pedro where his team hosted nine open houses, mailed 500 postcards, ran digital advertising and created a video that generated more than 1.5 million organic views. They found a buyer and opened escrow, but shortly before closing, that buyer backed out, and they had to start again.

They eventually found another buyer and successfully closed, but when they shared the case study on Instagram, they didn’t lead with the sale price or how much marketing they’d done. They opened with, “Imagine finally selling your house. Then the buyer backs out right before closing.”.

That opening puts the reader in the seller’s position. Most homeowners can imagine how frustrating that experience would be, and it naturally creates curiosity about what happened next. From there, they explained how they responded, got the property back in front of buyers and ultimately closed.

Sources indicate that why it matters: In today’s market, there are many stories of buyers backing out of deals. This approach allows you to create content that keeps you top of mind, show sellers exactly how you work and reach a wider audience. Benyamein demonstrates you how to do it and shares a FREE Canva template to help get the job done.

VA loans often get passed over for conventional loans. Inman’s Nick Pipitone spoke with Fathom Realty’s Lindsey Schmidt, an Army veteran who served in Iraq, about why VA financing still carries a stigma among sellers and listing agents, how she gets around it and why VA assumptions remain one of the most misunderstood tools in the market.

Recent findings suggest that why it matters: Military members often have to move. Understanding and busting myths about VA loans can help you get ahead of objections before making an offer, which will help you get more deals across the finish line and get more service members into homes.

Compass has been busy, creating and formalizing policy around employees in association leadership positions and how Compass brokerage agents cooperate on private listings.

The company unveiled Thursday that it is filing 15 federal antitrust lawsuits against MLSs across eight states, accusing the organizations of illegally restricting how agents can publicly market homes outside their systems. Compass alleges that the MLSs unlawfully fine agents for publicly marketing listings outside the MLS, with penalties it notes can reach $15,000.

Why it matters: Compass International Holdings is at the moment in litigation with 16 total MLSs across 18 federal lawsuits. Not only is this big news that’s making waves throughout the industry, but its ripple effects could impact your MLS’s rules, if they haven’t already.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Lisa Stiffler on Nov 17, 2026 at 11:00 pmNovember 18, 2026 at 7:47 am.
  • Sila, a startup producing next-generation battery materials, announced a long-term customer agreement with Panasonic Energy Corporation of North America potentially worth more than $1 billion.
  • Sources indicate that panasonic, a battery supplier to Tesla, will buy Sila’s Titan Silicon anode material for its U.S.-made battery cells.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Lisa Stiffler on Nov 17, 2026 at 11:00 pmNovember 18, 2026 at 7:47 am.

Sila, a startup producing next-generation battery materials, announced a long-term customer agreement with Panasonic Energy Corporation of North America potentially worth more than $1 billion. To meet demand from Panasonic and other buyers, the company plans to expand its plant in Moses Lake, Wash., supporting roughly 500 additional manufacturing and construction jobs over the coming years.

Sources indicate that panasonic, a battery supplier to Tesla, will buy Sila’s Titan Silicon anode material for its U.S.-made battery cells. The silicon-carbon composite can replace some or all of the graphite in lithium-ion battery anodes to improve performance.

Sila began operations at its Moses Lake plant last year and has about 100 full-time employees at the site. The facility is still scaling up production, with initial capacity designed to supply batteries totaling about 2 gigawatt-hours — enough for roughly 20,000 to 50,000 EVs, depending on how the material is used.

The expansion will increase that capacity to tens of gigawatt-hours, stated Gene Berdichevsky, Sila’s co-founder and CEO.

It has been revealed that “This is a really crucial blueprint for reindustrializing the U.S.,” he stated. “We have to take new technology and leapfrog China, not just copy what they’ve done over the last 20 years.”.

Sources indicate that while the U.S. has expanded battery manufacturing, it still depends heavily on overseas suppliers for core materials and technologies, Berdichevsky mentioned. Sila aims to strengthen that domestic supply chain with higher-performing components.

Batteries support industries central to energy independence and national security. They power EVs, consumer devices, drones, robotics and hardware deployed in space, and provide backup electricity for data centers.

It has been revealed that berdichevsky stated Titan Silicon can help a battery store 20%–40% more energy in the same space, cut recharging time roughly in half and deliver more power than a battery using a conventional graphite anode. The anode itself is also much lighter and smaller.

According to recent reports, in August, Sila received a conditional federal loan commitment of up to $1.4 billion through the Pentagon’s Office of Strategic Capital to expand domestic battery technology manufacturing. The tech giant must meet financial, legal, technical and other requirements before the loan can be finalized.

Recent findings suggest that the startup previously received a $100 million grant during the Biden administration under a similar initiative to increase U.S. energy independence. Those funds helped build its plant in Washington.

Recent findings suggest that the company has also raised $1.6 billion from private investors, including a $300 million round announced in July. The 15-year-old company is valued at $2.27 billion, according to PitchBook.

Seattle-area startup Group14 also makes a silicon-carbon anode material. It operates a smaller-scale manufacturing facility at its Woodinville, Wash., headquarters and produces commercial-scale volumes at a plant in South Korea.

According to recent reports, group14 has partially completed its Moses Lake manufacturing site but repeatedly delayed the start of production. It now targets mid-2027 to bring the first of two production units online, with no firm completion date for the second. It recently announced plans for a factory in Spain.

Growth is key to bringing down costs and making Sila’s technology competitive in mass-market batteries, Berdichevsky said.

“This is really the beginning of chapter three for our organization’s history,” he stated.

It has been revealed that the first two chapters were inventing the technology and moving from grams to tons of production, he added. This phase is about reaching the mass market. Sila aims to begin manufacturing at the expanded facility in 2028, with output increasing over time.

According to recent reports, “None of this is easy,” Berdichevsky said. “It’s not the inventing technology; it’s the manufacturing of it that’s really really hard, and we’re going to try to more than 10x the scale from what we’ve already done.”.

  • Recent findings suggest that verra was founded last year by Chief Executive Kashyap Nathan (pictured, right), who previously worked as a researcher at OpenAI Group PBC and Palantir Technologies Inc., and Christopher Farrington (left), a former software engineer at Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu Ltd.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 08:00 EST / NOVEMBER 24 2026.

Verra, an artificial intelligence startup building the institutional memory layer for consulting firms, mentioned today it has raised $5 million in seed funding to help those companies overcome their amnesia and make their decades of knowledge accessible to every employee.

In a recent development, today’s round was led by Kearny Jackson and saw participation from Andreessen Horowitz’s a16z Speedrun, Petra and a number of strategic investors. It comes just seven months after Verra, officially known as Lighthouse Software Technologies Inc., introduced its platform.

Recent findings suggest that verra was founded last year by Chief Executive Kashyap Nathan (pictured, right), who previously worked as a researcher at OpenAI Group PBC and Palantir Technologies Inc., and Christopher Farrington (left), a former software engineer at Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu Ltd. In an interview, Nathan explained that he and Farrington had seen firsthand how well-paid consultants would struggle with fresh customer engagements, wasting hours of time researching to surface institutional knowledge that their firm already possessed.

Sources indicate that “Consulting firms sit on decades of proposals, models and reports, and almost none of it is usable by the people who need it next,” Nathan stated. “We built the layer that makes that knowledge usable, and we built it to run inside the firm’s own cloud, because no consulting firm is going to send client work to a shared service.”.

Industry observers note that verra makes consulting firms’ institutional knowledge accessible through an artificial intelligence-native memory layer that indexes their past deliverables and distills their previous methodologies into reusable skills for autonomous agents. Then, those agents can utilize those skills to get started in tools such as Microsoft Word, PowerPoint and Excel, and generate a highly detailed draft for new client engagements in ten hours or less.

Nathan noted that’s a significant improvement. At most consulting firms, it typically takes about 80 hours to get that first draft ready. “The traditional approach involves a SharePoint search box and a junior analyst with a week to spare,” he explained. “The AI-native version of that is a chat tool that answers a question from a few retrieved pages and leaves the consultant to rewrite the output. But both start from a blank page.”.

Verra is also much more efficient, Nathan said. Whereas traditional chatbots can generate text snippets, Verra creates its sourced deliverables directly inside Office files that will be organized alongside the client brief.

According to recent reports, “Verra starts from the firm. It indexes everything the firm has produced, distills how each practice does its work, and then lets a consultant point at a new situation and get to most of a finished deliverable in Excel or PowerPoint, before the human analyst starts writing a line,” Nathan stated. “Every claim links to the page or cell it came from. The firm’s engineers and ours then build the specific workflows a team wants.”.

The architecture of Verra’s agents is important, too. The firm built them to run inside client’s clouds after looking at three realities of the professional services business. Consulting firms cannot allow their client’s data to leave their own environments, they will not trust an answer that can’t be verified, and AI will not be used if it forces them to drop the tools and systems they’re already using.

Industry observers note that it’s this approach that has been the secret to Verra’s promising early adoption. Its agents are already being used by two major global consulting firms in Berkeley Research Group and The Keystone Group. In the case of the former, more than 90% of its consultants are using Verra daily, and have generated more than 105,000 files since August while replacing the Tableau platform with a natural-language Snowflake interface. Berkeley calculates that Verra’s platform has helped the company to save around 215,000 analyst hours annually.

Recent findings suggest that “Verra hands our teams finished, sourced first drafts on engagements that used to start from a blank page,” remarked Berkeley’s global managing director of AI solutions, Raghav Vadlamani. “It has changed how quickly we move for clients.”.

Moving forward, Nathan wants to integrate Verra’s AI agents even deeper with the consulting firms it serves, so they can learn how the entire company works and improve its overall efficiency rather than just focusing on one engagement at a time. He also sees an opportunity to move into adjacent sectors such as investment research and accounting. He wants to give customers’ engineers a way to build on Verra’s platform too.

In a recent development, kearny Jackson Partner Sriram Krishnan remarked he used to work in the consulting industry himself and that he’s all too familiar with the rinse-and-repeat process that accompanies each upcoming client engagement. “What stood out to us was how quickly Verra became critical to the firms using it,” he said. “Their consultants adopt it, use it and demand more of it. It’s becoming the memory and operating layer for how consulting firms work.”.

Noted economist and longtime Bitcoin critic Peter Schiff has sounded the alarm about an upcoming financial apocalypse, warning that the crisis could be worse than the historic 2008 market crash.

On Nov. 20, Peter Schiff shared a series of troubling X posts warning about the potential for significant losses in the U.S. stock market, real estate, and cryptocurrencies amid escalating financial system stress.

The economist shared a video with a very alarming headline: "The Next Crash Will Be Worse Than 2008.".

In one of his most recent posts on X, Schiff argued that the recent gold price downtrend might signal a grim outlook for other key asset classes.

It has been revealed that "It's probably a bad sign that gold is falling this much. It probably means that the stock and real estate markets are going to fall even more in percentage terms," Schiff cautioned.

Recent findings suggest that according to Peter Schiff, gold's recent price behavior could be signaling deflation. As a result, this might lead to a more severe financial crisis.

However, Peter Schiff is convinced that the Federal Reserve will step in to prevent this financial apocalypse.

"Gold is signaling deflation. But asset deflation would bust the government and the banking system, so the Fed will pivot to avoid it," the economist explained.

Simply put, Schiff assumes that the Federal Reserve will pivot and introduce monetary stimulus to prevent a financial meltdown.

It has been revealed that in another startling prediction, the economist warned that the U.S. stock market might wipe out all its gains since President Donald Trump took office.

"There's a good chance that the U.S. stock market is about to give back all the gains since Trump took office," the economist predicted.

He also warned that there might be a recession. As a result, Trump will likely point to Democrats and their wins in the recent midterm elections as the reason for this recession.

Interestingly enough, Peter Schiff's bearish outlook also applies to Bitcoin (BTC), which has already suffered significant losses amid the overall market crash.

According to recent reports, on Nov. 18, Peter Schiff shared several alarming market indicators. According to his data, the Nasdaq has dropped 12.25%. AI infrastructure tech giant CoreWeave has plummeted 64%.

Bitcoin, on the other hand, has plunged 33.5% from its 2026 peak.

Additionally, the economist noted that the U.S. housing market index had dropped to 25, its lowest level since 2012. This demonstrates that the economic complications go well beyond AI stocks.

"Still think this is just about AI?" he asked.

  • The data for September reveals that home prices rose 2.1% year-over-year, unchanged from a month prior, resulting in an index reading of 308.06.
  • “Nominal home prices remain resilient, but inflation is once again widening the gap between nominal and real housing returns,” Rebecca Kaufman, the associate director of commodities at S&P Dow Jones Indices, said in a statement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Inflation continued to outpace home price growth in September, according to the S&P Cotality Case-Shiller Index released on Tuesday.

The data for September reveals that home prices rose 2.1% year-over-year, unchanged from a month prior, resulting in an index reading of 308.06. In contrast, inflation came in at 3.7% in September.

“Nominal home prices remain resilient, but inflation is once again widening the gap between nominal and real housing returns,” Rebecca Kaufman, the associate director of commodities at S&P Dow Jones Indices, said in a statement. “Consumer prices rose 3.7% year over year in September, accelerating from 3.4% in August, marking the 16th consecutive month in which U.S. home prices declined in real terms.”.

Month-over-month the national home price index was down 0.3%.

HousingWire Data, which is more current than Case Shiller shows that home price appreciation cooled for the week ending on Nov. 20, 2026. According to the data, the median list price for a single family home was $425,000, down 1.2% from a month prior and 0.7% from a year ago.

It has been revealed that case Shiller’s 10-City Composite index rose 3.5% annually to 330.38, down from a 3.6% annual increase in August. The 20-City index posted a 2.6% annual increase, the same as a month prior, coming in at a reading of 318.73. Both the 10-City and 20-City index recorded a 0.5% month-over-month decline prior to seasonal adjustment.

Of the 20 cities analyzed, Chicago was yet again the strongest market for home price growth, posting a 6.9% annual increase, followed by New York (5.8%) and Miami (4.6%).

“Miami’s rise is particularly notable: After moving into fourth place among the 20 cities in July and August, it has now climbed into the top three, a sharp reversal from its comparatively weak performance in 2025,” Kaufman remarked.

It has been revealed that at the other end of the spectrum, reporting annual price declines were Seattle (-1.88%),  Denver (-0.99%), Dallas (-0.9%), Las Vegas (-0.78%) and Tampa (-0.16%). This is the fourth consecutive month Seattle recorded the largest annual home price decline.

Sources indicate that housingWire Data reveals that the metro area with the largest annual price increase as of Nov. 20, 2026, was Monroe, Louisiana (+23.0%), followed by Grand Forks, ND-MN (+20.4%) and Cedar Rapids, Iowa (+18.2%). Santa Barbara, however, reported the largest annual price decline at -30.2%, followed by Fond du Lac, Wisconsin (-24.3%) and Dubuque, Iowa (-20.7%).

"This is arguably the biggest moment in the history of INEOS Automotive," Lynn Calder, CEO of Ineos Automotive, mentioned in a statement. "Setting up production there makes so much sense. It will empower us to invest, expand, and reach even more customers around the world.".

Li said BYD was looking closely at setting up a plant in France and wanted people there to think of it as a local firm. BYD plans to open additional European factories after its first plant, in Szeged, Hungary, begins mass production.

Breaking: ‘Absurd ambition’: Pulumi expands into software delivery with AI agents that ship and fix code

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1129 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Geekwire

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Todd Bishop on Nov 18, 2026 at 8:57 amNovember 18, 2026 at 9:01 am.
  • Cloud-infrastructure startup Pulumi has a name for its current fiscal year, which started in July: “the year of absurd ambition.” The first results arrived Wednesday: two products the Seattle tech giant talked about building for years but always found too big to take on.
  • The products, Pulumi Delivery and Pulumi Agents, let AI agents take over more of the work of getting new software up and running, and fixing it when something breaks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Todd Bishop on Nov 18, 2026 at 8:57 amNovember 18, 2026 at 9:01 am.

Cloud-infrastructure startup Pulumi has a name for its current fiscal year, which started in July: “the year of absurd ambition.” The first results arrived Wednesday: two products the Seattle tech giant talked about building for years but always found too big to take on.

The products, Pulumi Delivery and Pulumi Agents, let AI agents take over more of the work of getting new software up and running, and fixing it when something breaks.

According to recent reports, “The ceiling on what we can accomplish is no longer limited by the speed at which we can build software,” said Joe Duffy, the company’s co-founder and CEO, recounting the message he delivered to the Pulumi team. “It’s limited by how ambitious we’re willing to be and how substantial we’re willing to dream.”.

Industry observers note that the ambition is all the more notable because Pulumi is getting smaller. The firm has about 100 employees, down from about 130 last year. Duffy remarked there were no layoffs, and that AI has changed people’s roles and made the company more efficient.

Industry observers note that annual recurring revenue per employee more than doubled over the past year, he remarked. The organization isn’t profitable yet, but it has had a few months of positive cash flow this year. Pulumi hasn’t raised money since 2023, when it landed a $41 million round led by Madrona, bringing its total to about $99 million over the company’s lifetime.

It has been revealed that pulumi’s co-founders include Duffy and Eric Rudder, both Microsoft veterans. They started the company in 2017 to let engineers manage cloud infrastructure such as servers, networks and permissions by writing code in everyday languages like Python and TypeScript.

The new products take that approach further:.

Industry observers note that to decide whether a change is safe to ship, Pulumi Delivery can use Jev, an AI model from TypeSafe AI that estimates the odds of specific risks the team asks about in a planned change. If a risk is higher than the threshold the team sets, the release stops.

It has been revealed that duffy remarked he first noticed TypeSafe in May when it signed up as a Pulumi customer, because he liked the name. A few months later, Jev took off and TypeSafe used Pulumi to expand worldwide.

In a recent development, “Now even the call on whether a change ships can be made by a model,” said Daniel Gafni, a member of the technical staff at TypeSafe AI, in the Pulumi announcement. “That’s exactly the kind of decision we built Jev to make.”.

Recent findings suggest that both products are available now in public preview. Some features, including Jev decision gates and setting up agents, require Pulumi’s paid Pro or Enterprise aims.

Lucky timing: Pulumi’s founding bet on everyday programming languages turned out to suit AI agents, which are trained to be very good at writing exactly that kind of code.

“I wish I could say I predicted that 10 years ago, but it turns out in this case, what’s good for humans is also good for agents,” Duffy noted.

AI agents now handle 40% of the operations on the Pulumi platform that people used to do, up from 15% in April and none in January, Duffy said. Agents such as Claude Code, Codex and Pulumi’s own Neo are making infrastructure changes on their own.

Duffy noted many companies building AI coding tools stop once the code is written and reviewed. “For them, life stops at the merge,” he said. The new products cover the steps after that, from testing through release.

Plenty of company: Pulumi won’t have this market to itself. Duffy pointed to Harness, which calls it the “agentic SDLC” (short for software development lifecycle), and GitHub, which pitched “agentic software delivery” at its Universe conference last month. He said Cursor aspires to solve the problem and Anthropic built its own internal system.

The newly introduced products could replace some of the work now done by tools such as Argo CD and GitHub Actions, along with lots of homegrown scripts, he said.

“This is an industry-changing moment, and somebody has to solve this problem,” Duffy said. “And I think we are exceptionally well poised to do so.”.

Bring your own bot: Neo, the infrastructure agent Pulumi introduced last year, is now just one example of a Pulumi agent. Customers can set up as many as they want, each with its own job, instructions and tools. They can also bring their own agent, such as Claude Code or Codex, and run it in Pulumi’s cloud.

In a recent development, neo itself, which ran mainly on Anthropic’s Claude, can now use models from OpenAI or Google, too. “It’s not just Anthropic anymore,” Duffy remarked.

Agents can start work from an alert in PagerDuty, Datadog or Honeycomb, on a schedule or on request, and they report back to teams in Slack.

Pulumi has briefed about 50 customers, and about a dozen are in a private beta. Duffy said no launch in the company’s history has gotten a warmer reception, and he named Moderna among the customers eager to get it.

Pulumi has thousands of customers overall, including major companies such as BMW, Snowflake and Wiz.

According to recent reports, the business: Pulumi’s gross margins have stayed in the high 80s to low 90s even as agents drive up usage, Duffy stated. Many customers run Pulumi from inside their own Claude Code sessions, which means they’re paying both Anthropic and Pulumi.

Duffy remarked Pulumi wasn’t out looking for money when it raised its last two rounds. Investors came to the tech giant, and each deal came together in about 48 hours.

Madrona’s Tim Porter has joined the board, Duffy mentioned, taking the seat previously held by the late Soma Somasegar, who led Pulumi’s first investment.

In a recent development, about 40 of the company’s 100 employees are in the Seattle area, working out of an office at Two Union Square. Duffy noted Pulumi is hiring more people locally because in-person work still matters when building fresh products.

In a recent development, despite the smaller headcount, Pulumi is still hiring, including sales reps in nearly every region of the world. Inside the organization, Duffy remarked Pulumi is having a lot of success with “product-minded engineers who can think from our customers’ point of view, who can think like engineering managers, commanding a team of agents.”.

Asked whether a sale or more funding was in the cards, Duffy said Pulumi aspires to be a long-term successful business. “There are a variety of ways to get there,” he said. “But we want to get there on our own terms.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Homebuyer affordability improved slightly in October as lower purchase loan amounts offset higher mortgage rates, according to the Mortgage Bankers Association (MBA)’s Purchase Applications Payment Index (PAPI), released Tuesday.
  • Industry observers note that the index, which measures mortgage payments relative to borrower income, decreased 0.3% to a reading of 161.6 in October, down from 162.1 in September.
  • The improvement came despite the national median mortgage payment for purchase applicants rising to $2,236 in October, up $21 (or 0.9%) from $2,215 in September.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Homebuyer affordability improved slightly in October as lower purchase loan amounts offset higher mortgage rates, according to the Mortgage Bankers Association (MBA)’s Purchase Applications Payment Index (PAPI), released Tuesday.

Industry observers note that the index, which measures mortgage payments relative to borrower income, decreased 0.3% to a reading of 161.6 in October, down from 162.1 in September. A lower index reading indicates improving affordability.

The improvement came despite the national median mortgage payment for purchase applicants rising to $2,236 in October, up $21 (or 0.9%) from $2,215 in September. The median purchase loan application amount fell to $315,424 from $324,022, helping offset a 37-basis-point increase in mortgage rates.

“While the median mortgage payment rose $21 in October, payments as a share of earnings edged lower — slightly improving affordability,” Edward Seiler, MBA’s associate vice president of housing economics and executive director of the Research Institute for Housing America, stated in a statement.

Affordability remains weaker than a year ago. The median mortgage payment increased 9.7% from $2,039 in October 2025, while earnings grew 1.6%. As a result, the PAPI was up 8% year over year.

“Looking ahead, lower mortgage rates and stronger earnings growth would give prospective buyers more room in their budgets,” Seiler said.

The median mortgage payment for Federal Housing Administration (FHA) borrowers increased to $1,944 in October, up from $1,906 in September and $1,789 a year earlier. For conventional loan borrowers, the median payment rose to $2,258, up from $2,244 in September and $2,063 in October 2025.

Among borrowers applying for lower-payment mortgages, those in the 25th percentile, the median monthly payment increased to $1,536 in October from $1,525 in September.

According to recent reports, the PAPI for Black households decreased to 162.4 in October from 162.9 in September. For Hispanic households, it fell to 149.6 from 150.1, while the index for white households declined to 162.8 from 163.3.

Idaho had the highest PAPI reading in October at 269.8, followed by Nevada at 243.0, Rhode Island at 233.1, Arizona at 215.2 and Utah at 202.7. At the opposite end of the spectrum, Louisiana had the lowest reading at 119.8, followed by Washington, D.C., at 121.5, Alaska at 126.2, Iowa at 127.6 and Connecticut at 131.6.

The MBA’s mortgage payment-to-rent ratio also edged higher, increasing to 1.44 at the end of the third quarter from 1.43 at the end of the second quarter. The increase indicates that mortgage payments for home purchases rose slightly relative to rents.

Industry observers note that the U.S. Census Bureau reported that the national median asking rent increased to $1,541 in the third quarter from $1,531 in the second quarter. The ratio of mortgage payments for lower-payment applicants to median asking rents remained at 0.99 in September.

Separately, the MBA’s Builders’ PAPI demonstrated that the median mortgage payment for new-home purchase applicants increased to $2,375 in October, up from $2,307 in September.

  • SpaceX and Tesla $TSLA have appointed five directors to lead the special committees negotiating a possible merger, according to the Financial Times.
  • The SpaceX directors are Roelof Botha and Randy Glein.
  • The committees have brought on advisers to build the financial models each side will lean on when setting its bargaining stance for a possible all-stock merger, according to the Financial Times.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

SpaceX and Tesla $TSLA have appointed five directors to lead the special committees negotiating a possible merger, according to the Financial Times. Three of the directors come from Tesla and two from SpaceX.

The SpaceX directors are Roelof Botha and Randy Glein. Tesla is represented by Robyn Denholm, Kathleen Wilson-Thompson and Jack Hartung. The five are viewed as having no financial stake in the outcome, which qualifies them to steer the talks, according to the Financial Times.

The committees have brought on advisers to build the financial models each side will lean on when setting its bargaining stance for a possible all-stock merger, according to the Financial Times. Morgan Stanley $MS and Goldman Sachs $GS are advising SpaceX, and Evercore is advising Tesla.

The bankers are examining the areas where the two companies' businesses overlap, such as artificial intelligence models, semiconductor design and data center operations, according to the Financial Times. After the financial terms are worked out, the companies would move on to questions of governance, among them whether to name a chairperson, who would serve as CFO and which directors would keep their seats. The people cited by the Financial Times said the transaction might be wrapped up before the year closes.

A combination faces regulatory trouble because SpaceX holds U.S. defense contracts and Tesla depends on China, according to Reuters. Tesla and SpaceX did not immediately respond to requests for comment from Reuters and Benzinga.

The companies had been making headway in merger talks earlier this month, and an announcement could come as soon as December, according to Bloomberg.

According to recent reports, elon Musk disclosed in October, on SpaceX's third-quarter earnings call, that the boards had formed special committees of independent directors to examine a combination. "Because I'm a conflicted party, I can't actually be in the discussions of the special committees," Musk remarked. He said a merger would be a good idea but that shareholders have to support it, and that a deal would need the backing of 50% of all Tesla shareholders, not just a majority of votes cast.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Former National Association of Realtors Chief Financial Officer John Pierpoint has sued the organization for unpaid retirement compensation totaling more than $541,000, according to a complaint filed on Tuesday.
  • Pierpoint alleged NAR has paid senior vice presidents one year of their base salary at retirement since 2005.
  • Pierpoint retired from NAR on March 31, 2025 — a date he chose with the 2023 Sitzer | Burnett buyer-broker commission lawsuit in mind.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Former National Association of Realtors Chief Financial Officer John Pierpoint has sued the organization for unpaid retirement compensation totaling more than $541,000, according to a complaint filed on Tuesday.

Pierpoint alleged NAR has paid senior vice presidents one year of their base salary at retirement since 2005. To avoid booking the full expense when a senior vice president retired, NAR created a Compensation Reserve that let it steadily set aside funds throughout the executive’s tenure, which it would release at retirement. Pierpoint helped establish the reserve in 2005 at the direction of former NAR CEO Dale Stinton, court documents remarked.

Pierpoint retired from NAR on March 31, 2025 — a date he chose with the 2023 Sitzer | Burnett buyer-broker commission lawsuit in mind. The former CFO mentioned he was key in executing the buyer-broker commission settlement payout, which totaled $418 million. The first settlement payment, totaling roughly $200 million, was issued in February 2025, with subsequent payments of $72 million per year until the full $418 million is paid.

According to recent reports, pierpoint remarked he notified NAR of his impending retirement in late 2024 and requested his retirement payout. However, six days before his last day with NAR, Pierpoint alleged that a Grant Thornton auditor named White — there is no first name listed in the court documents — emailed him and said that “NAR had been ‘unable to locate any policy or verify any consistent practice’ concerning the Compensation Reserve or ‘the payout to executives of a full year of salary upon retirement.'”.

Sources indicate that white also allegedly said that the Compensation Reserve “was not used to fund” the exit packages of eight other senior vice presidents who retired before Pierpoint, which are listed in the court documents as L.J., F.S., B.M., D.H., J.G.,  J.B., D.G. and B.G. Real Estate News said L.J., D.G. and B.G. are likely former general counsel Laurie Janik, former SVP of talent development and resources Donna Gland, and former senior vice president and CEO Bob Goldberg.

As a result, Grant Thornton remarked it was “unable to approve the payout of a full year’s compensation without any concrete proof that such act is mandated by an employment agreement, policy or plan.”.

Pierpoint claimed NAR had the funds to pay his retirement benefit and provided a ledger outlining what the Association allegedly reserved from December 2014 to December 2024. He also remarked the trial balances NAR provided to outside auditors, including Grant Thornton, included evidence of the Compensation Reserve’s existence and purpose.

In a recent development, “NAR carried its obligation to Pierpoint at approximately 97.6 cents on the dollar three months before it refused to pay him anything,” the complaint read. “The practice NAR now claims it cannot verify is documented in NAR’s own ledger, its own year-end schedules, its own payroll records and its own audit files, and was paid to every one of Pierpoint’s predecessors who retired. NAR did not stop believing in its obligation; it stopped wanting to pay it.”.

Visualized with the help of AI.

Sources indicate that pierpoint’s counsel accused NAR of shirking its obligation to pay the former CFO due to its financial woes after the settlement. In December 2025, former NAR president Kevin Sears said the buyer-broker commission settlement saved the Association’s finances — the other option was to file an appeal and declare bankruptcy.

Industry observers note that “John Pierpoint helped guide NAR through an extraordinarily challenging period in its history, including the financial consequences of the antitrust litigation,” noted David Fish, an attorney with Workplace Law Partners, P.C., who represents Pierpoint. “After nearly four decades of service, he expected the organization to honor the same retirement compensation practice it had followed for other senior executives.”.

“We believe the evidence will establish that the financial pressures following the antitrust verdict did not relieve NAR of its obligation to pay compensation earned by its employees,” he added.

Industry observers note that pierpoint’s counsel is requesting that NAR pay the $541,059 retirement payout, statutory damages of 5 percent of the unpaid amount for each month it remains unpaid, attorneys’ fees and costs, and prejudgment and post-judgment interest. They also seek a jury trial.

NAR denied Pierpoint’s claims, saying that the former CFO has “[mischaracterized] a varied set of individual arrangements with departing executives as a uniform and guaranteed retirement benefit.”.

Recent findings suggest that “Mr. Pierpoint was not entitled to the payment he now seeks, and NAR’s decision was unrelated to its antitrust settlement or its financial condition,” an NAR spokesperson told Inman in an emailed statement. “NAR is committed to appropriate financial controls and responsible stewardship of its members’ dues dollars. NAR pays compensation and benefits that are actually owed, not just because a former executive requests payment. No such obligation exists here, and we intend to vigorously defend against these claims through the appropriate legal process.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 08:00 EST / NOVEMBER 24 2026.

According to recent reports, artificial intelligence website builder 10Web Inc. is introducing a latest feature that it claims can automatically turn content from Instagram, TikTok, Etsy, Google Business Profiles and more than 30 other sources into functioning websites and online stores.

It has been revealed that called Start from Anything, the feature targets small businesses that lack the time and expertise to build their own websites. Customers can paste a link to an existing online presence or upload files, and 10Web’s AI extracts the information needed to construct a website.

The system can convert photos and videos into galleries and product pages, use captions to populate product descriptions, and turn service information into dedicated pages. Business hours, addresses and location information can automatically populate contact pages, while social media posts can become news items and promotional offers.

10Web said its software also determines what functionality a website needs. Businesses offering services automatically receive booking capabilities, while those selling merchandise get online stores equipped to process orders and payments. Owners can subsequently modify their websites by conversing with AI.

In a recent development, “Nobody opens a bakery because they love choosing plugins,” Chief Executive Narek Torosyan stated in a statement. “Every question we ask an owner about software is a question we failed to answer ourselves.”.

The service departs from the prompt-based approach that has dominated generative AI website development. Although prompts can create attractive websites, they require owners to describe their businesses and often produce generic content that must subsequently be replaced or customized.

10Web’s approach is to reuse information businesses have already accumulated, such as photos, customer-facing descriptions, product catalogs and promotional materials.

Sources indicate that the firm stated it tested the technology using publicly available content, converting a concept store‘s Instagram presence and a vintage retailer‘s TikTok account into online stores. It also generated websites from a vacation property‘s Google profile and a small business’s Facebook page.

The upcoming capability builds on 10Web’s existing generative AI platform, which creates and manages websites using the open-source WordPress content management system.

In May 2025, the organization introduced an application programming interface that allows developers and software providers to incorporate AI website generation into their applications. The platform uses specialized AI agents to handle different aspects of website development, including design, content creation and functionality.

In a recent development, 10Web said the new feature includes hosting and is free to use for building and launching websites. The announcement did not specify charges for longer-term operation.

The organization said it serves tens of thousands of customers worldwide and attracts between 50,000 and 60,000 upcoming signups monthly.
