Lower mortgage rates could bring buyers back. What market will they return to?

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1150 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housingwire

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The possibility of mortgage rates falling below 7% before the holidays is back on the table.
  • But for housing professionals hoping to reengage buyers who stepped away from the market, mortgage rates are only part of the equation.
  • The homes available, the prices sellers are asking and the competition buyers face may look considerably different from when those buyers last searched.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The possibility of mortgage rates falling below 7% before the holidays is back on the table. In Tuesday morning’s Analyst Insights update in HousingWire Intelligence, HousingWire Lead Analyst Logan Mohtashami noted that the 10-year Treasury yield had reached 4.89%, approaching the 4.85% threshold he is watching, though mortgage spreads still need to improve.

But for housing professionals hoping to reengage buyers who stepped away from the market, mortgage rates are only part of the equation.

The homes available, the prices sellers are asking and the competition buyers face may look considerably different from when those buyers last searched.

Nationally, active single-family inventory stands at 894,692 homes, approximately 8% higher than a year ago. New pending listings increased 5.7% in the week ending Nov. 20, while new listings increased 1.2%.

That increase in contract activity is encouraging, but the broader picture remains more complicated.

HousingWire Data highlights that 44 of 57 large metro areas (77.2%) recorded an improving ratio of new pending listings to new listings over consecutive four-week periods, even as pending activity remained below year-ago levels.

During the comparable period in 2025, just three of 54 qualifying metros (5.6%) showed that same combination.

Recent findings suggest that an improving relationship between incoming listings and fresh contracts does not necessarily indicate strengthening buyer demand. And if lower mortgage rates do bring buyers back, the opportunities they encounter will vary considerably by market.

Consider Denver and Kansas City, two metro areas averaging nearly identical numbers of newly introduced pending listings per week but offering buyers different inventory and pricing environments.

Recent findings suggest that over the four weeks ending Nov. 20, Denver averaged 497 newly introduced pending listings per week, while Kansas City averaged 491. Both markets are experiencing substantially weaker contract activity than a year ago.

That’s where the similarities begin to fade.

Denver’s housing market offers buyers a different landscape heading into the holidays, with more available inventory, lower asking prices than during the spring and widespread price reductions.

For buyers who paused their home searches earlier this year because of affordability, Denver’s changing inventory and pricing conditions provide a reason to revisit their options, even before mortgage rates move meaningfully lower.

Kansas City’s median asking price has declined from its summer peak as price reductions have become more prevalent, although median asking prices remain above year-ago levels.

Industry observers note that kansas City offers buyers considerably more selection than a year ago. And while asking prices have moderated since the summer, higher median asking prices compared with last year could offset some of the affordability gains from lower borrowing costs.

Both markets offer more available homes than a year ago, but the pricing environments are different.

According to recent reports, in Denver, a decline in mortgage rates could coincide with lower asking prices and more available homes. In Kansas City, greater selection and recent pricing adjustments may create opportunities, even though the median asking price remains higher than it was a year ago.

Changes in median asking prices can reflect shifts in the composition of available inventory, not just changes in individual home prices. That’s why examining inventory, asking prices and price reductions together provides a more useful assessment of local buying conditions than any one metric alone.

Another consideration is whether contract activity is already beginning to strengthen, even with mortgage rates above 7%.

In Denver, weekly new pending listings increased across the four most recent reporting weeks:.

Cincinnati, Ohio, recorded a similar pattern, with weekly upcoming pending listings increasing from 397 to 459 over the same period.

According to recent reports, but Cincinnati presents a different inventory and pricing environment. Its median active list price is up 1.9% year over year, and the market has 2.44 months of inventory, compared with 3.01 in Denver.

While both markets have recorded three consecutive weekly increases in contract activity, buyers returning to Cincinnati could encounter a tighter inventory environment than those returning to Denver.

Neither market has recovered to last year’s level of contract activity, and several weeks of increases are not enough to establish a sustained recovery, particularly heading into the holidays.

It has been revealed that still, these are developments worth monitoring. If contract activity continues to strengthen while newly introduced listings decline seasonally, competition for available homes could increase.

Housing professionals don’t need to wait for mortgage rates to fall below 7% to start preparing for that possibility.

The more immediate opportunity is to understand how local market conditions have changed since buyers last evaluated their options.

In a recent development, for buyer’s agents: Revisit the searches of clients who paused their homebuying looks earlier this year. Has available inventory expanded in their price range? Are more homes experiencing price reductions? Changing market conditions may create opportunities worth exploring before rates move lower.

Industry observers note that for listing agents: More available inventory means more competition for sellers. Monitor latest pending listings alongside active inventory and price reductions to help sellers evaluate whether their pricing strategy remains competitive as buyer activity changes.

For mortgage lenders: Reengaging prospective purchase borrowers doesn’t have to begin with a conversation about mortgage rates. Understanding how available homes and asking prices have changed in a borrower’s target market can help make that conversation more relevant. Revisit purchasing power using current local asking prices and different mortgage rate scenarios.

In a recent development, for brokerage leaders: National mortgage rate movements can provide a reason to launch buyer reengagement campaigns, but local housing conditions should inform the messaging. A market with expanding inventory and declining asking prices presents a different opportunity than one with tighter inventory and strengthening contract activity.

Using HousingWire Intelligence, you can recreate the charts above for your own metro area, city or ZIP code.

Select single-family homes, choose the one-year view and examine four metrics together:.

Use the one-year view to understand seasonal patterns, then narrow your analysis to the most recent three or six months to identify changes in market conditions.

Looking at these metrics together can help you distinguish between a market offering greater selection and potential affordability opportunities and one where renewed buyer activity could increase competition for available homes.

Mortgage rates may give buyers a reason to reconsider their plans. Understanding how local market conditions have changed gives housing professionals a reason to reach out before they do.

Qualifying metro areas may differ between comparison periods. New pending listings represent homes entering contract, not closed transactions. Median active list prices reflect asking prices and may be influenced by changes in the composition of available inventory.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The latest data showcased by SosoValue shows that the leading Bitcoin fund has witnessed massive single-day withdrawals from investors who have ventured into its Bitcoin investment product.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

BlackRock, the leading asset management firm and Bitcoin’s largest ETF issuer, sparked discussions earlier today following a massive Bitcoin sale by the firm.

The latest data showcased by SosoValue shows that the leading Bitcoin fund has witnessed massive single-day withdrawals from investors who have ventured into its Bitcoin investment product.

Earlier today, BlackRock sold over half a billion dollars’ worth of Bitcoin after its spot Bitcoin ETF, also known as iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT), recorded a total of $541.08 million in net outflows.

This massive outflow has come as Bitcoin’s price decline continues to intensify, causing investors to aggressively pull their money out of the fund amid growing market fear.

While this marks the third time this week that BlackRock has recorded a net outflow amid persistent market volatility, it also marks the largest single-day outflow BlackRock has recorded since its launch.

Apparently, the record-breaking withdrawal that the fund just witnessed suggests that institutional and traditional investors are becoming less willing to retain their exposure to Bitcoin through asset managers, especially as Bitcoin’s price continues to slump further.

Although BlackRock has just suffered the largest withdrawal since it rolled out its Bitcoin investment product, the record outflow did not alter its dominance in the market.

Further data shows that the BlackRock spot Bitcoin ETF still boasts a massive $47.82 billion in assets under management, spotlighting its leadership in the Bitcoin ETF market.

This positions it far ahead of Fidelity, which ranks as the second-largest Bitcoin ETF with just $10.62 billion in net assets.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Z Squared Inc.
  • This quarter Z Squared completed its shift in focus from digital asset mining to AI infrastructure.
  • Recent findings suggest that the past few months have been hard on our sector, and I have felt it as a fellow shareholder.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

FORT LAUDERDALE, Fla., Nov. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Z Squared Inc. (Nasdaq: ZSQR) today issued a letter to shareholders from Chief Executive Officer David Halabu following the filing of its third-quarter Form 10-Q.

This quarter Z Squared completed its shift in focus from digital asset mining to AI infrastructure. It was a defining quarter for us, and I want to walk you through where we stand and where we're headed.

Recent findings suggest that the past few months have been hard on our sector, and I have felt it as a fellow shareholder. But a difficult market tends to blur two very different things: the conditions around a business and the fundamentals underneath it. The conditions have shifted. Financing is more expensive, investors are more cautious, and valuations across public markets have come down. The fundamentals have not. We believe AI still needs far more computing capacity than exists today, and the power to run it is still hard to find. Those fundamentals are why Z Squared exists.

It has been revealed that since we went public, our blueprint has been to move from digital asset mining into AI infrastructure. In my August letter I described the company as partway through that shift. This quarter we completed it. We directed that the mining fleet be powered down on June 16, and we do not expect to resume mining. We still own roughly 9,800 machines and we are evaluating the best way to realize value from them.

According to recent reports, that decision is also what drove our third-quarter net loss of $117.1 million. In our quarter-end review, the accounting question was a simple one: when would the fleet run again? With Dogecoin trading below our breakeven level, and more recently in the mid-5-cent range, near multi-year lows, we could not responsibly put a forecast price or date on it, and under the accounting rules that meant writing off the goodwill tied to the mining business. Approximately 94% of the loss consisted of non-cash impairment charges: $106.9 million on goodwill and $3.4 million on the machines. Neither charge came out of our cash, and they leave us with a balance sheet that reflects the business we are building.

Industry observers note that our focus now is the Union County Campus in El Dorado, Arkansas, which has access to about 8 megawatts of utility power today, on an interruptible basis under the site's existing electric service arrangements. That matters more than the number suggests. We believe demand for land with power already in place continues to outpace supply, as developers compete for sites that can support AI workloads. Upcoming grid connections can take years to secure, which makes energized sites like ours increasingly scarce. We have one, we hold an option on land next to it to grow, and we are in active commercial discussions with multiple parties for some or all of the existing 8 megawatts. We have not yet signed a lease or received a binding commitment. Capacity beyond the existing 8 megawatts, including the up to approximately 150 megawatts contemplated by our development blueprint, remains a development target and is subject to additional power arrangements, tenant commitments, financing, approvals and construction.

We are also finding ways to get more out of the site we already own. A2 Advisors' initial engineering review indicates that a large portion of the existing 10,000-square-foot mining facility on the campus may be suitable for retrofit, which, if confirmed, could meaningfully reduce the cost and time of our first build-out. A third natural gas pipeline has the potential to run lateral to our property , and we proposal to commission a feasibility study to determine how much additional power it could support.

According to recent reports, we finished September with $12.4 million in cash and no debt. Management believes our existing cash is sufficient to fund our existing operations and contractual commitments for at least twelve months. As the campus grows, we intend to finance each phase at the project level against a signed tenant lease, so new capacity is built for customers who have already committed.

In August I gave you items to measure us by, and we are delivering on them. Paradox closed on September 8, paid in preferred stock with no cash or debt at closing, and with additional preferred stock issuable only if development milestones are achieved. Site planning and engineering are underway with A2 Advisors, designed around requirements from several prospective tenants. On November 18 we confirmed a five-year option on approximately 89.56 adjacent acres, which we intend to exercise for an initial tract of up to 10 acres following a survey and site investigations, giving the campus room for a multi-phase path to larger capacity. And we are staying disciplined: major construction spending will follow a signed customer.

Industry observers note that I also told you to judge us on how we grow in a measured fashion. We remain debt-free. In recent weeks, tighter credit has weighed on AI infrastructure developers that carry legacy debt. We believe carrying no debt gives us the flexibility to move when the right opportunity comes along, and we are watching closely.

Our priorities for the coming months are clear:.

We are being deliberate about who we sign. The right tenant on the right terms, financed with discipline, is what we are accountable for and what we intend to deliver.

Industry observers note that our officers hold Z Squared shares alongside you, so we feel this market the same way you do. But market swings don't change the assets we own, the campus we are developing or our belief in both. Our job is to deliver on the priorities in front of us, and then position Z Squared for what comes next.

We believe we made the right move in repositioning this company early, and that repositioning is now behind us. Now comes the part I'm most excited about: putting it to work.

Thank you for your continued support. I look forward to updating you on our progress in the months ahead.

David HalabuChief Executive Officer & DirectorZ Squared Inc. (Nasdaq: ZSQR).

💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Todd Bishop on Nov 18, 2026 at 10:01 amNovember 18, 2026 at 10:08 am.
  • Blue Origin’s engines look like they’re off the hook, at least for now.
  • The two BE-4 engines Blue Origin makes for United Launch Alliance’s Vulcan rocket weren’t to blame for the low thrust in Sunday’s failed launch, according to preliminary findings released Wednesday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Todd Bishop on Nov 18, 2026 at 10:01 amNovember 18, 2026 at 10:08 am.

Blue Origin’s engines look like they’re off the hook, at least for now.

The two BE-4 engines Blue Origin makes for United Launch Alliance’s Vulcan rocket weren’t to blame for the low thrust in Sunday’s failed launch, according to preliminary findings released Wednesday. Instead, it appears the engines didn’t get enough fuel from the rocket, ULA mentioned.

Industry observers note that in its latest patch on the investigation, ULA said it had completed an initial integrated review of flight data. Preliminary data indicate the first stage’s low thrust came from “inadequate fuel supply from the vehicle to the BE-4 engines, not from the performance of the engines,” ULA said, adding that work remains to determine the cause.

In a recent development, on Tuesday, ULA stated early data suggested the first stage underperformed just after liftoff, leaving the rocket too low and too slow to put 40 of Amazon’s Leo internet satellites into orbit. It didn’t say then whether the engines played a role.

The BE-4s are made by Jeff Bezos’ Kent, Wash.-based Blue Origin. Blue Origin CEO Dave Limp said Wednesday on X that he was proud of the BE-4 team for its “rapid response and support of ULA’s investigation” and that the tech giant looks forward to Vulcan’s return to flight.

The finding matters for Blue Origin beyond Vulcan. Its own Upcoming Glenn rocket uses seven BE-4s on its first stage, and Amazon has 24 New Glenn launches reserved for Leo.

Industry observers note that ULA repeated that Vulcan’s second stage appears to have started normally and that its RL10 engines operated as planned but couldn’t make up for the earlier loss of performance. The six Northrop Grumman solid rocket boosters, the source of problems on two earlier Vulcan flights, appear to have performed normally, ULA noted.

The Federal Aviation Administration is overseeing the ULA-led investigation. Amazon’s next Leo launch is an Ariane 6 mission carrying 36 satellites, targeted for no earlier than Nov. 23 from French Guiana.

ULA remarked it will share more as the investigation continues.

Your real estate listing is stuck and a price drop will not fix it

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1010 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housingwire

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, there is a category of stuck listing that is going to become more common over the next few years, and most agents have not been trained for it.
  • Sources indicate that this came up on one of our Power Agent coaching calls.
  • It has been revealed that the building had a balcony and structural-compliance issue, the kind of inspection-and-repair requirement that has spread across the country since Surfside and that states like California have written into law for decks and balconies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, there is a category of stuck listing that is going to become more common over the next few years, and most agents have not been trained for it. It is the listing that cannot sell for a reason that has nothing to do with price, photography or effort. It is the listing blocked at the building level, and if we keep coaching agents to treat every slow listing with a price reduction, we are going to watch good professionals burn good listings for no reason.

Sources indicate that this came up on one of our Power Agent coaching calls. An agent brought me a four-unit situation. The condo had been on the market for 86 days. She had lost two solid buyers. One was all cash, and the all-cash buyer still walked. Any time an all-cash buyer walks, leaders should pay attention, because the one thing you cannot blame is financing.

It has been revealed that the building had a balcony and structural-compliance issue, the kind of inspection-and-repair requirement that has spread across the country since Surfside and that states like California have written into law for decks and balconies. The repairs had not been started. A new management company had taken over months earlier and was still, in their words, figuring things out.

Industry observers note that because the work was un-started, the building landed on the list that does not qualify for conventional Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac financing. The financed buyers were gone instantly. The all-cash buyer pulled the association financials, saw thin reserves and un-started repairs, read it correctly as a poorly run building, and decided the headache was not worth it.

According to recent reports, powerfact: Structural-compliance problems do not lower a home’s price. They remove a home’s buyers.

Sources indicate that that distinction matters for anyone leading a team, because it changes the coaching. When a building cannot get conventional financing, the buyer pool does not shrink, it collapses to cash buyers willing to tolerate a troubled association. We just watched one of those rare buyers say no. Telling that agent to drop the price would have been coaching malpractice. The price was never the lever.

Here is the initiative I gave her, and it is the plan I would want every leader teaching.

Industry observers note that take it off the market, temporarily. Days on market is a public number, and a climbing one negotiates against your seller before an offer is ever written. Pull the listing before the clock becomes the story.

Then, stay hired. This is the step that separates an advisor from an order-taker. Taking a listing off the market should not end the relationship, it should restructure it. The agent and I built a latest listing agreement long enough to cover the repair timeline plus fresh marketing afterward at a likely new price.

If repairs take a couple of months and the sale takes several more, that is an eight or nine month agreement, not a renewal of the old 90 days. The property comes off the MLS and is not shown, but the agreement stays active. The agent keeps her position. The seller keeps a professional who is still working.

Sources indicate that then, advocate for the whole building. I told her to get in front of the management tech giant and the association board, the president and the vice president, and push to expedite repairs that are hurting all 54 owners. This is where a top producer builds a reputation that compounds. When you are the agent pushing a stalled building back into compliance, every owner in that building knows your name, and so does every agent who tried and gave up. In a 54-unit building, that is 54 future listing conversations you just earned by being the one who demonstrated up and did the work nobody else would touch.

We also talked through the rent-instead question, because these sellers had already relocated and were carrying the unit. Renting for a year while the building gets sorted is a legitimate option, but it has to be coached with the worst case on the table. In a tenant-friendly jurisdiction an eviction can run six to nine months. Florida’s landlord rules are workable. Other markets are not.

This property sits in California, and I told her plainly that I do not know California’s specifics well enough to promise a timeline, so she needs to find out. Because if the tenant will not leave and removal takes six months, the one-year rental really delivered about six months of clean cash flow. Leaders, this is the kind of worst-case math we owe our sellers, and it is exactly the math an anxious agent skips to avoid an awkward conversation.

Sources indicate that the larger point for the industry is this. Compliance-driven financing blocks are a growing reality, and they reward the agent who can diagnose, not just discount. The old reflex of lowering price until something moves does not clear a building-level obstacle, and agents who only know that one move will lose listings they could have saved. The professionals who win in this environment are the ones who can look a seller in the eye and say, the problem is not your price, the problem is your building, and here is the plan to fix it.

That is the advisor our clients actually need. Serve, don’t sell. In a market with this much noise, the agent who clings to a dying listing looks desperate, and the one who calmly takes the sign out of the yard, extends the agreement, and goes to fix the real problem looks like exactly what they are. The one in control.

Sources indicate that darryl Davis, CSP, is a national speaker, real estate coach, and the bestselling author of How to Become a Power Agent® in Real Estate. Learn more at darrylspeaks.com.

#179220. Yield-Bearing eZAR Blurs the Line Between Stablecoin and Investment Product

📅 03 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1357 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nulltx ↗ Open Full Page

Yield-Bearing eZAR Blurs the Line Between Stablecoin and Investment Product

📅 03 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1357 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nulltx

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • eZAR opened its rand-pegged token to the public on November 2 with R303 million in circulation.
  • Industry observers note that most stablecoin launches promise a token that never moves.
  • Sources indicate that according to launch reports, eZAR is now open to the public and to new institutional partners after almost a year of pilot operations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

eZAR opened its rand-pegged token to the public on November 2 with R303 million in circulation. Its reserve yield is the feature that puts the stablecoin label to the test.

Industry observers note that most stablecoin launches promise a token that never moves. eZAR's disclosures say its holders can make money or lose it. The rand-pegged token went live to the public on November 2, and its fine print reads more like an investment product than a payments coin.

Sources indicate that according to launch reports, eZAR is now open to the public and to new institutional partners after almost a year of pilot operations. The manufacturer claims R303 million worth of tokens had been issued and were in circulation as of October 30.

The project is a partnership between eZAR Ltd, asset manager Ninety One and AVBOB Financial Services, with AVBOB acting as lead institution and liquidity partner. CEO Sean Emery stated the team put "getting it right" ahead of "getting it significant" during the pilot. The message now is that eZAR is ready to scale.

In a recent development, the model also departs from the typical single-issuer coin. Neobanks, retailers, insurers and payment firms can plug the token into their own branded wallets and share in the economics. Transfers between participating wallets settle within seconds at any hour and, according to the firm, cost nothing.

The reserves backing eZAR are invested through a money market strategy run by Ninety One, mainly in the Ninety One Money Market Fund. Returns are distributed daily to partners after partnership fees, and each partner then decides on what terms its own customers receive a share.

Ninety One's head of digital assets, Adam Duxbury, described it as new rails under an old discipline. His firm has run money market strategies for 25 years, he said, and South Africa should build its own digital rand rather than import a dollar coin.

The framing is clever, since it presents the yield as a feature of "digital cash that can grow." Yet that same feature makes the classification question hard to avoid.

The risk language is the most revealing part of the launch. eZAR describes itself as a crypto asset issued by the eZAR En Commandite Partnership. It states that the token is not legal tender, not a bank deposit and not a banking product, and that it carries no guarantee.

Sources indicate that the details that follow set it further apart. The R1 redemption value depends on available liquidity. Money market returns can be positive or negative, so capital is at risk. Holders also own no units in the underlying fund and have no direct claim on it.

Industry observers note that "Capital at risk" rarely appears in stablecoin terms. A payments token is meant to hold its value and let consumers redeem at par, yet eZAR's own documents hedge on both counts. Back in March, a market survey from Blockhouse had already noted that eZAR doesn't qualify as a stablecoin under most regulations. The live launch now tests that observation against a real product.

In the major rulebooks, the yield is the sticking point. The US GENIUS Act bars permitted payment stablecoin issuers from paying holders any form of interest or yield solely for holding, using or retaining the token. The EU's MiCA framework takes a similar line on interest. The logic is that a payment token paying a return starts to function like an unregulated deposit.

In a recent development, the OCC issued its final GENIUS Act rules on October 21, and they confirmed that ban for covered issuers. The contested ground lies elsewhere, in who sits between the issuer and the holder. Earlier OCC proposals set a rebuttable presumption against yield arrangements run through affiliates and related third parties, whereas the statute itself names only issuers.

According to recent reports, eZAR's design lands squarely in that gray zone. Returns flow to partners, and the partners decide how customers share in them. Whether that amounts to an issuer paying yield or a partner passing on profit is precisely the kind of question US regulators are now wrestling with, and it would be a difficult one to argue before the OCC.

eZAR doesn't operate under the US or EU regimes, so none of those rules apply to it directly. eZAR Ltd is described as an authorised financial services provider responsible for the main technology and services behind the partnership. That technology also draws on the South African Reserve Bank's Project Khokha 2, where eZAR's parent company, Block Markets Africa, was a technical contributor.

It has been revealed that this background signals a serious, institution-backed build rather than a speculative launch. Even so, the rand stablecoin field is getting crowded. ZARU launched earlier this year as an institutional-grade rand coin, and a pattern is emerging of different models competing for the same local payments niche.

It has been revealed that the bigger question is whether South Africa will define stablecoins narrowly, as the US and EU do, or leave room for hybrid products like this one. Because the network is permissioned, the reported circulation figure also rests on manufacturer disclosure rather than a public ledger, which makes the regulatory and disclosure framework matter even more.

For everyday users, the appeal is easy to see. A rand token that moves in seconds, costs nothing to send and might earn a daily return makes an attractive pitch. For partners, shared infrastructure with a revenue share offers a way into digital payments without building a coin from scratch.

The trade-off sits in the disclaimers. A holder who treats eZAR like a bank balance could be caught off guard by liquidity-dependent redemption, or by a money market return that dips below zero. That gap between how the product feels and how it is legally defined is where regulators tend to step in.

Industry observers note that eZAR is best understood as a hybrid: a payments token with an investment return attached. It may well succeed on those terms. Still, as more jurisdictions tighten the stablecoin definition around no-yield, par-redemption tokens, products like this will increasingly be judged on what they are rather than what they are called. How South African regulators treat eZAR in the coming months will show which way that debate is heading.

Three XRP Ledger amendments linked to native lending have each gained two validator votes since Nov. 17, according to XRPScan data. As of Nov. 20, 2026, Single Asset Vault (XLS-65) had 25 votes, and Lending Protocol (XLS-66) and the LendingProtocolV1_1 patch had 24 votes each.

XRPScan data shows that LendingProtocolV1_1 has been up for a vote since Sept. 29, 2026, when it came with the v3.4.0 release. According to the patch's voting history, it had about 19 votes for most of October. It started to gain votes again in late October. XRP was trading at $0.96 on Friday.

Lending is built directly into the XRP Ledger's code, with no third-party smart contracts. According to Ripple, lenders deposit into a Single Asset Vault, and the Lending Protocol lets loan brokers use that capital "to issue loans and track repayments onchain.".

Recent findings suggest that the model is close to how banks lend. Loans have fixed terms and a repayment schedule, and credit brokers vet borrowers before the loans are issued. On Nov. 19, Clearpool highlighted the full lending flow on the XRPL Devnet with Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin. In the demo, "An approved lender funds a private vault, and a borrower accepts and repays a loan underwritten offchain by a broker," Clearpool wrote.

Through Single Asset Vault (XLS-65), XRP holders will be able to deposit their coins into shared liquidity pools, and institutional borrowers will take loans from those pools at a fixed rate. After the loan is repaid, "the lender redeems at a higher share price," according to the Clearpool demo.

Sources indicate that the amendments still need more votes before they can activate. "An amendment needs more than 80% support, held for 14 days, to activate," XRPScan says on its amendment pages. For the current set of 35 validators, the site puts the threshold at "more than 80% of 35 votes, so 29 needed.".

— Weiwei Yang has left Microsoft after more than a decade to co-found a startup that is “building the power grid for the AI age,” according to her LinkedIn profile.

Yang was most recently a senior director with Microsoft Research, working on grid technology. Her team built a grid dataset and released small foundation models to help users operate and expand electrical infrastructure.

Yang thanked her community at the tech giant, adding, “I hope the relationships and collaborations we’ve built continue well beyond Microsoft, and that we find many fresh ways to work together.”.

According to recent reports, — Allie Mellen has joined Microsoft as principal director for security research and threat intelligence. Mellen was previously a principal analyst at Forrester. She also wrote “Code War,” a book that explores cyberattacks as a powerful geopolitical weapon.

In her new role, Mellen said she will lead strategy for protection and threat intelligence, “helping shape what intelligence we produce, how AI can improve its speed and quality, and how we turn that knowledge into better protection for customers.”.

— Agility Robotics, the Salem, Ore., firm that had its Nasdaq debut earlier this month, has announced three leadership changes:.

— Former tech executive Drew Sheriff has been named CEO and president of the Space Needle and Chihuly Garden and Glass. Sheriff was previously a vice president at DoorDash and has held leadership roles at Amazon, Starbucks and Parachute Home. His roles focused on customer experience, product growth, strategy and marketing.

“His skill set is the ideal background for charting how we attract customers and how we delight customers in this newly introduced age,” Jeff Seely, board chair for the Space Needle and Chihuly Garden and Glass, told the Seattle Times.

— Microsoft has named Caroline King as director of its Washington state community and philanthropy team, with a focus on advocacy work across housing, affordability and other priority issues.

According to recent reports, king is the founder and past CEO of Washington STEM, an organization that coordinates research, advocacy, policy, philanthropy and partnerships to support science, technology, engineering and math education in the state. She most recently served as a leader on the governing body of an international school in Luxembourg.

— Longtime Amazon and Microsoft tech exec Scott Wiltamuth has retired — mostly.

Wiltamuth joined Amazon in 2011 as an AWS vice president overseeing a large organization building developer and management tools. In 2018, he took a seven-month leave for colon cancer treatment. After returning, he sought a director-level position and thanked firm leaders for helping him find a better fit. “Their flexibility and creativity enabled me to extend my AWS career,” he said.

Wiltamuth launched his tech career at Microsoft in 1993 and left nearly 19 years later as director of program management for Visual Studio Pro.

He now spends time with his wife and family, traveling, golfing, swimming and reading. “I don’t plan to pursue another full-time operational role,” Wiltamuth said, “but may do some part-time work.”.

Recent findings suggest that — Adam Nygate has exited Palo Alto Networks to co-found and lead a stealth startup based in Seattle. He was founder and CEO of Huntr, a platform launched in 2019 where security researchers could submit information on AI and machine learning vulnerabilities. Protect AI acquired Huntr, and Palo Alto Networks later acquired Protect AI.

“Huntr was a bet that open source gets safer when vulnerabilities are visible to the people who can fix them, even when that made life uncomfortable for vendors who’d rather keep things quiet,” Nygate said in a post announcing his career change and impending newly introduced baby.

— BluePill, a Seattle-based marketing startup that helps brands predict consumer behavior, has named Mike Weis as chief revenue officer and head of sales.

It has been revealed that weis has 40 years of experience in consumer packaged goods, retail and commerce, beginning his career as a Pacific Northwest leader at Unilever and holding executive positions at Catalina and Quotient Technologies. Recent roles include adviser at Contento2, eGateway Capital and And1 Advisors.

“Beyond the incredible résumé, Mike is one of the kindest, most genuine, and most passionate people I’ve met. Someone who has accomplished so much, yet brings so much humility, curiosity, and energy to every conversation,” noted Ankit Dhawan, CEO and founder of BluePill.

— Glacis, a Seattle startup that builds tamper-proof records of AI behavior, has named Caer Mistral Sanders as a technical co-founder. Sanders has rolled out startups and joins Glacis from Thoughtworks. Before that, she held leadership roles at Wayfair and Onshape. As a teenager, she published a book on mixed-reality control systems and won a world robotics championship.

In a recent development, in a post announcing the new role, Sanders mentioned she has designed medical record systems, researched robot communication, patented cryptographic technology and built widely used AI platforms. “This is the first time in my career I get to bring all of those skills to bear on one problem, and I couldn’t be more excited!” she added.

— The PNW Battery Collaborative has welcomed Jason Demeny as its director of communications. Demeny is a marketing leader whose past employers include Crusoe, Patch, Qualtrics and Apptio. Earlier in his career, he spent more than a decade at Microsoft over two stints, most recently leading teams that served the Azure Partner Experience group.

The nonprofit PNW Battery Collaborative brings together startups, innovators and researchers focused on energy storage.

Industry observers note that — Tom Wheeler, former chairman of the Federal Communications Commission, has joined the advisory council for Known, a Bellevue, Wash.-based firm building accountability infrastructure for autonomous AI. Wheeler led the FCC from 2013 to 2017.

Known, previously called Identity Digital Innovation Labs, spun out of Identity Digital in September.

According to recent reports, — Versium has promoted Matthew Baumgartner to vice president of engineering. The Redmond, Wash.-based company provides data and software that help businesses identify potential customers, fill in missing contact information and target their marketing. Baumgartner has been with Versium since 2018.

— Charlie Trillingham has been named communications manager for the University of Washington AI and Machine Learning for Engineering programs and the UW NSF AI Institute for Dynamic Systems. He previously served as a marketing and communications lead for the Buerk Center for Entrepreneurship within the UW’s Foster School of Business.

Brava Security finds exposed log collectors could let attackers tamper with breach evidence

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (979 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Siliconangle

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that A new report out today from security operations startup Brava Security Inc.
  • Dubbed “Ghost Feeds,” the research is stated to show that attackers able to write into those collectors may be able to tamper with the evidence a security team uses to investigate a breach.
  • According to recent reports, as part of the research, a decoy security information and event management system with no legitimate traffic was deployed on the public internet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 09:00 EST / NOVEMBER 24 2026.

Sources indicate that A new report out today from security operations startup Brava Security Inc. find that more than 2,300 exposed log collectors at nearly 1,200 organizations accepted fabricated security events without requiring credentials, raising questions about the reliability of the data that security teams depend on.

Dubbed “Ghost Feeds,” the research is stated to show that attackers able to write into those collectors may be able to tamper with the evidence a security team uses to investigate a breach.

According to recent reports, as part of the research, a decoy security information and event management system with no legitimate traffic was deployed on the public internet. Within about two hours, unknown parties had begun reading from the decoy. Attempts to inject fabricated events followed shortly after. The activity continued for at least two weeks.

Following on from the decoy, the researchers sent a single harmless, uniquely marked event to internet-exposed log collectors running any of seven logging products, including Elasticsearch, Splunk and Fluent Bit. More than 2,300 of those endpoints were found to accept the event with no authentication required. The number of organizations affected may be higher still, according to Brava, since its researchers were able to identify the owners of only about a third of the endpoints.

Recent findings suggest that results varied by platform, with about three-quarters of the exposed Elasticsearch clusters that responded accepting the test event. Nearly two-thirds of sampled TCP Syslog collectors also accepted it, as did 43% of identified Fluent Bit endpoints.

In a recent development, splunk, the report notes, is a different story. Thanks to default authentication requirements, its HTTP Event Collector rejected 58% of test writes. The catch is that the primary forwarding port on a standard Splunk installation was shown in laboratory testing to accept unauthenticated events in plain text. More than 100,000 internet hosts listen on that port number, with 42% of a sample accepting the unauthenticated events.

It has been revealed that according to the researchers, the damage from forged telemetry can go well beyond false alerts. In one lab test, 13 cents’ worth of bandwidth generated enough data to exceed a Splunk daily license allowance by 2.39 times in 141 seconds. Should that happen repeatedly, search can be disabled while logs continue to come in, potentially leaving a security team unable to investigate.

According to recent reports, “Security teams cannot afford to assume that everything appearing in their SIEM is trustworthy,” stated Idan Basre, Brava’s co-founder and chief executive, who led product management for Microsoft Defender before starting the company. An attacker able to influence that evidence, he warned, could potentially “change the outcome of an investigation before anyone realizes the underlying data has been compromised.”.

Brava’s researchers also wanted to know what manipulated logs would do to AI-powered security operations. To find out, three popular open-source AI security operations center tools were given the same suspicious login scenario.

In a recent development, all three initially identified the activity correctly. Once the researchers had injected 10 fabricated Windows events into the logs, the same suspicious login went unnoticed by all three.

Since AI investigators are “only as reliable as the evidence they analyze,” according to Brava co-founder and Chief Technology Officer Itay Gabbay, attackers able to write into the systems supplying that evidence may be able to influence what security teams and their AI agents end up dismissing.

To help organizations check their own exposure, Brava is releasing ghost-telemetry-check, a free, open-source tool designed to test whether a logging pipeline will accept unauthenticated events. Detection rules for Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel and other platforms are also included in the release.

It has been revealed that brava formally debuted earlier this month with $15 million in seed funding led by F2 Venture Capital and Pitango Venture Capital. Its platform is said to use multi-agent AI to generate the telemetry an attack would produce without carrying out the attack, showing companies which threats their existing defenses would miss.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Steve's teenage son, the Fantastic Four, Doctor Doom's warning, Thor's confession and Cyclops's rallying cry: 5 reveals from the final trailer.
  • Industry observers note that for years, Marvel Studios treated the Avengers story as finished, with its heroes retired or their roles handed to successors.
  • Marvel started reopening the past before its final trailer came out, and it did so by returning to the old film itself.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Steve's teenage son, the Fantastic Four, Doctor Doom's warning, Thor's confession and Cyclops's rallying cry: 5 reveals from the final trailer.

Industry observers note that for years, Marvel Studios treated the Avengers story as finished, with its heroes retired or their roles handed to successors. Avengers: Doomsday is the studio's attempt to open that story back up. The previous Avengers film was Avengers: Endgame in 2019, according to Notebookcheck. Marvel is coming back to a series it set aside years ago, so it has to rebuild the team rather than resume where it left off. The filmmakers present at least one homecoming as certain rather than risky. Directors Joe and Anthony Russo have called Steve Rogers the character who changed their lives and described his return as inevitable, according to the Dallas Morning News. For viewers, the question is therefore not whether the old heroes will come back but what Marvel has to disturb to bring them back.

Marvel started reopening the past before its final trailer came out, and it did so by returning to the old film itself. The studio re-released the 2019 finale as Avengers: Endgame Encore with four minutes of fresh footage tied to Doomsday, Variety reports, which put the setup for the new film in theaters inside the old one. Audiences paid to see that setup, and the re-release opened at No. 1 at the domestic box office with $26 million. That means a large audience had already watched Doomsday's groundwork before Marvel demonstrated its last trailer. It also leaves the trailer in an awkward position. To surprise people who have seen that much, Marvel has to reveal moments the film might once have saved for opening night.

The Hollywood Reporter highlighted the most startling moments shown in the last Doomsday trailer, from a glimpse of Steve's family life to a warning from Doctor Doom and an X $TWTR-Men rallying cry. Marvel will release the film on Dec. 18, 2026, and these moments give audiences their clearest look at it until then. Read together, they tell one story: heroes pulled out of lives they had settled into, and a villain who wants those lives back.

Before anyone throws a punch, Marvel indicates the life Steve chose when he walked away from the fight. The final trailer starts at home with Steve and Peggy Carter, whose teenage son doesn't know that his father was once Captain America, according to The Hollywood Reporter. Endgame ended with Steve returning as an old man, The Dallas Morning News reports, and the trailer now shows the middle of the life that film only implied. His peace depends on keeping the hero buried, even from his own family, and by opening in that house, Marvel makes everything that follows a threat to the home.

It has been revealed that marvel's earlier footage left fans guessing about Steve's family. After the first teaser, Rolling Stone suggested that the baby in it was Steve's child with Peggy, according to The Dallas Morning News. The final trailer gives Steve and Peggy a teenage son, which fits that guess and settles a mystery Marvel could have kept until opening night.

It has been revealed that steve gave up the role for good instead of taking a break from it. He handed his shield to Sam Wilson at the end of Endgame, according to The Dallas Morning News, so a return now would mean leaving his family rather than stepping back into an old job.

The trailer doesn't say what Steve will have to give up once he is pulled back into the fight.

Sources indicate that four heroes show up at Steve's peaceful home to draw him out of retirement. Reed Richards, Sue Storm, Johnny Storm and Ben Grimm are the ones at his door, according to The Hollywood Reporter. Variety reports that Pedro Pascal plays Mister Fantastic. None of them served with Steve, so Marvel makes the recruitment a meeting between strangers rather than old friends.

Sources indicate that the Four want more from Steve than an extra pair of hands. Variety reports that their aim is to put him in charge of the Avengers in the fight against Doctor Doom. The saga had let Steve go, and this visit returns him to the head of the team.

In a recent development, steve's return also means a change of place. The Four take him back to the main timeline, according to Variety, away from the one where he settled down after Endgame.

Steve can rejoin the Avengers only by walking out of the house where the Four found him.

In the final Avengers: Doomsday trailer, Doctor Doom treats the heroes as thieves. Robert Downey Jr.'s Victor von Doom indicates they are living "stolen lives" and wants them returned, according to The Hollywood Reporter. The heroes have settled down since their last fight, and Doom's line is an ultimatum rather than a taunt.

In a recent development, the trailer makes the threat personal through the footage that plays while Doom speaks. His line runs over Steve leaving with the Fantastic Four and over scenes of Thor's daughter, Love, and Ant-Man's daughter, Cassie, according to Gizmodo. Heard against those images, "stolen lives" points at the families the heroes love, not a city or the team.

In a recent development, for all its menace, the trailer never indicates how Doom would take those lives, though one shot may hint at it. In that shot two planets move toward a third, and Gizmodo suggests that the image may point to an incursion, a danger Marvel raised earlier in Loki and Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness. The film has not confirmed the incursion guess. If it proves right, Doom's demand would carry a threat from those earlier stories into the Avengers saga.

Doom has named what he wants returned, and the film will have to show how he means to collect it.

Sources indicate that thor's call for the heroes to unite comes with an admission that he can't tell who most of them are. Thor, played by Chris Hemsworth, tells the merging teams to drop their bickering, according to The Hollywood Reporter. "I don't know what half of you do. I don't even know who half of you are," Thor says, as reported by Notebookcheck. For viewers, that joke takes off some pressure. If Thor can't keep track of everyone, Marvel isn't asking the audience to keep track either.

Recent findings suggest that the bickering Thor wants to end is a real fight between heroes from two franchises.   • A “Saturday Night Live” skit about caring for aging relatives touched a viral nerve after it aired over the weekend, including with Melinda French Gates, who offered her own “fact check” on the too-close-to-home comedy.
  • The sketch, a fake commercial, stars host John Mulaney as a man who has found an easy way to care for his aging father without upending his own life: “Sister,” an “elder care system” that is free and is, in fact, his sister.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Kurt Schlosser on Nov 18, 2026 at 1:23 pmNovember 18, 2026 at 1:23 pm.

A “Saturday Night Live” skit about caring for aging relatives touched a viral nerve after it aired over the weekend, including with Melinda French Gates, who offered her own “fact check” on the too-close-to-home comedy.

The sketch, a fake commercial, stars host John Mulaney as a man who has found an easy way to care for his aging father without upending his own life: “Sister,” an “elder care system” that is free and is, in fact, his sister.

French Gates wrote on Instagram this week that the sketch “is funny because it’s a little too true.” Using research from Pivotal, her investment and philanthropic organization, she went through the ad’s claims one by one and found that most held up:.

Sister will provide. True, French Gates said, citing AARP and the National Alliance for Caregiving. Among adults ages 55 to 64, women are nearly 40% more likely than men to care for an older relative, and nearly 40% more likely to provide constant care.

Industry observers note that she’ll quit her job. “Mostly true,” at least the job part. Catalyst found that 42% of women who voluntarily left jobs in 2025 cited caregiving as the main reason.

Paid help is pricey. “True, unfortunately.” New America puts the average home health aide at more than $6,600 a month, and 24-hour care can top $25,000.

Sister may break down. Also true. In the Caregiving in the U.S. 2025 report, nearly two-thirds of caregivers said they were under moderate or high emotional stress, and women felt the strain more than men did.

It has been revealed that “Free” is misleading. French Gates said Sister isn’t free; she’s the one paying for the care, in lost wages, stalled careers, thinner retirement savings and less time for her own life.

French Gates has made women’s health and caregiving central to her work since she stepped down as co-chair of the Gates Foundation in 2024.

Recent findings suggest that she left with $12.5 billion to put toward her work on behalf of women and families. Much of that work runs through Pivotal, the Seattle-area organization she founded to handle her philanthropy and investments. In June she pledged another $215 million for women’s health, which brought her giving in that area to more than $600 million over two years. The pledge included $10 million to the Menopause Society for better menopause care in the U.S.

The sketch has been shared widely across the country this week, in part because it lines up so closely with the research.

According to recent reports, in its own analysis, The Newly introduced York Times cited studies showing that daughters generally provide at least twice as much care to aging parents as sons do. The U.S., unlike many wealthy countries, offers no federal paid leave or long-term care insurance for family caregivers.

French Gates stated she welcomed the conversation.

Recent findings suggest that “I’m so glad we’re talking about this, and laughing about it,” she wrote on Instagram. “We need more honesty about what caring for loved ones really takes and why so much of that work falls to women. But I’d love for the day to come when these jokes don’t pack quite the same punch — because we’ve made it so much easier to care for the people we love.”.

That experience shaped the AI Operations Accelerator, which begins with one workflow and an agreed outcome, then builds and improves the capability through real use.

The tech giant is developing an approach in which a dedicated owner works directly with delivery teams and uses AI to turn real work, lessons learned, and customer outcomes into timely stories for customers, partners, employees, and the market.

The same capability is intended to support sales enablement, creating a shared foundation for translating operational progress into clear commercial narratives.

"Teams are learning and delivering faster every week," Greg added. "The opportunity is to close the gap between what we are doing and what we are communicating by bringing PR closer to the work and giving it clear ownership.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Kurt Schlosser on Nov 18, 2026 at 2:03 pmNovember 18, 2026 at 2:03 pm.

Google is bringing Seattle-based Howie, maker of an AI scheduling assistant that works from your inbox, into its Google Labs division.

Terms of the deal were not disclosed this week. Google Labs, the company’s experimental arm, revealed the acquisition in a post on X, saying it “can’t wait to learn from them as we build the next generation of intuitive AI tools together for small businesses.”.

Howie CEO and co-founder Austin Petersmith remarked on LinkedIn that the team will continue building Howie at Google. “Howie has always been built on top of Gmail and Google Calendar, so Google Labs is the perfect place for us to take this product to the next level,” he wrote.

In a recent development, petersmith co-founded Howie around 2023 with CTO Dave Newman. The two first worked together in 2013 at Assembly, which Newman co-founded, and prototyped an AI assistant in 2015 before deciding the market wasn’t ready.

Industry observers note that we’re excited to welcome Howie to Google Labs! The @Howie_ai team has spent years figuring out scheduling and calendar management. We can’t wait to learn from them as we build the next generation of intuitive AI tools together for small businesses 🤝 https://t.co/8bzjebeGdD.

People cc Howie on an email thread, and it coordinates meeting times, adds events to calendars, follows up as needed and flags scheduling conflicts. Customers set their own rules in an open-ended preferences document, such as “if it’s a pitch call, set it to 25 minutes and use Zoom.”.

Behind the scenes, Howie ran tasks through fine-tuned language models and looped in human scheduling experts when the AI wasn’t confident.

Howie raised a $6 million seed round led by True Ventures in September 2025, when it launched publicly out of private beta. At the time, it had more than 1,000 paying customers, including startup founders, venture capitalists, recruiters, consultants and journalists, and was scheduling more than 5,000 meetings a week.

According to recent reports, the deal comes as Google and rivals including OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta race to build AI agents that complete tasks on behalf of users. Google Labs acquired music generation platform ProducerAI earlier this year.

Astelia’s autonomous network mitigation blocks AI-driven exploits without a patch

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (917 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Siliconangle

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that exposure management company Astelia Inc.
  • It has been revealed that the new capability has been designed to address what Astelia indicates is the problem of frontier AI models cutting the time to exploit to almost zero, leaving manual triage and remediation unable to keep up.
  • “For years, security teams have been told to patch faster,” said co-founder and Chief Executive Alon Noy, adding that the advice “stops working when the exploit arrives before the change window does.”.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 09:00 EST / NOVEMBER 24 2026.

It has been revealed that exposure management company Astelia Inc. today unveiled the launch of autonomous network mitigation, a upcoming capability that allows organizations to block artificial intelligence-driven exploits at the network level, even when a patch isn’t available or can’t be applied.

It has been revealed that the new capability has been designed to address what Astelia indicates is the problem of frontier AI models cutting the time to exploit to almost zero, leaving manual triage and remediation unable to keep up. Astelia argues that autonomous remediation isn’t a viable option for large enterprises, where every patch requires a change window so it doesn’t break key business processes. In many cases, there is also no patch to apply because the vendor hasn’t released a fix yet or, for older and end-of-life systems, never will.

“For years, security teams have been told to patch faster,” said co-founder and Chief Executive Alon Noy, adding that the advice “stops working when the exploit arrives before the change window does.”.

Autonomous network mitigation is designed to block the path an attacker would use to reach a vulnerable system instead of changing the system itself. Mitigations are applied automatically within policies the organization sets. Nothing on the asset is changed, allowing business-critical systems, including operational technology, to stay online.

Recent findings suggest that underpinning the service is Astelia’s reachability analysis, which maps an organization’s real network topology and applies agentic AI to analyze the requirements of each exploit. By correlating exploit conditions with network topology, the platform identifies which vulnerabilities are reachable by attackers and through which paths. In one enterprise deployment, approximately 40 million vulnerabilities were reduced to fewer than 2,000 that were reachable, according to the company.

Key features of autonomous network mitigation include the ability to identify the most effective choke point on an attack path and drive the mitigation through an organization’s web application firewall or intrusion prevention and detection system. A single rule at a choke point is remarked to protect every vulnerable server behind it, compared with one change per server when patching. Because mitigations are only applied to paths that have been proven reachable, the service doesn’t add rules for exposure that doesn’t exist.

Industry observers note that every mitigation applied by Astelia can also be rolled back, something that isn’t always possible with a patch. That is said to allow teams to act quickly without putting business operations at risk.

It has been revealed that autonomous network mitigation can be deployed through Astelia Agents, the firm’s suite of AI agents, as a dedicated agent that applies mitigations on its own. The agent can also be connected with other agents to respond to urgent threats such as zero-day vulnerabilities and critical disclosures. Astelia gave the example of the PHP2Shell remote code execution flaws disclosed in October, which left end-of-life PHP servers with no official fix.

Each organization sets its own guardrails on how mitigations are applied. Users can require human approval for specific environments or actions, according to the organization. Every action is logged and can be audited. Analysis on the Astelia platform continues to run on read-only integrations, with mitigation actions using scoped permissions that each organization enables and controls.

Autonomous network mitigation initially supports web application firewall and intrusion prevention and detection rules, with support for firewall rules planned in the future.

According to recent reports, founded in 2024 by former leaders of the Israeli National Red Team, Astelia is a venture capital-backed organization that raised $35 million in combined seed and Series A funding in February. Investors in the company include Index Ventures, Team8 and Holly Ventures.

Recent findings suggest that as of Nov. 20, Shiba Inu (SHIB) is about $10 million in market capitalization short of overtaking Bittensor (TAO) for the No. 33 spot in CoinMarketCap's global crypto ranking. TAO has a market cap of $2.18 billion at a price of $186.41, and SHIB has $2.17 billion at $0.000003691 and ranks No. 34.

A gain of about 0.5% in SHIB's price, with TAO's price unchanged, would be enough for the meme coin to take Bittensor's place in the ranking.

Industry observers note that TAO is the token of the Bittensor AI network, and Digital Currency Group (DCG) founder Barry Silbert has been one of its most vocal backers. Silbert also runs Yuma, a DCG tech giant that builds on Bittensor.

At Fortune's Brainstorm Tech conference in September 2025, Silbert mentioned that Bittensor was the thing he had gotten most excited about since Bitcoin. "I want to open up the development and the access to AI, and Bittensor is enabling that," he said at the time. Silbert also said that Bittensor is building a "world wide web of intelligence.".

It has been revealed that on Dec. 30, 2025, DCG's Grayscale filed with the SEC to convert its Grayscale Bittensor Trust into a spot exchange-traded fund on NYSE Arca under the ticker GTAO. The filing came after Bittensor's first halving in mid-December 2025, and at the end of that month, TAO was trading at about $222. "We're pleased to take this early step as we continue to expand the tools available to investors," a Grayscale spokesperson stated.

The gap between the two tokens closed because TAO fell. TAO was one of the market's strongest tokens this year. In April, the token was up 55% since January, and in October it rallied again and was up 43% for the year, according to TradingView data.

The November correction erased those gains. On Nov. 20, TAO was trading 16.95% below its January level, and it lost 12.16% over the past week.

SHIB spent most of the year in the red. The meme coin rose about 25% in January, and it has not been in positive territory since February. By Nov. 20, SHIB had lost about 50% since the start of the year, and it fell 13.79% over the past week.

In a recent development, TAO had a 24-hour trading volume of $172.19 million on Nov. 20, and SHIB had $55.17 million, according to CoinMarketCap data. TAO has a maximum supply of 21 million tokens, the same as Bitcoin's, and SHIB has about 589 trillion tokens in circulation.

Shiba Inu developer Mazrael responded to the drop on X on Nov. 17. "1 SHIB is always 1 SHIB," he wrote in reply to a user who pointed to the falling price.
