💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ahead of Nvidia’s board of directors voting unanimously to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang less than two weeks after his ouster, President Donald Trump effectively gave them a major reprieve from some legal liabilities, one corporate governance expert noted.
  • Trump told CNBC on Monday that Nvidia’s board “did ask for assurance on the national security threat,” seemingly referring to a White House guarantee that the board would be exempt from liability regarding its former and current CEO’s embroilment in an international scandal.
  • A White House spokesperson confirmed Trump’s role to Fortune: “President Trump was totally involved, and this is a great decision by the Nvidia board.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ahead of Nvidia’s board of directors voting unanimously to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang less than two weeks after his ouster, President Donald Trump effectively gave them a major reprieve from some legal liabilities, one corporate governance expert noted.

Trump told CNBC on Monday that Nvidia’s board “did ask for assurance on the national security threat,” seemingly referring to a White House guarantee that the board would be exempt from liability regarding its former and current CEO’s embroilment in an international scandal. “And we gave them assurances at least with everything we know, and we know a lot.”.

A White House spokesperson confirmed Trump’s role to Fortune: “President Trump was totally involved, and this is a great decision by the Nvidia board. We have to protect our geniuses.”.

Huang, who cofounded the semiconductor chip giant 33 years ago, resigned earlier this month following revelations of an affair with a woman, Alice Huang, whom U.S. intelligence reportedly deemed a Chinese operative. Alice Huang was also an executive at Singapore-based cloud computing organization Megaspeed, which is being investigated for allegedly smuggling at least $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia chips. The Nvidia CEO also faces allegations of affairs with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of health care, and a second unnamed Nvidia employee; it is unclear which scandal prompted his resignation.

Nvidia’s board reportedly met on Sunday night, just hours after Trump made a call on social media for Huang’s reinstatement.

Ann Lipton, a law professor at the University of Colorado, Boulder, who specializes in corporate governance, stated Trump’s assurances over national security were likely one of the defining factors in the board’s decision to reinstate Huang, as it granted the board a fresh level of legal protection.

“Once it became clear that the board was no longer going to be legally vulnerable, that’s when I think it became inevitable that this was going to play out,” Lipton told Fortune.

Nvidia’s board had no clear succession initiative, and Huang had up to 60 direct reports, making it difficult to check the CEO’s authority, some experts warned. In its announcement of Huang’s reinstatement, Nvidia said it would hire a chief compliance officer, which the organization has never had.

In a recent development, in September 2003, the Securities and Exchange Commission concluded its probe into the manufacturer and filed financial reporting fraud charges against former CFO Christine B. Hoberg, claiming she had failed to report $3.3 million in expenses. The CFO paid a $672,000 settlement. In 2022, Nvidia paid the SEC $5.5 million in civil penalties over inadequate disclosures regarding how cryptocurrency mining bolstered its gaming GPU sales.

Nvidia has also previously been accused of using monopolistic tactics, including in 2021, when the Federal Trade Commission blocked the manufacturer’s attempt to purchase chip firm Arm. Now, in addition to the Department of Justice investigating Nvidia’s knowledge of Megaspeed’s alleged chip smuggling, it is also reportedly facing an SEC probe over any accounting irregularities and inadequate disclosures over questionable chip sales in Asia.

Sources indicate that while loose board oversight works when stock prices are high, Lipton mentioned, any legal scandal can put the board in jeopardy, which is what happened when news of Huang’s affair came to a head. Legal scandals don’t just put the company in jeopardy, but also the board personally. If the board hadn’t pushed Huang to resign earlier this month, they could have been held liable for a failure of oversight or acquiescing in securities fraud, according to Lipton.

“In that context, it may very well have seemed to the board like firing Huang and creating this internal investigation was really the only way that they could separate themselves from him,” she said.

While there was market pressure to rehire Huang—Nvidia’s stock fell 28% from Huang’s resignation through Friday’s market close—Trump’s assurances alleviated legal pressures put on the board, and the individuals on the board, Lipton explained.

In a recent development, “What the board would have been vulnerable to is essentially a claim that they fail to exercise proper oversight,” she said. “You can’t make that claim if the president of the United States is assuring you that there are no legal risks, even if something were to be uncovered, even if something were to be uncovered by a future administration.”.

Nvidia did not immediately respond to Fortune’s request for comment.

Trump’s comments don’t guard Nvidia’s board from all legal risks, however. According to Jonathan Macey, a professor of corporate law, corporate finance, and securities law at Yale Law School, while board members may not face criminal legal pressure, they are still vulnerable to civil risks for corporate governance failures.

Recent findings suggest that board members may still be subject to lawsuits filed by shareholders, as well as congressional investigations, particularly after a Democratic midterm sweep. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer signaled on Monday prepares to probe parties involved in Huang’s reinstatement.

“Democrats will wield their full power to investigate any wrongdoing by the Trump administration, Jensen Huang, other Nvidia executives, and anyone selling out our national security for financial gain,” Schumer wrote on social media.

Trump’s comments about his role in reinstating Huang have raised speculation about the president’s plans to preemptively pardon the Nvidia CEO, but corporate governance experts agreed Trump pardoning Huang would not hold the same benefits for Nvidia’s board. A preemptive pardon—which the Trump administration has offered no public intentions of issuing—would signal that there was a nontrivial possibility of Huang being in danger of a criminal conviction, which could mount even more pressure on the board as to why they reinstated him.

“All that does is mean that this guy probably did something really awful from a director’s point of view,” Macey told Fortune. “It makes it worse.”.

StepSecurity, led by two Microsoft vets, raises $20M to defend developers’ tools from hackers

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (879 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Geekwire

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Todd Bishop on Nov 20, 2026 at 8:28 amNovember 20, 2026 at 8:34 am.
  • StepSecurity’s co-founders spent more than two decades combined at Microsoft.
  • Their old employer is not the only one with this problem.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Todd Bishop on Nov 20, 2026 at 8:28 amNovember 20, 2026 at 8:34 am.

StepSecurity’s co-founders spent more than two decades combined at Microsoft. This week, as their startup announced a upcoming round of funding, its researchers were also investigating a hacked Microsoft software package.

Their old employer is not the only one with this problem.

Sources indicate that stepSecurity, a Seattle-area cybersecurity startup, raised a $20 million Series A round led by Elephant, with participation from existing investors Runtime Ventures, Inner Loop Capital and SaaS Ventures. The company has now raised $23 million, including a $3 million seed round in 2024. Axios Pro first reported the latest round.

The startup protects the systems used to build software: developers’ laptops, code repositories, package downloads and CI/CD pipelines, the automated systems that assemble and ship code.

Industry observers note that the problem is that attackers increasingly slip malicious code into open-source software that developers download. That code can do damage as soon as it runs on a developer’s laptop or build system, stealing the passwords and keys that unlock other systems.

Recent findings suggest that “A supply chain attack used to take a skilled team,” CEO Varun Sharma wrote in a blog post announcing the funding. “Now one person can vibe code it.”.

Sources indicate that sharma spent about 15 years at Microsoft, where he led a team in Azure Security focused on making security easier for developers. CTO Ashish Kurmi spent nearly eight years at Microsoft before leading cloud security at Uber and infrastructure security at Plaid.

The two met at Microsoft and started StepSecurity in 2021, after working through the fallout from the SolarWinds and Codecov supply chain attacks at their respective employers.

A busy week: The Microsoft package, agent-framework, is the Python version of Microsoft’s open-source toolkit for building AI agents.

Industry observers note that it gets roughly 190,000 downloads a month. Two malicious versions published on Nov. 17 to PyPI, the main public repository for Python software, included code designed to steal cloud and CI/CD credentials as soon as Python started up, SecurityWeek reported. PyPI quarantined both versions, and a Microsoft maintainer mentioned an investigation was underway.

That’s one entry in a long list. StepSecurity’s announcement also cites the $6.3 billion Binance breach in October, which the FBI attributed to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group. Binance has said the attack started with a compromised employee laptop.

Industry observers note that it also points to a tampered copy of Anthropic’s Claude Code extension that sat in Cursor’s extension marketplace for about 11 hours last month. Cursor said up to 5,000 consumers may have received the malicious version.

StepSecurity claims it documented 56 confirmed compromises of trusted software components between August 2025 and August 2026, and roughly one every three days from March 2026 through the August report.

Industry observers note that how it works: StepSecurity got its start with its own tool, Harden-Runner, which is free for open-source projects. It watches automated builds on GitHub and flags anything unexpected in the processes they run, the network connections they make or the files they change.

According to recent reports, more than 20,000 open-source projects use it, the company indicates, up from about 3,000 at the time of the seed round. Unusual behavior spotted in those public builds has helped StepSecurity catch attacks early, the company says, including the March 2025 compromise of tj-actions, a widely used add-on for GitHub’s build automation.

StepSecurity’s paid products also protect developers’ laptops and check code repositories. Its Secure Registry service screens software packages before a firm’s builds download them from public sources such as npm, the main public repository for JavaScript packages. It blocks versions known to be compromised and holds brand-latest releases for a waiting period, giving researchers time to catch malicious ones before anyone installs them.

Recent findings suggest that along with the funding, StepSecurity is making Secure Registry free for public GitHub projects that use Harden-Runner and run their builds on GitHub’s servers. The free version defaults to a two-day waiting period and supports JavaScript packages, with Python, Java, Ruby and Rust planned.

StepSecurity has plenty of competition. Socket, a San Francisco startup that screens open-source packages for malicious code, raised $60 million at a $1 billion valuation in May. Sonatype, JFrog and Endor Labs also sell tools that can block risky packages before they’re installed.

In a recent development, growth spurt: StepSecurity states its annual recurring revenue grew fivefold in 2024, fivefold again in 2025 and more than fivefold so far this year. It didn’t disclose dollar figures.

Named customers include Circle, Dexcom, Kong, Mercari, Chainguard and XBOW.

The tech giant has 27 employees, up from four, including the founders, at the time of the seed round. Sharma is based in Sammamish and Kurmi in Kirkland, and the rest of the remote-first team is spread across the U.S., Canada and India.

What’s next: StepSecurity prepares to extend its protections to agent sandboxes, the isolated environments where AI agents run code. Its argument is that anyone who asks an AI agent for a spreadsheet may be downloading and running open-source packages.

The firm indicates it also plans to double its team over the next 12 months, mostly in security research, engineering and sales and marketing.

3 ways Disney+ now sells Avengers: Doomsday tickets inside the app

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, disney+ offers a Tickets tab, post-trailer prompts and pause screens for Avengers: Doomsday seats.
  • Sources indicate that streaming services have started selling the moments when people stop watching.
  • Disney is making this pitch for its next superhero film on a deadline.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, disney+ offers a Tickets tab, post-trailer prompts and pause screens for Avengers: Doomsday seats. See how each of the 3 routes works.

Sources indicate that streaming services have started selling the moments when people stop watching. A pause, the last seconds of a trailer or the gap between episodes once held nothing but a viewer waiting for the next thing, and now those moments hold offers. TheDesk.net reports that Disney $DIS, Netflix $NFLX, Amazon $AMZN and Warner Bros Discovery $WBD are all putting more into ad-supported streaming. With that much money behind ads, the companies are rebuilding the viewing screen so it can show sales messages. Disney owns both Marvel and Disney+, according to ABC News. As Disney pushes further into ads, its own film studio can become a customer of its own streaming service, and the advertiser and the outlet can be the same organization. For the viewer, the line between watching a show and being sold something gets thinner.

Disney is making this pitch for its next superhero film on a deadline. Avengers: Doomsday opens in theaters on Friday, Dec. 18, according to ABC News. Disney+ puts its ticket offers in front of fans before that date, while they are still deciding whether to go and when to buy seats. Disney did not build the tools behind these offers for a single movie. "Each release informed the next, enabling teams to achieve parity across platforms and scale rapidly while maintaining high creative and performance standards," Alex Combs, vice president of product management for ad platforms at Disney Entertainment and ESPN, mentioned, as reported by TheDesk.net. That makes the ticket routes part of an ad system Disney designed to reuse, not a one-time Marvel promotion. A fan who enjoys the shortcut is also the target of that system.

Recent findings suggest that what's on Disney+ gathered the Disney+ routes for buying seats to the upcoming Marvel movie, and a fan inside the app has more than one way to reach a ticket. Each route raises the same question for anyone planning to see the film: Is it a shortcut worth taking, or an ad that happens to end in a ticket?

According to recent reports, fans can now start buying seats for Avengers: Doomsday from a Tickets tab inside Disney $DIS+, according to What's on Disney+. A fan no longer has to leave the app and look up a theater chain's website to begin the purchase. Disney also controls the home screen around that tab, so the same organization decides both what a viewer watches and where the ticket offer appears.

According to recent reports, disney is also filling its service with reasons to see the upcoming film. Avengers: Endgame Encore is a new edit of the last Avengers film with four minutes of added footage that points toward Doomsday. It debuted on Disney+ on Nov. 13, 2026, according to ABC News. Fans can watch that footage weeks before the film reaches theaters, while they are still deciding about tickets. Disney also groups earlier Marvel reveals and movies into a collection called "Countdown to Avengers: Doomsday," which presents the older titles as viewing to finish before the new release. By the time a viewer opens the Tickets tab, Disney may already have spent hours of that viewer's watching time pointing them toward it.

Recent findings suggest that for a fan who has already decided to go, starting the purchase inside the app is a real convenience. It is less clear whether the tab persuades anyone else.

The tab is easy to use, but the urge to use it may have come from the same screen.

Disney $DIS+ puts its ticket pitch in front of Avengers fans at the moment a trailer finishes, when most viewers would otherwise move on to the next thing. What's on Disney+ reports that a fan who finishes the last Avengers: Doomsday trailer in the app is prompted with either a phone alert or a scan code for Fandango. Both prompts move the next step off the TV and onto the phone in the viewer's hand, so the fan doesn't have to go looking for showtimes.

Disney+ starts the sale, but it doesn't finish it. The prompt only links out to Fandango, and the purchase itself takes place on Fandango's side. In practice, the post-trailer prompt works much like an ad with a link attached. A fan who follows it ends up making the same Fandango purchase they could have made by opening the site on their own, only sooner.

The shortcut saves the fan a search, not a checkout.

Sources indicate that disney $DIS+ now answers the pause button with a sales pitch for Avengers: Doomsday. Viewers usually pause to grab a snack or answer the door, and it is the one moment when they aren't asking to be shown anything. When a viewer pauses any title, Disney+ shows a Doomsday screen with links to buy tickets, according to What's on Disney+. Someone partway through a show with no connection to the Avengers gets the same ticket pitch as a devoted Marvel fan.

The Doomsday screen is ad space that Disney already sells. TheDesk.net reports that Disney's Pause Ads format runs when a viewer pauses a program. The Marvel ticket offer uses that same trigger, which makes Doomsday one more advertiser in a slot that Disney also offers to outside brands. A viewer who finds the screen handy is still looking at an ad, and the convenience is simply the way Disney delivers it.

Disney has not shown that its pause screens sell movie tickets. The results Disney has shared for upgraded pause formats such as Pause Plus Trivia come from its own beta testing, according to TheDesk.net. Those are the organization's own numbers, and none of them link a pause screen to a ticket purchase. Nobody yet knows whether a screen that demonstrates up during a pause moves anyone from the couch to a theater seat.

For a viewer, the pause screen is an ad first and a shortcut second, and it is worth tapping only for someone who had already decided to go.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Charles Hoskinson’s Cardano-linked privacy blockchain Midnight has inked a big initial deal with a Japanese payments company as it aims to make further inroads into traditional finance.

The news comes soon after a key breakthrough for Midnight in the United Kingdom, where Monument Bank started tokenizing customer deposits on the blockchain.

Recent findings suggest that per a Nov. 19 NADA NEWS report, Midnight Foundation President Fahmi Syed stated the foundation had inked an MOU (memorandum of understanding) with a major Japanese payments manufacturer.

Syed did not name the manufacturer. But the deal is a big one for Midnight’s bid to establish a presence in Japan’s financial services sector.

However, it is just an initial agreement, and no commercial services have been rolled out in Japan yet.

It is also worth noting that the Midnight Foundation is talking to some major Japanese banks and companies working with intellectual property and medical data.

According to Syed, he spent two days in Tokyo meeting with major financial institutions and other companies.

Japan has been a key market for Midnight, along with the United States.

According to Midnight Foundation Japan country manager Taro Kimura, Japan is the only Asian country where the foundation has a local representative on the ground.

Midnight has been eyeing Japan more keenly due to the country’s sizeable Cardano community.

The Japanese push comes hot on the heels of a historic development in the British banking sector.

It has been revealed that on Nov. 18, British financial institution Monument Bank started tokenizing retail customer deposits on Midnight. It is the first UK bank to launch such a product on a public blockchain.

Industry observers note that the first phase of the venture involves up to £250 million in tokenized deposits. For this, the bank is offering customers a 12-month fixed annual interest rate of 5.2%.

Midnight employs zero-knowledge cryptography to safeguard sensitive transaction details, unlike traditional public blockchains. As a result, banks can meet compliance requirements while keeping their customers’ private information and transaction details out of public view.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When Lang Walker, the late Australian billionaire property developer and philanthropist, and his wife, Sue Walker, first saw Yaukuve Levu Island, Kadavu, Fiji, surrounded by the Great Astrolabe Reef, the land was largely overgrown, with the remains of a development that had never been completed.

Industry observers note that “We anchored the boat out the front, looked at it and thought what a wonderful place this could be,” Sue Walker recalls. “It took eight years and an enormous amount of hard work to bring that vision to life.”.

That effort led to Kokomo Private Island, which officially opened in March 2017.

Today, the property features 21 beachfront villas and five hilltop residences, each with a private pool; three principal dining venues, with more than 80% of herbs and greens sourced from the island’s 5.5-acre organic farm; the Yaukuve Spa Sanctuary with its dedicated fitness center; and no shortage of adventure and cultural activities available to its guests.

It has been revealed that my husband and I had a chance to experience the tropical island paradise for ourselves in September. Throughout our stay, we were struck by Kokomo’s sheer natural beauty and how much the luxury hospitality experience was rooted in a genuine sense of place.

Increasingly, hotels and resorts highlighting local character rise to the top of travelers’ wishlists. Nearly three-quarters of luxury travelers won’t pay for accommodations that feel generic, per a report from Preferred Hotels & Resorts, and 77% of travelers prioritize authentic experiences representative of local culture, according to research from Booking.com.

Kokomo serves as a lesson in hospitality excellence — what it takes to succeed in a travel landscape increasingly defined by a desire for authenticity and local character. Here’s how every business can do the same.

After a long day (or more) of travel, first impressions are key. Guests want to feel at ease and an immediate sense of place. But, sometimes, that’s the straightforward part. Sustaining that genuine warm welcome throughout the stay also matters.

Staff members at Kokomo give it its personality and make guests feel at home, often forming relationships that bring people back year after year, Walker says.

Additionally, Kokomo has developed a close relationship with the local community, where some staff members are from: supporting local employment, working with neighboring villages, and contributing to education, healthcare and community initiatives.

Sources indicate that “Authenticity comes from allowing those relationships and traditions to exist naturally, rather than trying to manufacture an experience for guests,” Walker says. “When someone shares a story about their village, introduces a guest to a local custom or folklore or even simply welcomes them with genuine Fijian hospitality, that’s what stays with people.”.

Our arrival and journey to Kokomo was seamless from the first “bula” (Fijian for “hello” and a wish for life and good health). After a 45-minute seaplane ride, we touched down on the crystalline blue waters in front of Kokomo. We were given a salusalu, a traditional garland worn around the neck, and coconut water, and listened to a group of staff members sing traditional Fijian welcome songs.

That warmth and hospitality extended throughout our time at Kokomo, across the interactions we had with staff and when we visited the nearby Dravuni Village, which is home to a small indigenous Fijian community. We heard traditional songs, learned about their hand-woven crafts, participated in a kava ceremony and toured the village with a staff member who’d grown up there.

The business lesson is this: Lean into what makes a destination special, and the cultural touchstones that define it, for an authentic welcome that extends from the first moment to the last.

Industry observers note that of course, as much as people want to soak up all a destination has to offer, they’ll spend a good portion of their vacation in their accommodations. Ideally, those accommodations capture the destination’s unique characteristics while prioritizing comfort.

From the beginning, the Walkers wanted Kokomo to feel like home, “albeit a rather extraordinary one,” where families could create lifelong memories with the privacy, space and luxury afforded by their own quiet corner of the island.

Sources indicate that “For me, true luxury isn’t about formality,” Walker indicates. “It’s about comfort, freedom, being able to enjoy yourself without feeling constrained by the usual expectations of a hotel. Children should be able to run around, explore and have adventures, while their parents and grandparents can relax and enjoy the island in their own way.”.

Our one-bedroom beachfront villa, just steps from the ocean, felt sprung from the tropical landscape itself. The high ceilings, neutral stone and wood, and ample windows, the better to display the expansive patio with its private pool and the dazzling ocean view, created an indoor-outdoor flow with understated natural elegance.

When it comes to architecture, interior design, or landscape, embracing what sets the place surrounding it apart from any other, rather than competing with it, helps establish that seamless, one-of-kind experience guests won’t forget.

Recent findings suggest that whether a guest is a serious gourmet or not, meals will stand out as part of the experience (a three-times-a-day touchpoint). For remote resorts where guests rely solely on the dining on-site, it’s even more critical to deliver elevated, locally-defined experiences.

Early on, the Walkers realized they had access to the best ingredients on their doorstep — fresh seafood and the climate and space to grow much of the island’s own produce — and built their culinary philosophy around that, Walker indicates.

In a recent development, “A fish caught locally that morning, vegetables picked from the garden, herbs cut just before they’re used,” she explains. “You can’t get much fresher than that. Building and operating a resort in such a remote location comes with enormous logistical challenges, so growing more of our own food and reducing our reliance on imported produce makes sense on many levels.”.

We had a chance to go on a tour with Kokomo’s executive chef Marty Kindleysides. He gave us an inside look at the island’s farm and hydroponic gardens, which help shape the menus across its restaurants: the Beach Shack on Kokomo’s western beach; Walker D’Plank, featuring Asian-influenced cuisine, near the arrival jetty; and the poolside Kokocabana, highlighting Italian-inspired dishes.

From the beautiful lunch Kindleysides prepared for us with farm-fresh ingredients like squash and kale, to all of the meals we enjoyed at the other dining venues, including a showstopping dinner by Chef Caroline during a curry-themed night at Walker D’Plank, the food was flavorful, intentional and reinforced a singular dining experience.

Guests should never feel like the food where they’re staying is an afterthought; it’s another opportunity — and a very memorable one — to showcase innovation and what makes a setting unique.

At a remote tropical resort like Kokomo, guests have the luxury of a picture-perfect natural setting offering once-in-a-lifetime activities. But striking the balance between making the most of the environment and protecting it is also critical.

Lang was an avid diver for most of his life and immediately recognized the wonder of the Great Astrolabe Reef. The Walkers saw it as their responsibility to look after it, so they set out to help guests experience and understand it.

“There’s something quite powerful about a child helping to plant coral, or a family learning about the individual manta rays that return to our waterways each season,” Walker claims. “Suddenly conservation becomes personal. You’re no longer looking at a beautiful reef, rather, you’re beginning to understand how it works and why protecting it matters.”.

We had the opportunity to meet with a marine biologist to learn about the manta rays and conservation efforts. Kokomo has partnered with Manta Project Fiji to research and protect Fiji’s reef manta rays since 2017. More than 500 manta ray sightings were recorded during the most recent monitoring period. We even went to look for them by boat, but unfortunately with it being the tail end of the season, didn’t spot any.

Sources indicate that additionally, the marine biologist led us on a guided coral restoration tour, where we snorkeled over some of the current projects underway. More than 2,000 corals have been transplanted as part of Kokomo’s coral restoration. The island also has six active coral nurseries, which can support more than 10,000 corals per season.

Bringing guests into the very projects that protect the place they’re staying gives them destination-driven, extraordinary experiences while safeguarding them for future generations.

Relaxation means different things to different people, but centralizing spa and wellness options in one place, and melding personalized comfort with distinct ambiance, gives everyone the option to design an ideal routine to reset.

The Walkers wanted to build on the feeling guests have upon arrival — everyday life demands removed by the grandeur of nature — and developed the Yaukuve Spa Sanctuary with that in mind.

“The gardens, the tropical landscape, the sense of privacy all contribute to the experience,” Walker indicates. “I wanted guests to feel that they could completely switch off, even if only for an hour or two. I don’t think wellness needs to be complicated or overly prescriptive. Sometimes the greatest luxury is having the time and space to do what makes you feel good, without the schedule or expectation.”.

Recent findings suggest that we enjoyed Kokomo’s signature “Pacific Mastery Massage,” which incorporates centuries-old methods from traditional Fijian Bobo, combining variable pressure and rhythmic movement with the preferred oil blend. Before and after the service, we sipped iced hibiscus tea (the flower is often seen in Fijian landscaping) in the garden setting.

It has been revealed that guests will remember how a vacation makes them feel, so making sure they have the option to truly unwind, whatever that looks like for them, is key. Infusing it with a local twist means they won’t forget exactly where they experienced it.

At the end of the stay, as we departed on the one-hour helicopter ride back to the hangar, spotting our villa on the lush island encircled by a shock of turquoise, we came away already nostalgic for the trip, and with a deeper appreciation for Fiji’s natural beauty and vibrant culture.

We would love to return some day (maybe to snorkel with the mantas) — and that’s exactly what the Walkers intended.

“More than anything, I hope guests leave Kokomo feeling they’ve been part of something special,” Walker indicates. “That they’ve spent quality time with the people they love, experienced the generosity of our Fijian team and discovered a part of the world they’ll always remember. If they leave feeling as though Kokomo is their island home, then we’ve achieved what we set out to do.”.

When Lang Walker, the late Australian billionaire property developer and philanthropist, and his wife, Sue Walker, first saw Yaukuve Levu Island, Kadavu, Fiji, surrounded by the Great Astrolabe Reef, the land was largely overgrown, with the remains of a development that had never been completed.

“We anchored the boat out the front, looked at it and thought what a wonderful place this could be,” Sue Walker recalls. “It took eight years and an enormous amount of hard work to bring that vision to life.”.

That effort led to Kokomo Private Island, which officially opened in March 2017.
